sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: What does blood alcohol concentration measure, and what unlawful limits apply to drivers over twenty-one versus under twenty-one?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.memory_hook: Point zero eight over, zero-two under
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: Blood alcohol concentration measures the alcohol in the bloodstream, and a driver over the age of twenty-one breaks the law by driving at point zero eight percent or higher while a driver under the age of twenty-one breaks it at point zero two percent or higher.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: What substances and vehicles fall under West Virginia's definition of driving under the influence?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: Driving under the influence means being under the influence of alcohol, drugs or controlled substances while driving any motor vehicle.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: What test agreement binds every licensed West Virginia driver when charged with impaired driving, and what happens if you refuse?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.memory_hook: Refusing chemical test suspends one year
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: Under West Virginia's implied consent law every licensed driver agrees to take a chemical test when charged with driving under the influence, and refusing that test suspends the driving privilege for at least one year.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: What happens to your driver's license and renewal rights when West Virginia revokes your driving privilege?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: Revocation means a driver's license and all driving privileges on public highways are terminated and cannot be renewed, though in certain circumstances the DMV may accept and act on an application for a new license.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: How does West Virginia define a suspension of a driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: Suspension means a driver's license and all driving privileges on public highways are withdrawn only temporarily.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: What is the core difference between a license suspension and a license revocation?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: A suspension withdraws the driver's license and driving privileges only temporarily, while a revocation terminates them so that the license cannot be renewed.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: Which age group faces the point zero two percent alcohol limit, and which faces point zero eight percent?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: The lower point zero two percent blood alcohol limit applies to drivers under the age of twenty-one, while the point zero eight percent limit applies to drivers over the age of twenty-one.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: What specific act does implied consent penalize on its own, and for at least how long?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: The implied consent law penalizes refusing the chemical test itself, with a suspension of the driving privilege for at least one year.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: Whom does the West Virginia handbook define as a driver?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: The handbook calls a driver any person who drives, operates or physically controls a motor vehicle in a place open to the public for vehicular traffic, or who is required to hold a driver's license.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: What does a state-issued driver's license authorize, and what conditions shape that permission?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: A driver's license is a permit or license the state issues that authorizes a person to drive a motor vehicle in a specific class or classes, subject to whatever restriction or endorsement it carries.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: Which three roles qualify someone as an operator of a motor vehicle on a highway?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: An operator is a person who drives a motor vehicle, has actual physical control of it, or steers a vehicle that a motor vehicle is towing on a highway.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: Who counts as a commercial driver on West Virginia public streets or highways?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: A commercial driver is anyone who drives a commercial motor vehicle on public streets or highways for any purpose.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: How many phases make up West Virginia's graduated driver's license program, and what age span does it cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.memory_hook: Three phases ages fifteen to eighteen
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: The graduated driver's license is a three-phase licensing program for ages fifteen to eighteen that lets young drivers build skill and confidence through safe, measured steps, and each phase has its own requirements and restrictions.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: Besides the motorist powering the front vehicle, who else counts as an operator during a highway tow?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: An operator includes a person steering a vehicle that a motor vehicle is towing on a highway, not only the person driving the towing vehicle under power.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: How much space does the legal term highway cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: A highway is the entire width between the boundary lines of any way that is maintained and open to the public for vehicular travel.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.front: Which portion of a highway counts as the roadway, and what is left out?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.expected_back: The roadway is the part of a highway that is improved, designed or ordinarily used for vehicle travel, not counting the berm or shoulder.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: What three features can separate opposing roadways on a divided highway?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: A divided highway carries opposing traffic on separate roadways split by an unpaved strip of land, a raised median or another physical barrier.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: How does an interchange move traffic between two or more roadways?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: An interchange is a system of connecting roadways with one or more grade separations that moves traffic between two or more roadways on different levels.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: What shared highway area forms an intersection, even when one road ends without crossing through?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: An intersection is the area two or more highways share where they meet at or close to right angles, even if one highway does not cross the other.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: What does an acceleration lane let an entering driver do beside a high-speed highway?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: An acceleration lane is an extra lane beside a high-speed highway that lets an entering driver build up speed before merging into the through lanes.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: Why is a deceleration lane placed beside regular highway travel lanes?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: A deceleration lane sits beside the regular lanes so that vehicles leaving the highway can slow down without blocking through traffic.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: What movement does the term merging traffic describe?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: Merging traffic means vehicles entering moving traffic lanes from the adjacent lanes on the left or right.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: How does the handbook define right-of-way?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: Right-of-way is the privilege of using the highway immediately.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: How do acceleration lanes and deceleration lanes split entering and leaving highway duties?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: An acceleration lane serves drivers entering a high-speed highway, whereas a deceleration lane serves drivers leaving it.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: Does the berm or shoulder belong to the roadway, the highway, or both?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: The roadway is only the portion of the highway used for vehicle travel, so the berm or shoulder belongs to the highway but not to the roadway.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: How does an interchange differ structurally from an intersection?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: An interchange links roadways on different levels through grade separations, whereas an intersection is simply the area where two or more highways meet at or near right angles.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: Which weight rating, passenger capacity, or cargo requirement makes a vehicle a commercial motor vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: A commercial motor vehicle has a gross vehicle weight rating of twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, is built to carry sixteen or more passengers counting the driver, or hauls hazardous materials in any weight class that requires placards.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: What passenger capacity and transport purpose define a bus in West Virginia?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: A bus is a motor vehicle built to carry more than seven passengers and used mainly to transport people for compensation.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.front: Who can own a school bus, and what transport job defines it?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.expected_back: A school bus is a motor vehicle, owned by a public agency or privately owned and operated, that carries children to or from school.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: What wheel count, pedal feature, horsepower, engine size, and top-speed limits define a moped?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: A moped is a two- or three-wheeled cycle with foot pedals and an independent power source of at most two horsepower, an engine no larger than fifty cubic centimeters and a top speed of thirty miles per hour.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: How does West Virginia define a motorcycle by seating, vehicle exclusion, and wheel count?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: A motorcycle is a motor vehicle other than a tractor that has a seat for the rider and is designed to travel on no more than three wheels touching the ground.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: What maximum engine size defines a motor-driven cycle, and how are scooters and mopeds treated?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.memory_hook: Up to two-fifty cc, no mopeds
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: A motor-driven cycle is a motorcycle, including any motor scooter, whose motor does not exceed two hundred fifty cubic centimeters, and mopeds are excluded from the term.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: What two traits define a motor vehicle in the handbook?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: A motor vehicle is any self-propelled vehicle that does not run on rails.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: What makes a four-wheeled vehicle a true low-speed vehicle, and do modified golf carts or all-terrain vehicles qualify?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: A low-speed vehicle is a four-wheeled motor vehicle built and designated as a low-speed vehicle on its manufacturer's certificate of origin, and modified golf carts and ATVs do not qualify.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: On which roads and maximum speed zones may a low-speed vehicle operate?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: Low-speed vehicles may run only on private roads or on public roads and streets inside a municipality where the speed limit is twenty-five miles per hour or less.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: How old must a West Virginia antique vehicle be, and how may its owner use it?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: West Virginia treats a motor vehicle as an antique when it is more than twenty-five years old and is owned only as a collector's item for club events, tours, parades and similar outings rather than for everyday transportation.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: What work is a farm tractor designed and mainly used to perform?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: A farm tractor is a motor vehicle designed and used mainly in agriculture to pull plows, mowing machines and other implements of husbandry.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: How does the handbook define an implement of husbandry?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: An implement of husbandry is a vehicle designed or adapted for agricultural purposes and used by its owner mainly in agricultural operations.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: How do the engine ceilings of a moped and a motor-driven cycle compare?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: A moped is limited to two horsepower and fifty cubic centimeters, while a motor-driven cycle may carry a motor of up to two hundred fifty cubic centimeters and expressly excludes mopeds.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: Why doesn't counting two or three wheels tell you whether a machine is a motorcycle or a moped?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: A motorcycle may travel on up to three wheels and a moped likewise has two or three wheels, so wheel count alone does not separate the two categories.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: What separates West Virginia's school bus definition from its general bus definition?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: A school bus is defined by its purpose of carrying children to or from school and may be publicly or privately owned, which sets it apart from the general bus definition built on passenger count and compensation.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: How do the passenger thresholds differ between a commercial motor vehicle and a general bus?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: A vehicle built for sixteen or more passengers counting the driver is a commercial motor vehicle, while the bus definition starts at more than seven passengers carried for compensation.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: Why do modified golf carts and all-terrain vehicles fail West Virginia's low-speed vehicle definition?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: A modified golf cart or an ATV is not a low-speed vehicle, because the term covers only a four-wheeled vehicle designated as such on its manufacturer's certificate of origin.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.front: What separates a farm tractor from an implement of husbandry?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.expected_back: A farm tractor is the motor vehicle that pulls plows and mowing machines, while an implement of husbandry is the agricultural vehicle or equipment itself that is designed or adapted for farm use.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: What are blind spots around your vehicle, and how must you check them?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: Blind spots are the zones on both sides of a vehicle that the driver cannot see without turning the head.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: How does the handbook define following distance?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: Following distance is the space cushion kept between your vehicle and the one directly ahead of you.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: Which four responder fleets does the handbook specifically name as authorized emergency vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: Authorized emergency vehicles include fire, police, chartered rescue squad and ambulance vehicles together with other emergency vehicles.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: Who counts as a pedestrian under the handbook's definitions?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: A pedestrian is any person traveling on foot.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: What two categories make up a wireless communications device?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: A wireless communications device is a handheld device used to reach a wireless telephone service, or a text messaging device.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: What must every non-exempt West Virginia resident hold and carry when driving on public roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: Anyone who lives in West Virginia and wants to drive a motor vehicle on public roads must hold a West Virginia driver's license unless expressly exempt, and must carry that license while driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: When is someone in the United States armed services exempt from needing a West Virginia driver's license?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: A person operating a motor vehicle in the armed services of the United States while performing official duties is exempt from the West Virginia license requirement.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: Which nonresident visitors may drive without a West Virginia license, and for how many days per calendar year?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: A nonresident who is at least sixteen years old and holds a valid license from another state or country is exempt from needing a West Virginia license, but only for ninety days in a calendar year.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: When is an out-of-state college or university student exempt from getting a West Virginia license?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: A nonresident attending a West Virginia college or university who holds a valid license from another state is exempt from the West Virginia license requirement.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: How can habitual alcohol use or narcotic drug addiction affect license eligibility?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: A habitual user of alcoholic beverages or a person addicted to narcotic drugs can be denied a driver's license.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: Can someone suspended or revoked in another state or foreign jurisdiction get a West Virginia license right away?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: A person whose driver's license has been suspended or revoked by West Virginia, another state or a foreign jurisdiction can be denied a license until that suspension or revocation period expires.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: When may the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles deny an applicant on public-safety grounds?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: A license can be denied to anyone the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles has good cause to believe would endanger public safety or welfare when operating a motor vehicle.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: What educational failure allows West Virginia to deny a driver's license to an applicant under eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.memory_hook: Under eighteen neither enrolled nor graduated
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: A person under the age of eighteen who is neither enrolled in nor graduated from an approved educational institution can be denied a driver's license.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: Does the ninety-day calendar-year limit apply to general nonresident drivers or to nonresident college students?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: The ninety-day calendar-year limit attaches to the general exemption for nonresident drivers at least sixteen years old with a valid out-of-state license, not to the separate exemption for nonresident college students.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: Which four proof categories must every first-time applicant bring, and what happens to your original papers?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: Every first-time license applicant must bring documents proving identity, Social Security number, any legal name change that has ever occurred, and West Virginia residency, and the DMV scans the documents securely and returns them.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: How many identity proofs and residency proofs must new, transfer, and expired-license applicants bring alongside Social Security and name-change records?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: New, transfer and expired-license applicants must provide one proof of identity, their Social Security number, two proofs of West Virginia residency showing name and physical address, and proof of legal name change if the name differs from the identity document.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: Which three groups does the handbook treat as first-time applicants?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: The handbook treats as a first-time applicant anyone who has never held a driver's license or ID card, who is transferring an out-of-state license, or whose West Virginia license has been expired for more than three years.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: Why must your full legal name match Social Security Administration files when presenting your one identity proof?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.memory_hook: State verifies every Social Security record
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: You must present exactly one proof of identity and must provide your Social Security number, and your full legal name must match the name on file with the Social Security Administration because the DMV checks every number with that agency.

sec02-card-sec02-F40.front: Along with one identity proof, two residency proofs, Social Security number, and the application form, which certified records link a changed name?
sec02-card-sec02-F40.memory_hook: Certified marriage divorce or court order
sec02-card-sec02-F40.expected_back: A first-time applicant for an instruction permit, driver's license or identification card must provide a Social Security number, one proof of identity, two proofs of West Virginia residency and the application form the DMV provides, plus name-change documents such as a certified marriage certificate, divorce decree or court order when the name has changed.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: What two card options does West Virginia issue, and what determines which documents you bring?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: West Virginia offers two kinds of driver's license and ID card, a Not For Federal Use card and a REAL ID or For Federal Use card with a gold star, and the documents you must bring depend on which type you choose.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: When does an expired West Virginia license or an expired out-of-state license trigger full retesting?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.memory_hook: Three years in-state, any expired transfer
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: A West Virginia license expired three years or more sends the holder through the full examination process as a first-time applicant, and an expired out-of-state license also requires retesting.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: Which United States birth certificates prove identity, and which two records are rejected?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: An original or certified copy of a United States birth certificate proves identity, including State Department and military birth certificates, but hospital birth certificates and Bureau of Census records are not acceptable.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: Which United States passport credentials count as acceptable proof of identity?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: A valid United States passport or passport card is an acceptable proof of identity.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: Which valid, unexpired federal documents let a foreign-born applicant prove identity?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: A foreign-born applicant may prove identity with a valid, unexpired Department of Homeland Security document such as a Permanent Resident Card, an employment authorization document, a certificate of naturalization or citizenship, a consular report of birth abroad, or a foreign passport carrying a valid United States visa with the approved arrival record of the most recent admittance.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: What happens if your name or birth date conflicts with Social Security Administration records?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.memory_hook: Fix mismatch before any card issues
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: If your name or date of birth does not match Social Security Administration records, the problem must be corrected before an instruction permit, license or identification card can be issued.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: What must an applicant submit if legally ineligible for a Social Security number?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: An applicant who is not eligible for a Social Security number must submit a letter from the Social Security Administration stating that ineligibility.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: Which original tax or payroll records prove your Social Security number besides the card itself, and what copy is rejected?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: Acceptable proof of Social Security number is the original card in your current legal name, an original Wage and Tax Statement or a payroll stub showing the employer's name and identification number along with your name, address and number, or a ten ninety-nine form showing your full number and name, and a photocopy of the Wage and Tax Statement is not acceptable.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: When must you bring legal name-change proof, and why does the state require it?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.memory_hook: Link every legal name ever used
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: Proof of legal name change is required if your name has ever changed, because the DMV must be able to link every legal name you have used.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: Which official records prove a legal name change, and which ceremonial wedding papers are rejected?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: Acceptable proof of a legal name change is a marriage certificate for each marriage if married more than once, an amended birth certificate, a court order or a divorce decree showing the legal name, while souvenir marriage documents and minister's copies are not acceptable.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: How do State Department and military birth certificates compare with hospital certificates and census records?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: State Department and military birth certificates count as proof of identity, while hospital birth certificates and Bureau of Census records do not.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: How can an original Wage and Tax Statement cover two requirements, and what age cap or copy rule applies?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.memory_hook: Original under eighteen months counts twice
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: An original Wage and Tax Statement proves the Social Security number and may also serve as one residency proof if it is not more than eighteen months old, but a photocopy of it is not acceptable.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: What four rules govern your two West Virginia residency proofs regarding boxes, bill age, and married spouses?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.memory_hook: Two physical, ninety days, spouse allowed
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: Two proofs of West Virginia residency are required, documents showing a post office box are not acceptable, any recurring document such as a utility bill cannot be more than ninety days old, and a married applicant may use documents in the spouse's name together with a marriage certificate.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: Which household bills, registrations, financial papers, and employer stubs count toward West Virginia residency, and what utility or paystub traps fail?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: Residency proofs include a West Virginia utility bill that is not a termination notice, tax records with a West Virginia street address, mortgage or homeowner insurance documents, a voter registration card, a vehicle registration card, a bank statement, a rental or lease agreement, an auto insurance card, a hunting license and a paycheck stub from a West Virginia employer showing a current physical address that is not handwritten.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: Which school, emergency-address, postal, benefit, tax, or residential-facility letters also prove West Virginia residency?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: Further residency proofs include a college admissions letter showing in-state residency, a nine one one address letter, a Social Security benefits letter, a Post Office letter assigning a new physical West Virginia address, a Wage and Tax Statement not more than eighteen months old, and a letter from a shelter, hotel, nursing home or similar facility giving its physical address and stating that the applicant lives there.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: Why does West Virginia refuse to issue any license or identification card without an in-state physical address?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: An applicant for any driver's license or identification card must be a West Virginia resident, and the DMV will not license or issue a card to anyone who does not give a West Virginia physical address.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.front: May a former West Virginia resident who now lives in another state renew a West Virginia card?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.expected_back: A former West Virginia resident who now lives elsewhere may not renew a West Virginia license or identification card until residency in the state is established again.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.front: Once your two residency documents are scanned on file, when must you bring two residency proofs again?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.expected_back: Once a new resident's two residency documents have been scanned into the record, later renewals or transactions require two residency documents again only if the physical address has changed.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: How does the freshness deadline on recurring bills compare with a Wage and Tax Statement used for residency?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: A recurring residency document such as a utility bill may be no more than ninety days old, whereas a Wage and Tax Statement used as residency proof may be up to eighteen months old.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: Why does one Post Office address fail residency while another Post Office letter passes?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: A document showing a post office box is rejected as residency proof, while a letter from the Post Office assigning the applicant a new physical West Virginia address is accepted.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: Besides first-time proofs, what credential or record must an out-of-state transfer applicant hand over, and how fresh must a record be?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: An applicant transferring a license from another state must also hand in the current out-of-state license or present a certified driving record from that state dated thirty days or less before the application.

sec02-card-sec02-F41.front: Which steps and screenings let a new resident transfer a valid, unexpired out-of-state license without road testing?
sec02-card-sec02-F41.expected_back: A new resident with a valid, unexpired out-of-state license may transfer it after passing a vision screening, completing a brief alcohol awareness course and surrendering the out-of-state license, and must present every document required of a first-time applicant.

sec02-card-sec02-F42.front: Within how many days of establishing residency must a newcomer apply to drive, and how does a motorcycle endorsement transfer?
sec02-card-sec02-F42.memory_hook: Apply within thirty days, fee transfers
sec02-card-sec02-F42.expected_back: New residents who want to drive in West Virginia must apply for a West Virginia license within thirty days of establishing residency, and a motorcycle endorsement on the old license transfers for an additional fee.

sec02-card-sec02-F43.front: What happens if a newcomer's out-of-state license is expired over three years or cannot be physically produced?
sec02-card-sec02-F43.memory_hook: Over three retests, missing needs record
sec02-card-sec02-F43.expected_back: If the out-of-state license has been expired for more than three years, the new resident must take every examination required of a first-time applicant, and a new resident who cannot produce the out-of-state license must obtain a certified driving record from the former state to waive testing.

sec02-card-sec02-F44.front: What blocks a newcomer whose out-of-state license is suspended or revoked, and may they drive in West Virginia meanwhile?
sec02-card-sec02-F44.expected_back: A new resident whose out-of-state license is suspended or revoked will not be licensed in West Virginia until the Problem Driver Point System issues a clearance, and driving in the state on a license suspended or revoked anywhere is illegal.

sec02-card-sec02-F47.front: What happens when renewing any West Virginia license, including commercial, expired three years or more?
sec02-card-sec02-F47.expected_back: Anyone renewing a West Virginia license, including a commercial driver's license, that has been expired for three years or more must retest through the full examination process with all first-time documents, and an expired out-of-state license also requires retesting.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: In what year did West Virginia adopt the two-thousand-five federal licensing standards, and what is that program's goal?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: In twenty eleven West Virginia adopted the federal licensing standards of the REAL ID Act of two thousand five, a secure license and identification card program meant to improve the integrity and security of all driver's licenses and ID cards nationwide.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: How does the thirty-day deadline for new state residents compare with the deadline for reporting an in-state move?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.memory_hook: Thirty days new resident, twenty move
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: New residents have thirty days after establishing residency to apply for a West Virginia license, while an in-state address change must be reported to the DMV in writing within twenty days.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.front: When does transferring from another state waive exams, and when must the newcomer take every first-time test?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.expected_back: A transfer applicant who presents a valid out-of-state license, or a certified driving record when that license cannot be produced, waives the testing requirement, but an out-of-state license expired more than three years brings every first-time examination.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.front: Which national registry screens every West Virginia license applicant and renewing driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.expected_back: Every license applicant and every renewing driver is reviewed through the Problem Driver Point System, a national driver registry that tracks violations and suspensions from state to state.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.front: What must you do about pending citations or suspensions in another jurisdiction before getting or renewing a West Virginia license?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.expected_back: The DMV is prohibited from licensing a driver whose record shows an unsettled problem in another state or jurisdiction, so pending citations and suspensions elsewhere must be satisfied before applying for or renewing a West Virginia license.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.front: How does West Virginia notify and penalize you when another state reports an unpaid citation, and how do you reinstate?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.expected_back: When another state reports an unpaid citation, the West Virginia DMV notifies the driver by certified mail at the address in its system, allows a certain amount of time to resolve it, and then suspends the license, and the driver must supply proof of payment or of satisfying the court order before reinstatement.

sec02-card-sec02-F39.front: After paying off an overdue citation, should you expect the court to notify motor vehicle records automatically?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.expected_back: Unpaid citations remain the driver's own responsibility, and the court should not be expected to notify the DMV when an unpaid citation is resolved.

sec02-card-sec02-F45.front: How quickly must you report an address change in writing, what penalties apply, and does a Post Office forward work?
sec02-card-sec02-F45.expected_back: A driver who changes address must notify the DMV in writing within twenty days, failure to do so can bring a fine or imprisonment, and telling only the Post Office does not update the DMV record or forward DMV mail.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: What notice precedes suspension for an unpaid out-of-state ticket, and whose proof restores the license?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.memory_hook: Certified mail first, driver's proof restores
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: A suspension for an unpaid out-of-state citation follows certified-mail notice and a period to respond, and reinstatement requires the driver's own proof of payment because the court will not notify the DMV.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: What does a gold star printed on a West Virginia license or identification card signify?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.memory_hook: Approved for airports and federal sites
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: A license or ID card certified as REAL ID compliant carries a gold star on its face showing that it meets full federal requirements for use at airports and other designated federal facilities across the country.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: How long does a permanent license take to arrive by mail, and what lets you drive meanwhile?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.memory_hook: Mailed fifteen-to-twenty business days, temporary covers
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: A license applied for at any DMV location arrives at the applicant's address by mail in approximately fifteen to twenty business days, and a temporary license issued when the application is accepted covers the production and shipping time.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: What documents renew a Not For Federal Use card when nothing changed versus when your address or name changed?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.memory_hook: Card and form unless details changed
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: A renewal applicant for a Not For Federal Use card with no changes brings only the current license or ID card and the renewal application, while an address change requires two proofs of West Virginia residency and a legal name change requires proof of that change.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: Where can you request a duplicate for a lost, stolen, or destroyed license, and when are extra proofs needed?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.memory_hook: Online or regional, proofs if changed
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: If a driver's license is lost, stolen or destroyed, a duplicate can be requested online or at a Regional Office, with proof of any legal name change and two residency proofs if the address changed since the last card.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: What documents must an applicant provide for a For Federal Use renewal or duplicate?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: A For Federal Use renewal or duplicate applicant must provide one proof of identity, a Social Security number, two proofs of West Virginia residency with name and physical address, and proof of legal name change if the name has ever changed.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: How much extra does a For Federal Use card cost, and how is it delivered?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.memory_hook: Extra ten dollars, mailed fifteen-to-twenty days
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: The For Federal Use card costs an additional ten dollars and is mailed to the applicant in fifteen to twenty business days, with a temporary license issued when the application is accepted.

sec02-card-sec02-F46.front: Besides address or name-change proofs, what database or non-citizen requirements apply when getting a duplicate license?
sec02-card-sec02-F46.memory_hook: Fix missing number, verify non-citizen status
sec02-card-sec02-F46.expected_back: To obtain a duplicate license you present two residency documents if your address changed and evidence of any name change, you must supply your Social Security number if it is missing or wrong in the DMV database, and a non-citizen must present the documents that verify legal status, identity and residency.

sec02-card-sec02-F48.front: How do card orientation and color coding distinguish ages fifteen to seventeen, eighteen to twenty, and twenty-one-plus?
sec02-card-sec02-F48.memory_hook: Vertical red, vertical blue, horizontal adult
sec02-card-sec02-F48.expected_back: Applicants aged fifteen to seventeen receive a vertical license or instruction permit color-coded red, applicants aged eighteen to twenty receive a vertical card color-coded blue, and applicants twenty-one or older receive a horizontal license with a landscape background.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: How do document requirements differ between a For Federal Use renewal and an unchanged Not For Federal Use renewal?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.memory_hook: Full packet federal, current card standard
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: A For Federal Use renewal needs the full document set of identity proof, Social Security number, two residency proofs and any name-change proof, whereas a Not For Federal Use renewal with no changes needs only the current card and the renewal application.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: Which two age brackets receive vertical cards in red or blue, and when does the card turn horizontal?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.memory_hook: Red teens, blue eighteen-twenty, horizontal twenty-one
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: Red color coding marks license holders aged fifteen to seventeen and blue marks those aged eighteen to twenty, both on vertical cards, while a horizontal landscape card marks age twenty-one or older.

sec02-card-sec02-F49.front: Along with a Social Security number and two residency proofs, which status credentials qualify an immigrant applicant?
sec02-card-sec02-F49.memory_hook: Green card, resident stamp, or re-entry
sec02-card-sec02-F49.expected_back: An immigrant applying for a permit, license or identification card provides a Social Security number, two proofs of West Virginia residency, and one of a Permanent Resident Card, a valid temporary resident stamp in a foreign passport with English translation or on the arrival record, or a valid re-entry permit.

sec02-card-sec02-F50.front: What passport, arrival, status, and school or work verification must a non-immigrant applicant bring alongside residency and Social Security items?
sec02-card-sec02-F50.memory_hook: Passport arrival status plus school-work letter
sec02-card-sec02-F50.expected_back: A non-immigrant applicant provides a Social Security number or a Social Security Administration denial letter, two residency proofs, a valid foreign passport, the federal arrival record, a visa when the applicant's nation requires one, original documents verifying status and authorized stay, and written school verification for student statuses or employer verification for work statuses.

sec02-card-sec02-F51.front: Which arrival, assurance, and sponsor documents must a refugee with an approved sponsoring organization present?
sec02-card-sec02-F51.expected_back: A refugee applicant provides a Social Security number or denial letter, two residency proofs, an arrival record showing the grant of refugee status, a Reception and Placement Program Assurance form, and written verification of identity and residency from an employee of a State Department approved sponsoring organization.

sec02-card-sec02-F52.front: What documents qualify an unsponsored refugee or asylum seeker alongside two residency proofs and Social Security or denial letter?
sec02-card-sec02-F52.memory_hook: Stamped arrival record plus work authorization
sec02-card-sec02-F52.expected_back: A refugee without an approved sponsoring organization, or a person seeking asylum, provides two residency proofs, a Social Security number or denial letter, an arrival record stamped as refugee or asylee, and employment authorization documents.

sec02-card-sec02-R12.front: Which non-citizen applicant groups may substitute a Social Security denial letter, and which list requires the number itself?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.expected_back: Non-immigrant and refugee applicants may substitute a Social Security Administration denial letter for a Social Security number, while the immigrant document list on the same page names only the Social Security number.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: What minimum age, written consent, and front-seat supervision rules govern a Level One graduated instruction permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: A Level One graduated instruction permit requires being at least fifteen years old and having written consent from a parent or legal guardian on the DMV application form, and the holder may drive only with a licensed driver at least twenty-one years old in the right front passenger seat.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: Which tests qualify a fifteen-year-old for a Level One permit, and what replaces parental consent for a married minor under eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: Obtaining a Level One graduated instruction permit requires being at least fifteen, passing a vision screening and a knowledge test, and presenting parental consent on the DMV form, although a married applicant under eighteen may present a certified marriage certificate instead of parental consent.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: Which two official credentials must you present every single time you apply and test for a Level One permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: Each time you apply and test for a Level One permit you must show a certified birth certificate issued by a United States state or governmental agency responsible for vital records, together with a Social Security number issued by the Social Security Administration.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: Between which daily hours may a Level One permit holder operate a vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: A Level One permit holder may drive only between five in the morning and ten at night.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: Besides the supervising licensed adult, how many non-family passengers may ride with a Level One permit holder?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: A Level One permit holder may carry only two additional non-family passengers besides the supervising licensed adult driver.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: What happens to a Level One instruction permit if the holder racks up two convictions?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Two convictions at Level One result in revocation of the instruction permit for ninety days.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: What blood alcohol standard and occupant restraint duty bind a Level One permit holder?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: Under the zero tolerance rule a Level One permit holder may not have any measurable amount of alcohol in the system while operating a motor vehicle, and must require every occupant to obey the safety belt law.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: How much does each knowledge test attempt cost, and what is the printed fee here for the Level One permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: The knowledge test fee is seven dollars and fifty cents for each attempt, and the Level One graduated permit itself also costs seven dollars and fifty cents.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: Under what single emergency circumstance may a Level One permit holder use a wireless communication device while driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: A Level One permit holder may not use a wireless communication device while operating a motor vehicle unless the device is being used to contact a nine one one system.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: Can a Level One permit be renewed, and what three things happen if you surrender it for any reason?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: A Level One permit is nonrenewable, and anyone who surrenders it for any reason must complete the examination process again, hold the permit for one hundred eighty consecutive conviction-free days, and resubmit proof of identity, Social Security number and West Virginia residency.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: When does a Level One permit expire, and why does a thirty-day grace period follow?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: A Level One permit is issued up to the applicant's eighteenth birthday and expires on that birthday, with a thirty-day grace period beyond it to allow time to complete the road skills examination.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: How do late-night driving rules between ten at night and five in the morning change from Level One to Level Two?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: Level One holders may drive only between five in the morning and ten at night, while Level Two holders may drive at any hour but need a supervising adult between ten at night and five in the morning.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: How does reaching your eighteenth birthday on a Level One permit compare with surrendering it early?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: A Level One permit expires on the eighteenth birthday with a thirty-day grace period for the road skills exam, and surrendering it means repeating the examination and another one hundred eighty conviction-free days.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: How does the Level Two limit on non-family passengers under twenty change after the first six months?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: At Level Two the passenger limit is no non-family passenger under twenty during the first six months and no more than one during the second six months.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: How does the thirty-day birthday grace period for updating card color at eighteen or twenty-one differ from the Level One grace period?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.memory_hook: Card color swap versus road exam
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: A license that expires on the eighteenth or twenty-first birthday carries a thirty-day grace period meant for obtaining the correctly colored license, a different purpose from the Level One grace period for the road skills exam.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: What age span, clean-driving streak, and exam unlock a Level Two intermediate license?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.memory_hook: Sixteen-to-eighteen, one-eighty clean days, road test
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: A Level Two intermediate license requires being between sixteen and eighteen, completing every Level One requirement, having at least one hundred eighty consecutive conviction-free days at Level One immediately before the application, and passing the road skills test.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: What practice-hour log or school course qualifies a Level Two applicant, and what phone rule still applies?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.memory_hook: Fifty hours ten night, or driver-ed
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: A Level Two applicant must also present a parent or guardian log certifying at least fifty hours behind the wheel including at least ten hours at night, or complete a driver education course approved by the West Virginia Department of Education, bring identity and residency documents, and not use a wireless device while driving except to contact nine one one.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: During which hours may a Level Two driver go solo, and when must a licensed adult twenty-one or older ride along?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: A Level Two holder may drive without a supervising adult between five in the morning and ten at night, but must have a supervising licensed adult twenty-one or older in the vehicle between ten at night and five in the morning.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: Which four trips let a Level Two driver operate past ten at night without a supervising adult?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.memory_hook: Work school religion or life-saving emergency
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: The Level Two night-driving rule does not apply when the licensee is participating in, going to or returning from lawful employment, a school-sanctioned activity, a religious activity, or an emergency that requires preventing bodily injury or the death of another person.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: Which non-family passengers are restricted during the first and second six-month halves at Level Two?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: During the first six months at Level Two the holder may not carry any non-family passenger under the age of twenty, and during the second six months may carry no more than one such passenger.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: Which two safety mandates carry straight over from Level One into Level Two?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: Like Level One permit holders, Level Two license holders may not drive with any measurable alcohol in their system and must require every occupant to follow the seat belt law.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: What happens if a driver under eighteen surrenders a Level Two intermediate license for any reason?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: A Level Two holder under eighteen who surrenders the intermediate license for any reason must start over with a Level One instruction permit.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: Which four items must you present each time you apply and test for a Level Two license?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: Each time you apply and test for the Level Two license you must show a certified birth certificate from a United States vital-records agency, provide a Social Security number, the fifty-hour driving log and all documentation required for licensing.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: How many conviction-free months are needed to move from Level One to Level Two, and what does a conviction do?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: To graduate from Level One to Level Two you must be conviction-free for six months, and each conviction restarts the six-month window from the date of that conviction.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: After two convictions revoke a Level One permit for ninety days, how do you get back on the road?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: Two convictions at Level One revoke the graduated permit for ninety days, after which you must re-apply and retest for the Level One permit.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: How long must a Level Two holder drive conviction-free to reach Level Three, and what happens after a conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: To graduate from Level Two to Level Three you must be conviction-free for twelve months, and a conviction restarts the twelve-month period from that point.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: What consequences hit after a first conviction versus a second moving-violation conviction at Level Two?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: A Level Two holder must enroll in a driver improvement program after the first conviction, failing to enroll keeps the driver at Level Two until age eighteen, and a second moving-violation conviction revokes the driving privilege until eighteen with retesting as a first-time applicant.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.front: How does a non-emergency wireless-device citation under age eighteen affect graduation clocks at Level One or Level Two?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.expected_back: Drivers under eighteen may not use a wireless communication device while driving except to contact a nine one one system, and a citation for such use at Level One or Level Two restarts the conviction-free period, six months at Level One and twelve months at Level Two.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.front: Must a seventeen-year-old who qualifies for Level Three upgrade right away?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.expected_back: Once eligible for a Level Three license the driver may choose to apply for it or to keep the Level Two license and its restrictions until age eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.front: What age and clean-driving record unlock Level Three, and where must you apply?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.expected_back: Level Three eligibility requires twelve months of conviction-free driving at Level Two, being at least seventeen, and completing all requirements, and the application is made in person at a DMV Regional Office or Testing Center.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: How do the required conviction-free windows compare between Level One and Level Two?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: The conviction-free window is six months at Level One but twelve months at Level Two, and in both cases a new conviction restarts the clock.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: How does the revocation penalty for two convictions at Level One compare with a second moving violation at Level Two?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: Two convictions at Level One bring a ninety-day revocation followed by retesting, whereas a second moving-violation conviction at Level Two revokes driving until eighteen with retesting as a first-time applicant.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: Once a seventeen-year-old finishes twelve conviction-free months at Level Two, what two choices exist?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: Level Three requires age seventeen and twelve conviction-free months at Level Two, yet a qualified driver may choose to stay at Level Two with its restrictions until eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: Which electronic items are barred from the testing room, and who is allowed inside?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: No cell phones, smart glasses, Bluetooth devices or other electronic devices are permitted in the exam room, and only the applicant taking the test may be in the room.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: Who conducts official vision and knowledge exams, and what happens once you pass?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: Driver examiners give the vision and knowledge tests at DMV-designated locations, and once you pass the required tests the examiner approves your application for processing.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: What minimum visual acuity in at least one eye qualifies an applicant for a West Virginia license?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: To qualify for a West Virginia driver's license you must have at least twenty-forty vision in one eye.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: Does passing the online written knowledge test give you immediate permission to drive?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: Applicants may take the written knowledge test online as part of the license application process, but the certificate from that test is not permission to drive and the applicant must still go to a DMV location for processing.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: What permit does an applicant eighteen or older earn after passing vision and knowledge exams, and who must ride up front?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: An applicant eighteen or older who completes the application, presents the required documents and passes the vision and knowledge tests receives a regular Class E instruction permit, which allows driving only while a licensed driver twenty-one or older occupies the front seat.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: How long does a regular instruction permit stay valid, and what happens if it expires?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: A regular instruction permit is valid for six months, and if it expires the holder must retake both the vision and knowledge tests to obtain another permit.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: How long must an adult permit holder never licensed at Level Two hold the instruction permit before road testing?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: A permit holder who has never been licensed at Level Two or a comparable graduated level must hold the instruction permit for at least thirty days before becoming eligible for the road skills test.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: For a regular adult instruction permit, how does total validity compare with the minimum wait before road testing?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.memory_hook: Valid six months, wait thirty days
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: A regular instruction permit stays valid for six months, but a holder never licensed at Level Two must keep it at least thirty days before taking the road skills test.

sec03-card-sec03-R13.front: How does the online Know to Drive test differ from testing with a designated driver examiner?
sec03-card-sec03-R13.expected_back: Driver examiners give the official vision and knowledge tests, while the online Know to Drive test is only part of the application and its certificate is not permission to drive.

sec03-card-sec03-F38.front: Under West Virginia's Drive for Five program, in which years does a driver's license expire?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.memory_hook: Expires when age divides by five
sec03-card-sec03-F38.expected_back: Under the Drive for Five program every driver's license expires in a year in which the holder's age is divisible by five, so a license is normally valid for five years.

sec03-card-sec03-F39.front: For how many years may an initial license run when aligning a driver's age with the five-year cycle?
sec03-card-sec03-F39.expected_back: To phase a driver into the five-year cycle the initial license may be issued for three to seven years depending on age at renewal, so a driver who will be thirty-four in the expiry year receives a six-year license that expires at age forty.

sec03-card-sec03-F40.front: On what exact calendar day do modern West Virginia licenses expire, and which two birthdays add a thirty-day color grace period?
sec03-card-sec03-F40.memory_hook: Expires on birthday, eighteen twenty-one grace
sec03-card-sec03-F40.expected_back: Driver's licenses issued after the first of January two thousand one expire on the holder's birthday rather than at the end of the month, and a license expiring on the eighteenth or twenty-first birthday carries a thirty-day grace period to obtain the correctly colored license.

sec03-card-sec03-F41.front: What per-year rate sets renewal fees, and what does a twenty-one-year-old pay through age twenty-five?
sec03-card-sec03-F41.memory_hook: Five dollars yearly, twenty at twenty-one
sec03-card-sec03-F41.expected_back: Renewal fees are five dollars for each year until the holder's age is next divisible by five, so a driver renewing at twenty-one receives a license expiring on the twenty-fifth birthday and pays twenty dollars.

sec03-card-sec03-F42.front: Which male applicants can register with Selective Service on the back of a license, permit, or photo card form?
sec03-card-sec03-F42.expected_back: Young men aged fifteen to twenty-six may register with the United States Selective Service when applying for a license, permit or photo identification card by checking a box on the back of the application.

sec03-card-sec03-F43.front: Which three health or hearing conditions can an applicant print on a card by marking the back of the application?
sec03-card-sec03-F43.expected_back: An applicant who is diabetic, deaf or hard of hearing may have that designation placed on the license or identification card by indicating it on the back of the application form turned in at application.

sec03-card-sec03-F44.front: How do you update organ-donor registry status online versus changing the donor symbol printed on your physical card?
sec03-card-sec03-F44.expected_back: Checking the organ donor box on the back of the application sends the applicant's information to a regional organ donation group for the registry, and while registry membership can be changed online at any time, changing the designation printed on the card requires a new license and any applicable fees.

sec03-card-sec03-F45.front: Which discharge, military card, or license-plate records verify honorable discharge for a veterans designation?
sec03-card-sec03-F45.expected_back: An honorably discharged veteran who wants the veterans designation must have status verified through discharge documents such as the DD two fourteen form, a military identification card or a current military license plate registration card, and the DMV may also confirm plate status through the vehicle system.

sec03-card-sec03-F47.front: On the printed fee table, what fees apply to Level One at fifteen, Level Two at sixteen, and Level Three at seventeen versus eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F47.memory_hook: Five, five, then two-fifty or five
sec03-card-sec03-F47.expected_back: The fee table shows a Level One permit at age fifteen expiring on the eighteenth birthday plus a thirty-day grace period for a five-dollar permit fee, a Level Two license at sixteen valid until eighteen for five dollars, and a Level Three license at seventeen valid until twenty-one for two dollars and fifty cents per year or five dollars per year when first issued at eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F48.front: What fees apply to an adult permit, Class E yearly plus expired fee, Class F yearly, a duplicate, and a knowledge test?
sec03-card-sec03-F48.expected_back: A regular instruction permit at eighteen runs six months from issuance for seven dollars and fifty cents, a Class E driver's license costs five dollars per year with a five-dollar expired fee, a Class F license costs two dollars and fifty cents per year, a duplicate license costs seven dollars and fifty cents, and every knowledge test attempt costs seven dollars and fifty cents.

sec03-card-sec03-F49.front: How much extra does it cost to obtain, renew, or duplicate a For Federal Identification card?
sec03-card-sec03-F49.expected_back: An additional ten dollars is required to obtain, renew or duplicate a For Federal Identification driver's license or identification card.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: Why can your very first license under Drive for Five run anywhere from three to seven years instead of exactly five?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: The Drive for Five cycle gives a five-year license, but the first license in the cycle may run anywhere from three to seven years so that expiry lands in a year when the age is divisible by five.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: Why do two drivers pay different renewal totals even though the five-dollar yearly rate stays identical?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: The renewal fee is five dollars for each year until the age divisible by five, so the total varies with the term even though the per-year rate has not increased.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.front: How does the per-year fee for a Level Three license change if first issued at seventeen versus eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.memory_hook: Two-fifty at seventeen, five at eighteen
sec03-card-sec03-R11.expected_back: A Level Three license costs two dollars and fifty cents per year when issued at seventeen but five dollars per year when first issued at eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.front: When must a teen under eighteen transferring from out of state take both knowledge and road skills tests like a brand-new applicant?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.expected_back: An applicant under eighteen transferring from another state without a graduated license that equals or exceeds West Virginia's Level Two, or from a jurisdiction with no graduated program, must take the road skills test and knowledge examination as if never licensed.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.front: How does bringing a current prior-state driving record help an under-eighteen transfer applicant?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.memory_hook: Credits prior time toward Level One
sec03-card-sec03-F35.expected_back: An under-eighteen transfer applicant who presents a current driving record from the previous jurisdiction is credited with the time the previous license was held toward the required Level One period, and that record becomes part of the West Virginia driving record.

sec03-card-sec03-F36.front: Where do restriction codes and explanations appear on a West Virginia license, and what can breaking one cause?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.expected_back: The DMV may impose license restrictions for safe operation, shown by a number or letter code in the restrictions field on the front of the license with the explanation on the back, and driving in violation of a restriction is a serious offense that can bring suspension or revocation.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.front: Which vision, vehicle-equipment, time-of-day, or medical restrictions appear on the handbook's list?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.expected_back: Listed license restrictions include artificial limbs, corrective lenses, automatic transmission, mechanical signals, hand controls, outside mirrors, motor-driven cycle, daylight driving only, an ignition interlock, a spinner knob and a medical variance, and the DMV may impose others not listed.

sec03-card-sec03-F46.front: To whom must you produce your license on demand, what offense is failing, and how do you avoid conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-F46.memory_hook: Show valid license later avoids conviction
sec03-card-sec03-F46.expected_back: You must carry your driver's license when driving and produce the license or instruction permit on demand to any law enforcement officer, magistrate or DMV official, a violation is a misdemeanor, but there is no conviction if the license was valid at the time of arrest and is produced in court or at the arresting officer's office.

sec03-card-sec03-F50.front: Along with your driver's license, which two vehicle documents must stay aboard and be shown during a moving-violation stop?
sec03-card-sec03-F50.expected_back: Along with the driver's license you must keep valid proof of West Virginia liability insurance and the current registration card in the vehicle, and show them with the license when a law enforcement officer stops you for a moving violation.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.front: When does a misdemeanor charge for failing to produce your license end with zero conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.expected_back: Failing to produce a license on demand is a misdemeanor, but a driver whose license was valid at arrest and who later produces it in court or at the officer's office is not convicted.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: At least how many items appear on West Virginia's knowledge screening, and what topics do they cover?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: The knowledge examination has at least twenty-five questions based on the basic knowledge, traffic rules, regulations, signs and markings found in the handbook.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: How many of twenty-five knowledge items must be right to pass, and how are timed-out blanks scored?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: Automated testing is given at all locations, you must answer nineteen of the twenty-five questions correctly to pass, and because the test has a time limit any question not answered in the prescribed time counts as incorrect.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: Who may use the headphone audio version, what may DMV staff never do, and why might you wait?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: An audio version of the knowledge examination with headphones is available for the reading impaired, it covers the same material under the same rules, DMV employees may not read, reword or explain questions beyond what printed-test applicants receive, and headsets are limited so you may have to wait.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: How do the twenty-five minimum count, nineteen passing mark, and countdown timer interact?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: The knowledge examination asks at least twenty-five questions and requires nineteen correct answers, and an unanswered question counts as wrong once the time limit runs out.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: Why are DMV employees barred from reading, rewording, or explaining prompts on both audio and printed versions?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: The audio knowledge test covers the same material under the same rules as the printed test, so staff may not read, reword or explain questions for either version.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: What visual acuity must new and renewing applicants meet, and what three extra visual traits may be checked?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: Every applicant, new or renewing, must pass the vision screening, which requires twenty-forty vision or better using both eyes, with or without conventional corrective lenses, and no serious visual defect, and depth perception, color recognition and peripheral vision may also be checked.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: May applicants wear bi-optic or telescopic lenses to pass West Virginia's visual acuity standard?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Special lens arrangements such as bi-optic or telescopic lenses may not be used to satisfy the visual acuity standard.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: When is a corrective-lenses restriction added, and how can an applicant with sight in one eye pass?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: If glasses or contact lenses are needed to reach twenty-forty vision the license carries a corrective lenses restriction code, and an applicant with only one eye may pass if that eye sees twenty-forty or better.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: What steps follow when an applicant falls short of twenty-forty acuity or shows a serious visual defect?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: An applicant with vision below twenty-forty or a serious visual defect fails the screening and is told to consult a vision specialist, and if the vision cannot be corrected to that level a licensed vision care specialist must send the DMV a statement describing the condition and recommending whether and under what restrictions the applicant can drive safely.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: Which body may review a vision specialist's statement at the Commissioner's discretion before licensing?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: Vision specialist statements may be reviewed by the Driver's License Advisory Board at the discretion of the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles before an instruction permit or license is issued.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: How does West Virginia's twenty-forty standard treat two eyes, one eye, and bi-optic or telescopic optics?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.memory_hook: Two or one twenty-forty, no telescopic
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: The vision standard is twenty-forty with both eyes, yet an applicant with a single eye passes with twenty-forty in that eye, and neither may be reached with bi-optic or telescopic lenses.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: What separates getting a simple corrective-lenses code from needing a specialist's statement and possible board review?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Needing glasses to reach twenty-forty earns a corrective lenses restriction, whereas vision that cannot be corrected to twenty-forty requires a vision specialist's statement and possible advisory board review.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: Which legal standards and documents must your road-skills vehicle meet, and what can defects cause?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: The vehicle used for the road skills test must comply with registration, vehicle inspection and equipment laws, needs a valid inspection sticker and proof of insurance, and vehicle defects may constitute failure of the examination.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: If a minor vehicle issue turns up before driving, what may the examiner allow and what swap is barred?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: The examiner may permit a minor defect to be corrected so the examination continues, but you may not continue the examination in another vehicle on the same test date.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: What happens if an applicant cannot locate and demonstrate every safety control, including the parking brake?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: The examiner cannot give the driving test unless the vehicle is in safe condition and legally equipped, and an applicant who cannot both locate and demonstrate every piece of safety equipment, including the parking or emergency brake, automatically fails the road skills test.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: Which flashing colors, noise devices, window items, and extra spotlights count as illegal vehicle equipment?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: Illegal equipment includes red or blue flashing lights, which only authorized emergency vehicles may carry, sirens, bells or whistles, a cutout or loud-sounding muffler, signs, posters or stickers on the windshield or windows unless required or permitted by law, and more than one spotlight.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: What limits govern side cowl lights, backup lamps, forward-lit reverse lights, and cargo past fenders?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: It is also illegal to have more than two side cowl or fender lights, more than two backup lights, backup lights that show light while the vehicle moves forward, or any load extending beyond the fender line on the left side or more than six inches beyond the fender line on the right side.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: Which windshield, window-tint transmission, lens, and body or door defects make a vehicle illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: Further illegal equipment includes a vehicle without safety glass, windows tinted to less than thirty-five percent light transmission, a broken or cracked windshield, holes in the body, broken lenses, and doors or windows that do not operate.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: How do fixing a minor car defect and switching to another vehicle on the same date differ?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: A minor defect may be corrected so the road test continues, but switching to a different vehicle on the same test date is not permitted.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: What are the maximum legal counts for spotlights, side cowl lamps, and backup lights, plus reverse-light behavior?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.memory_hook: One spot, two cowl, two reverse
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: A vehicle may carry at most one spotlight, two side cowl or fender lights and two backup lights, and backup lights must never show light while moving forward.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: Why do left-side and right-side cargo overhang limits differ at zero inches versus six inches past fenders?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: A load may not extend beyond the fender line at all on the left side but may extend up to six inches beyond it on the right side.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: What minimum light percentage must window tint pass, and does legal tint excuse cracked glass or broken lenses?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: Window tint must let through at least thirty-five percent of light, and a cracked windshield or a broken lens is illegal equipment regardless of tint.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: Which five driver qualifications does West Virginia's licensing evaluation measure against state standards?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: The driver examination is a series of tests measuring your qualifications against established standards, covering vision, color recognition, knowledge of traffic laws, recognition of road signs, and the ability to operate a motor vehicle safely and skillfully in traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: What is the examiner watching during your drive, and why shouldn't a clipboard mark rattle you?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.memory_hook: Focus driving, marks aren't always errors
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: Examiners are trained professionals who ride along only to see that you can control the vehicle and observe the rules of the road, so concentrate on your driving rather than your errors, and a mark on the score sheet does not necessarily mean you made an error.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: How well does the West Virginia DMV ask every licensed motorist to drive once licensed?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: On behalf of the state the DMV asks every licensed driver to drive as well as or better than during the examination.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: Who must complete the short DUI awareness course after road skills, and how is completion recorded?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Every first-time applicant for a driver's license must complete a short DUI awareness course given upon passing the road skills test, including out-of-state drivers coming into West Virginia even if previously licensed here, and completion is shown by a card or a stamp on the application.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: Does holding a West Virginia license years ago exempt an incoming out-of-state driver from DUI awareness?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: The short DUI awareness course after the road skills test is required of first-time applicants and of out-of-state drivers coming into West Virginia even if they once held a West Virginia license.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: Why must drivers memorize traffic sign shapes and colors rather than relying on printed words alone?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: The shape and color of a sign carry meaning, so a driver should still recognize a sign and respond correctly when fading light, fog, rain, snow or darkness make the letters hard to read.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: Which sign uses the eight-sided octagon exclusively, and what two actions does it require?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: The eight-sided octagon is reserved for stop signs, which require a complete stop and giving the right-of-way to pedestrians and to all cross traffic before moving again.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: Where do you halt at a stop sign when a crosswalk exists versus when no markings or crosswalk exist?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: At a stop sign you stop behind any marked or unmarked crosswalk, and where there are no pavement markings or crosswalk you stop before entering the intersection at a place where you can see traffic coming from all directions.
