sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: What right-of-way duty does an upside-down triangular traffic sign impose?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: An upside-down triangular sign requires you to yield the right-of-way to cross traffic or to merging traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: What roadway restriction begins right at a pennant-shaped traffic sign?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: A pennant-shaped sign marks the beginning of a no-passing zone.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: What hazard ahead is announced by a circular yellow-and-black road sign?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: A yellow-and-black circular sign gives advance warning of a railroad crossing ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: What does a five-sided pentagon sign mark, and how far along abutting streets does a West Virginia school zone reach?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: A pentagon-shaped sign warns of a school zone ahead or marks a school zone crossing, and a school zone covers the school grounds plus any abutting street or highway for one hundred twenty-five feet from the grounds.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: What is West Virginia's maximum school-zone speed limit, and under what two triggers does it apply?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: The maximum speed limit in a school zone is fifteen miles per hour when children are present or when the sign specifies it.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: Which two vehicle situations are marked by an upright triangle with a red border and fluorescent orange center?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: A right-side-up triangular emblem with a reflective red border and a fluorescent orange center identifies a slow-moving vehicle or a vehicle that has made an emergency stop.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: How does the required driver action differ between an eight-sided octagon and an upside-down triangle?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: The octagon demands a complete stop before giving way, whereas the upside-down triangle only requires yielding the right-of-way to cross or merging traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: Which two high-risk zones are separated by round yellow-and-black signs versus five-sided pentagon signs?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: The yellow-and-black circle is the advance warning of a railroad crossing, while the pentagon marks a school zone or school crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: How does a sideways no-passing pennant differ from an upright red-bordered orange triangle?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: The pennant marks where a no-passing zone begins, while the right-side-up triangle with a red border and orange center marks a slow-moving or emergency-stopped vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.front: How do the hundred-twenty-five-foot school boundary and the fifteen-mile-per-hour speed cap work together?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.expected_back: A school zone reaches one hundred twenty-five feet along the street from the school grounds, and its fifteen miles per hour limit applies when children are present or when specified.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: What do square and rectangular signs regulate, and how do white, solid red, and diagonal-bar red designs differ?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.memory_hook: White regulates, red urgent, slash bans
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: Square and rectangular signs show traffic regulations such as speed limits and guide your speed and direction, most are white with black letters, a very important message is red with white letters, and a red outline with a diagonal bar always means no.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: Where does a No U-Turn sign forbid turning your vehicle around?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: A no U-turn sign means you may not turn around in the middle of a street or at an intersection.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: What do No Right Turn and No Left Turn signs prohibit, and at what two intersection setups are they placed?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: No right turn and no left turn signs show which direction you cannot turn at an intersection, and they are used where a one-way street is met or where turning would be unsafe.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: What danger awaits any motorist who drives past Wrong Way or Do Not Enter signs?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: Wrong way and do not enter signs warn that traffic in that direction is prohibited, and a driver who enters a lane so marked will likely run into another vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: How is a highway lane beneath a Dual Turn Lane sign shared, and what maneuver is strictly prohibited inside it?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.memory_hook: Both ways turn left, zero passing
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: A dual turn lane sign is posted over a highway lane used only for left turns from either direction, traffic from both directions shares that lane, and a turning lane must never be used to overtake and pass other vehicles.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: Where along divided highways stand lane direction signs, and what mistake do they prevent?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: Lane direction signs are posted between divided highway lanes at the openings in the dividers where streets intersect, to remind you which side of the divider you belong on.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: What does a One Way sign reveal about a cross street, and how are consecutive downtown blocks usually arranged?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: A one way sign tells you that a cross street carries traffic in one direction only, and where one-way streets exist, consecutive blocks usually run in opposite directions.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: How do white highway speed-limit signs differ from black-on-yellow ramp advisory speed signs?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.memory_hook: Optimal legal max versus ramp advice
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: Speed limit signs show the fastest speed you may drive under optimal weather and road conditions and sometimes the minimum speed, while advisory speed signs at interstate entrance and exit ramps, black on yellow, show the maximum recommended safe speed for the ramp.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: How do black-on-white, white-on-red, and red-circle-with-bar regulatory panels rank urgency and bans?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.memory_hook: Routine law, urgent alert, flat ban
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: Most regulatory signs are white with black letters, a red sign with white letters carries a very important message, and a red outline with a diagonal bar always means no.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: What separates a regulatory speed-limit sign from a black-on-yellow ramp advisory sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.memory_hook: Legal cap versus recommended ramp pace
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: A speed limit sign is a regulation showing the fastest legal speed in optimal conditions, whereas a black-on-yellow advisory speed sign on a ramp only recommends a maximum safe speed.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: How does an overhead Dual Turn Lane sign differ in purpose from a lane direction sign at a median opening?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: A dual turn lane sign marks a center lane reserved for left turns from either direction and never for passing, while lane direction signs at divider openings only remind you which side of the divider to use.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: How are standard diamond warning signs styled, and which two hazard types may use yellow-green instead?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Diamond-shaped warning signs are yellow with black letters, usually appear without explanatory words, and warn of possible danger ahead with symbols or written warnings, while pedestrian and school warning signs may be yellow-green with black letters.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: What does a curve or sharp-turn warning tell you about regular highway speed, and what plaque may sit below it?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: A curve or sharp-turn warning means the curve ahead is too sharp to take at regular highway speed, and an advisory speed sign may be attached beneath it.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: What traffic movement must you watch for at a crossroads or side-road warning sign?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: A crossroads or side road warning tells you to watch for other vehicles entering or leaving the highway.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: How do lane-ending, added-lane, and merge warning diamonds differ in what happens ahead?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: A lane-ending warning shows which lane is ending, an added-lane sign advises that a lane is being added, and a merge warning means traffic may be moving into your lane, so be ready to change speed or lane to avoid a crash.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: What roadway flow does a two-way traffic warning sign announce?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: A two-way traffic warning indicates that you are on, or the road ahead carries, two-way traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: What specific hazards and responses match hill, low-clearance, and slippery-when-wet warning signs?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: A hill warning calls for special care and slowing before starting downhill, a low clearance warning gives the height of a bridge or underpass ahead, and a slippery when wet warning calls for reduced speed on a stretch more slippery than other roads.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: What duties follow a pedestrian-crossing warning versus a signal-ahead warning?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: A pedestrian crossing warning tells you to watch for and yield to people walking across the road, and a signal ahead warning tells you a traffic signal is ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: Which two specific warning subjects switch from standard yellow diamonds to yellow-green with black markings?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: Warning diamonds are yellow with black letters, but pedestrian and school warning signs may instead be yellow-green with black letters.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: What shapes and basic background color identify construction and maintenance work-zone signs?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: Construction and maintenance signs notify drivers of unusual or potentially dangerous conditions in or near work areas, most are diamond-shaped with a few rectangular, and orange is the basic color for work zone devices.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: Which five channeling devices steer traffic through work zones, and what helps drivers see them after dark?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: Barricades, vertical panels, drums, cones and tubes are the channeling devices that alert drivers to work zone hazards and guide them safely through, and at night they often carry flashing or steady-burn lights.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.front: What two messages do large flashing or sequencing arrow panels deliver day and night in work zones?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.expected_back: Large flashing or sequencing arrow panels may be used in work zones day and night to guide drivers into certain lanes and to tell them that part of the road ahead is closed.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: How do diagonal stripes on a work-zone barricade or vertical panel show which side to pass on?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: The diagonal stripes on a barricade or vertical panel point toward the side traffic should pass, so stripes sloping downward to the right mean bear right and stripes sloping downward to the left mean bear left.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: What high-visibility clothing and handheld tools do work-zone flaggers use to control traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: Flaggers wearing orange vests, shirts or jackets use red-orange flags or stop and slow paddles to stop, slow or guide traffic safely through work zones.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: Which way do you steer when barricade stripes slope downward right versus downward left?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: Barricade stripes sloping downward to the right tell the driver to bear right, and stripes sloping downward to the left tell the driver to bear left.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.front: How can you still decode an unfamiliar road sign that never appeared in the driver handbook?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.expected_back: Not every sign appears in the handbook, most signs are self-explanatory, warning signs often use pictures instead of text, and the shape and color of a sign are strong indicators of its meaning.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.front: What navigation questions do guide signs answer, and what four subtypes belong in the guide family?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.expected_back: Guide signs tell you where you are, what road you are on and how to get where you want to go, and include service, location, route marker and distance signs.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.front: Which background colors pair with white lettering for directional guides, motorist services, and parks?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.memory_hook: Green direction, blue services, brown parks
sec07-card-sec07-F32.expected_back: Most guide signs are white on green, motorist services signs are white on blue, and signs for parks and public recreation areas are white on brown.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.front: What details appear on intersection guide signs, interstate exit signs, and advance interstate signs?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.expected_back: Guide signs placed before intersections show the direction to cities, interstate exit signs show where the exit is and its number, and advance interstate signs may add the road, location, attraction or upcoming routes and the distance from the exit.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.front: What helpful details do highway distance signs and amenity or rest-area guide signs display?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.expected_back: Distance signs on main highways show the distance to places and routes, other guide signs show the amenities available off interstate exits or mark designated places for travelers to rest, and some carry a symbol above a description or arrow.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.front: How do West Virginia and U.S. highway route markers differ in color from interstate shields?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.expected_back: West Virginia and United States route markers are generally black on white, while interstate markers are red, white and blue.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: What travel categories correspond to white-on-green, white-on-blue, and white-on-brown signs?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.memory_hook: Directions green, services blue, parks brown
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: White on green guides direction, white on blue marks motorist services, and white on brown marks parks and public recreation areas.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: What color difference separates state and U.S. route markers from interstate route markers?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: State and United States route markers are generally black on white, while interstate markers are red, white and blue.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: What speed standard does West Virginia enforce alongside posted signs, and which road types receive statutory defaults?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: Most speed limits are posted, but West Virginia law also prohibits driving at any speed greater than is reasonable and prudent for existing conditions, and the law sets designated speeds for highways and for areas such as school zones and business and residential districts.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: What are West Virginia's four default speed limits for interstates, open county highways, business or residential streets, and active school zones?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Unless otherwise posted or unreasonable for conditions, the designated limits are seventy miles per hour on an interstate, fifty-five miles per hour on an open county highway, twenty-five miles per hour in business or residential areas, and fifteen miles per hour in a school zone while children are present along the roadway.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: What property and how much adjoining street distance make up a legal West Virginia school zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: A school zone is all school property including the school grounds and any street or highway abutting the grounds for one hundred twenty-five feet along the street or highway from the grounds.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: Under what three conditions may an authorized emergency vehicle exceed posted speed limits?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: Authorized emergency vehicles may exceed posted speed limits while on emergency duty with their emergency signal equipment operating, as long as other road users are not endangered.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: How does West Virginia's unposted interstate speed limit compare with an open county highway?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: The interstate designated limit is seventy miles per hour, while an open county highway is limited to fifty-five miles per hour, each unless otherwise posted.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: How does the designated speed limit drop when moving from business or residential streets into a school zone with children present?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: Business and residential areas carry a twenty-five miles per hour limit, but a school zone drops to fifteen miles per hour while children are present along the roadway.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: Which vehicles alone may legally exceed a posted limit, and what safeguards still bind them?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: Only an authorized emergency vehicle on emergency duty with its signal equipment operating may exceed the posted limit, and even then only without endangering other road users.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: What assumption do surrounding motorists make about your path, and how do turn signals protect you?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Other drivers expect you to keep traveling in the same direction, so your turn signals tell them you intend to turn or change lanes, and you should give them time to react to your moves.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: Before which five everyday maneuvers must you activate your turn signal?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: Use your turn signal before you change lanes, turn at an intersection, enter or leave an interstate, pull away from the curb, or pull over to the side of the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: How far ahead must you signal a turn, and why must you cancel the blinker afterward?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: Signal every time you make a change and at least one hundred feet before you plan to turn, then switch the signal off after completing the turn, because driving with a signal on without turning creates confusion.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: What happens if you signal too early or too late for a turn located right past an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: When you plan to turn just beyond an intersection, signaling too soon can make other drivers think you are turning at the intersection and pull into your path, while signaling too late leaves drivers behind too little time to react, so judge the traffic conditions.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: Which left-arm positions communicate slow or stop, right turn, and left turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.memory_hook: Down stop, up right, straight left
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: The hand signals are an arm pointing down for slow or stop, an arm pointing up for a right turn, and an arm held straight out for a left turn.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: Why must you balance the one-hundred-foot signal rule carefully when turning into an entrance right past an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: A turn signal is required at least one hundred feet before the turn, yet for a turn just past an intersection signaling too early misleads other drivers as surely as signaling too late.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: Match left-arm down, left-arm up, and left-arm straight out to their exact meanings?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.memory_hook: Down slow, up right, out left
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: An arm pointing down signals slowing or stopping, an arm pointing up signals a right turn, and an arm straight out signals a left turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: Why must every driver both obey posted speed limits and adapt speed to changing conditions?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Exceeding the speed limit endangers the lives of others as well as your own, so observe speed limits and adjust your speed to the driving conditions.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: At which four roadway features and under what visibility or traction conditions should you reduce speed?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: You should slow down when approaching and crossing an intersection, approaching and going around a curve, approaching the top of a hill, traveling on a narrow road, and whenever traffic, weather, roadway hazards or other conditions limit visibility or stopping distance.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: How does climbing speed shrink your ability to handle your own mistakes or another driver's error?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Your speed determines how much time you have to react, and the higher the speed the less time there is to spot hazards, judge the speed of other vehicles and act to avoid your own mistakes and those of other drivers.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: How does the West Virginia manual sum up its simple safety rule for speed?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: The simple safety rule for speed is to observe and follow the limits and always drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for the existing conditions.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: Where on the roadway should you position your vehicle whenever moving slower than normal traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: When you drive at less than the normal speed of traffic you should drive as close as possible to the right edge of the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: What must you do when driving below the designated speed on a two-lane road with no clear passing lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: If you must drive slower than the designated speed on a road with one lane in each direction where overtaking traffic has no clear lane for passing, pull off at the first safe turnout to let faster traffic pass.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: Where should your left and right hands grip the steering wheel, and what two benefits does that placement give?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: Keep both hands on the steering wheel, with the left hand at about the eight o'clock position and the right hand at about four o'clock, which gives maximum control and reduces the chance that a deploying air bag knocks your hands off the wheel.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: Why can you still receive a speeding citation while driving below the posted number?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: A posted limit is a ceiling, not a target, because driving faster than is reasonable and prudent for the conditions is illegal even below the posted number.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: How do right-edge positioning and safe turnouts work together when you drive slower than traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: A slow driver keeps as far right as possible, and on a road with one lane each way and no clear passing lane must pull off at the first safe turnout to let faster traffic by.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: Which clock positions mark West Virginia's recommended steering grip, and what safety device drives that lower placement?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: The recommended grip puts the left hand near eight o'clock and the right hand near four o'clock on the wheel, a low position chosen partly because of the air bag.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: Aside from traffic conflicts or officer orders, which five everyday spots forbid stopping, standing, or parking, including hydrant footage?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: Except to avoid a conflict with other traffic or to obey a law, officer or signal, stopping, standing or parking is prohibited on a sidewalk, in front of a public or private driveway, within an intersection, within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant, and on a crosswalk.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: What no-parking distances apply at corner crosswalks, stop signs or signals, and railroad rails, plus curb cuts?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.memory_hook: Twenty crosswalk, thirty sign, fifty rail
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: Parking is also prohibited within twenty feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, within thirty feet of any stop sign or traffic control signal, in front of a wheelchair ramp or curb cut, and within fifty feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Where is parking banned around street work, curb-parked cars, bridges or tunnels, and daily-delivery mailboxes?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.memory_hook: No work zones, bridges, twenty-foot mail
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: Parking is further prohibited beside or opposite a street excavation or obstruction where it would obstruct traffic, on the traffic side of a vehicle stopped or parked at the curb, on any bridge, elevated structure or highway tunnel, and within twenty feet of a mailbox served by a carrier making daily deliveries by motor vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: Where on highways is parking prohibited, and what curb paint color signals a no-parking zone?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: Parking is prohibited on any controlled-access highway, anywhere on a highway where it endangers the safety and convenience of the traveling public, and wherever official signs prohibit it, and a curb in a no-parking zone may be painted yellow.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: List the four climbing no-parking distances from fire hydrant to corner crosswalk, stop sign, and railroad rail?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: The no-parking distances climb from fifteen feet at a fire hydrant, to twenty feet from a crosswalk at an intersection, to thirty feet from a stop sign or signal, to fifty feet from the nearest railroad rail.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: What mailbox buffer, elevated or enclosed structures, highway class, and curb color all forbid parking?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Within twenty feet of a daily-delivery mailbox, on any bridge or tunnel and on any controlled-access highway are all banned parking spots, and a yellow-painted curb marks a no-parking zone.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: Why must every motorist master proper turning procedures, and who suffers most in turn crashes?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Improper turns cause many traffic crashes and pedestrians and bicyclists are often their victims, so a driver must learn and follow correct turning procedures.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: Instead of diving late, what three checks come before moving into a turning lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Prepare for a turn instead of deciding at the last moment, and before entering the turning lane signal, look in the mirrors and check the blind spot by glancing over the proper shoulder.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: How far ahead must you signal a turn, and when should your braking happen?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: Signal at least one hundred feet before turning, slow down before the turn, and do not brake while turning.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: What traffic and pedestrian checks precede a turn, and where must the maneuver end?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Before turning make sure it is safe by checking traffic to the front and rear and watching for pedestrians, and always finish the turn in the proper lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: What must you do when turning left if oncoming traffic will reach the intersection around the same moment?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: When turning left watch for approaching traffic in the opposite lane, and if that traffic will reach the intersection at about the same time as you, stop until it is safe to turn.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: Why must your front wheels stay pointed straight ahead while stopped waiting to turn left?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: While waiting to turn left do not turn the wheels to the left, because a bump from behind could push your vehicle into oncoming traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: When are right turns on red and left turns on red permitted in West Virginia?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: Where no sign prohibits a turn on red, traffic facing a red signal may turn right after a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and traffic, and the same rule covers a left turn from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: Where do curves, hill crests, visibility distance, and signs make turning your vehicle around unlawful?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: It is against the law to turn your vehicle around near a curve, near the crest of a hill where a vehicle approaching within five hundred feet in either direction cannot see you, or where signs prohibit turning.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: How much clear visibility in both directions is required to turn around near a curve or hill crest?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: Turning around is illegal near a curve or hill crest whenever a vehicle approaching within five hundred feet in either direction cannot see you, and anywhere a sign prohibits it.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: Combine wheel angle and oncoming-traffic timing for waiting safely to turn left?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: A driver waiting to turn left keeps the wheels straight to avoid being pushed into oncoming traffic, and stops to let opposing traffic through when both would reach the intersection at about the same time.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: How far out from parked cars do you line up to angle park on the right, and when do you cut in?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: To angle park on your right, signal and slow down, stay parallel to the curb at least five feet out from the parked vehicles, steer sharply right when your front end is even with the rear of the space, pull slowly into the middle of the space, then straighten the wheel and roll forward until the front wheel barely touches the curb.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: What three precautions apply when backing out of a visibility-blocked angle parking stall?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: Backing out of an angle space is hazardous, so do not rely on the rear view mirror alone, move back cautiously watching for a pedestrian or vehicle that may suddenly appear if your view is blocked, and do not back across the center line.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: Which way do you turn front wheels when parking downhill, uphill with a curb, and uphill without a curb?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.memory_hook: Down in, up-curb out, curbless right
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: When parking on a grade turn the front wheels toward the curb side of the highway so the vehicle will not roll, which means wheels to the curb when facing downhill, wheels away from the curb when facing uphill with a curb, and wheels to the right when facing uphill without a curb.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: Along with setting the parking brake on a grade, which gear holds an automatic versus a manual car?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.memory_hook: Park automatic, reverse down, first up
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: On a grade set the emergency or parking brake and reinforce it by placing an automatic transmission in park, or a manual transmission in reverse on a downgrade and in first gear on an upgrade.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: Within how many inches of the curb must parallel-parked wheels rest, and how must the vehicle sit?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: When parallel parking on a two-way street the right wheels must be parallel to and within eighteen inches of the right curb, when parking on the left side of a road the wheels must be within eighteen inches of the left curb, and the vehicle must face the direction of traffic and be centered in the space.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: Where do you stop beside the front car to start parallel parking, and which way do wheels turn first?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: To parallel park, choose a space large enough, signal and stop even with the front vehicle about two feet out from it, then when traffic is clear turn the front wheels all the way to the right and back slowly toward the curb while looking behind you rather than relying on the mirror.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: When do you swing the wheel full left during parallel parking, and what ideal versus maximum curb gap applies?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: When your front bumper is opposite the rear bumper of the vehicle ahead, quickly turn the wheel all the way to the left and back slowly toward the vehicle behind without touching it, ending about six inches and never more than eighteen inches from the curb, then straighten the wheels, pull into final position and center the vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: What two steps are mandatory every time you leave a parallel parking stall?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: When leaving a parallel parking space always signal to show your intentions and make sure traffic is clear before pulling back onto the roadway.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: Contrast front-wheel direction for downhill, uphill with a curb, and uphill without a curb?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: Facing downhill the wheels turn toward the curb, facing uphill with a curb they turn away from the curb, and facing uphill without a curb they turn to the right.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: What starting side gap, ideal finished curb distance, and legal maximum curb distance frame parallel parking?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.memory_hook: Two feet, six ideal, eighteen max
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: Parallel parking begins about two feet out from the front vehicle, ends ideally about six inches from the curb, and may never finish more than eighteen inches from it.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: What minimum clearance starts an angle-parking entry, and what line must your exit never cross?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: An angle-parking entry starts at least five feet out from the parked vehicles, while the exit must never back across the center line.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: Which transmission position backs up the parking brake on downhill versus uphill grades for manual and automatic cars?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: On a grade a manual transmission is left in reverse when facing downhill but in first gear when facing uphill, while an automatic transmission simply goes into park.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: Which space zone is easiest to control, what crash type stems from tailgating, and what shapes safe distance?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: Following too closely causes most rear-end collisions, the space ahead of your vehicle is the easiest space to control and is called the following distance, and you must weigh traffic speed and road condition to leave enough distance to stop when necessary.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: How do you measure the three-to-four second following rule using a roadside landmark?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: To apply the three-to-four second rule choose a fixed object ahead such as a signpost, tree, overpass or bridge abutment, start counting one thousand one, one thousand two, one thousand three when the vehicle ahead passes it, and if you reach the object before finishing the count you are following too closely.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: How many seconds of following distance should you keep in darkness or rain versus on ice or snow?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: When it is dark or raining the following distance should be at least four seconds, and when there is ice or snow stay at least six seconds behind the vehicle in front.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: Compare minimum following counts for normal conditions, darkness or rain, and ice or snow?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.memory_hook: Three-to-four normal, four wet, six icy
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: The following-distance count is three to four seconds in normal conditions, at least four seconds in darkness or rain, and at least six seconds on ice or snow.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: What walk-around and head-turn habits apply before and during backing?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: Before backing, check completely around the vehicle for people and obstacles, look to the front, sides and rear and keep looking to the rear while backing, do not depend on the mirror, and back slowly into the proper traffic lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: What is the sole acceptable reason to reverse in a traffic lane, and where is backing strictly forbidden?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Backing up while in a traffic lane is not advisable except to back into a parallel parking space, and you must never back across other traffic lanes or through an intersection.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: How must a parked car face and clear the roadway, and how does West Virginia treat double parking?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: A vehicle must always be parked in the same direction as traffic moves on that side of the street, completely off the traveled portion of the road, and double parking is illegal and discourteous.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: What four steps secure a parked car when leaving, and what must you scan before opening a street-side door?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Whenever you park and leave the vehicle, turn off the engine, set the parking brake, lock the vehicle and take the keys, and because getting out on the street side is dangerous, look carefully for bicycles, motorcycles or larger vehicles that might hit your open door or you.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: What convenience tip applies to parking meters, and how should you protect yourself when sitting parked in busy areas?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: Keep change easily accessible in the vehicle for metered parking, and if you must stay in the parked vehicle in a busy area keep the doors locked until you are ready to exit and stay alert to your surroundings.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: Contrast the one acceptable live-lane backing move against the two backing moves banned everywhere?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: Backing into a parallel space is the only backing the handbook calls acceptable within a traffic lane, and backing across other lanes or through an intersection is never allowed.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: How should you respond when another motorist ignores right-of-way rules, and why?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: Courtesy is a key to safe driving and safety comes before right-of-way, so if another driver does not follow the right-of-way rules you give the right-of-way, because in every situation right-of-way is something to be given, not taken.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: Who must yield when pulling onto a public road out of a driveway, private lane, or alley?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: When entering a public street or highway from an alley, private road or driveway you must yield to the traffic already on the roadway.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: Who yields when two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection or a four-way stop together?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: At an uncontrolled intersection or a four-way stop, when you reach the intersection at the same time as another vehicle you yield to the driver on the right.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: What speed and right-of-way duties apply as you approach an intersection controlled by a yield sign?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: At an intersection with a yield sign, slow down before reaching the intersection and then yield the right-of-way to any vehicle in the intersection and to approaching traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: Which stream of traffic holds right-of-way whenever you prepare to turn left?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: When making a left turn you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: What complete sequence applies when an ambulance, fire rig, or police cruiser approaches with siren and lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: You must yield to any ambulance, fire or police vehicle sounding a siren and flashing warning lights by pulling to the right edge of the road clear of the intersection and stopping until it has passed, keeping your foot on the brake so the emergency driver knows you are stopped, and watching for other emergency vehicles before proceeding.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: Is yielding to a funeral procession law or courtesy in West Virginia, and when may you pass one?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: Yielding to a funeral procession is a courtesy rather than a legal requirement, once the lead vehicle has cleared an intersection the rest of the procession has the right-of-way, you should not cut in or out of it, and you may pass a procession on an expressway.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: What happens when a police officer's hand directions conflict with a posted sign, signal, or lane marking?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: The directions of a police officer overrule the message of any sign, signal or road marking.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: How should you treat a driver parallel parking ahead of you, and what simple rule guides right-of-way?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: Give ample space to the driver in front of you who is parallel parking, and remember the simple safety rule not to rush but to stop and give time to those who have the right-of-way.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: Compare who yields in an uncontrolled or four-way tie versus at a posted yield sign?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: At an uncontrolled or four-way stop intersection a tie goes to the driver on the right, whereas at a yield sign you yield to every vehicle already in the intersection and to approaching traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: Contrast your legal duty toward an emergency vehicle running siren and lights against a funeral procession?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: An emergency vehicle with siren and flashing lights requires pulling to the right and stopping, while yielding to a funeral procession is only a courtesy and a procession may be passed on an expressway.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: Pair the authority that overrides every traffic control with the core mindset of right-of-way?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: A police officer's directions overrule every sign, signal and marking, and right-of-way itself is always given rather than taken.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: Who yields when pulling from a driveway, alley, or private road, and who yields on a left turn?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: A driver entering from a driveway, alley or private road yields to everyone already on the roadway, and a driver turning left yields to oncoming traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: Where do blind sightlines and intersections prohibit overtaking?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: Passing is prohibited on a curve or hill or at any place where you cannot see oncoming traffic, and within one hundred feet of an intersection.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: Within what distance of bridges, viaducts, tunnels, underpasses, or railroad crossings is passing banned?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: Passing is prohibited within one hundred feet of a bridge, viaduct, tunnel or underpass and within one hundred feet of any railroad crossing.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: Which four traffic, sign, pedestrian, and centerline situations also forbid passing?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: Passing is also prohibited when an approaching vehicle is within your passing area, when a sign or highway marking tells you to keep right or not to overtake, when the vehicle ahead has stopped at an intersection to let a pedestrian cross, and when the solid yellow line is in your lane.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: Compare the distance buffer for bridges, tunnels, and rail crossings with the rule for a solid yellow line in your lane?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: The one-hundred-foot no-passing buffer applies before a bridge, viaduct, tunnel, underpass and any railroad crossing, while a solid yellow line in your lane bans passing at any distance.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: What zone, following cushion, and speed question should you check before passing on a two-lane highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Before passing on a two-lane highway make sure you are in a passing zone and keeping the three-to-four second following distance, and decide whether passing is necessary, because if you have to speed to pass you probably do not need to pass.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: Where must you look, what roadside hazards should you spot, and when do you signal before passing?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: Check ahead, to the rear and to the side before starting to pass, look for other dangers in the passing area such as a narrow bridge, side road or curve, and signal early enough that other drivers know your intentions.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: How do you warn the driver ahead as you pull left to pass during daylight versus at night?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: Move left when the way is clear and sound your horn to alert the driver ahead that you are passing, and at night you may also blink your headlights to signal that you are about to pass.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: When is it safe to signal back into your lane after passing, and when is passing on the right allowed?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Signal and return to your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle, both headlights, in your rear view mirror, and passing on the right is not permissible unless there is a lane designated for passing.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: Which three sight, oncoming-gap, and vehicle-capability conditions must all hold to pass safely?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: You cannot pass safely unless you can see far enough ahead, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle is capable of the speed needed to pass.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: Which side is standard for overtaking, and what sole roadway feature allows passing on the right?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Passing is done on the left, and passing on the right is allowed only where a lane is designated for passing.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: Contrast how you alert a vehicle you are overtaking in daylight versus after dark?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: The horn alerts the driver ahead that you are passing by day, and at night a blink of the headlights may serve the same purpose.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: Why isn't clearing the passed car's front bumper enough to pull back right, and what mirror cue confirms clearance?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: You return to your lane only when both headlights of the passed vehicle show in your rear view mirror, not when its front bumper merely drops behind you.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: List the mirror, shoulder, adjacent-lane, signal, and speed steps of a proper lane change?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: To change lanes properly check the rear view and side mirrors, make a head check over the left or right shoulder for anyone in your blind spot, check for other drivers moving into the same lane, then signal and change lanes while staying within the speed limit.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: At which two types of crossings must you never change lanes?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: Do not change lanes in an intersection or at a railroad crossing.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: Combine the two visual checks needed for every lane change with the two crossings where lane changes are banned?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: A lane change needs a mirror check plus a head check for the blind spot, and it is never made in an intersection or at a railroad crossing.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: Where must both directions stop for a flashing-red school bus, and which three cues allow proceeding?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: On every highway, street, parking lot, private road or driveway, traffic in both directions must stop before reaching a school bus whose red lights are flashing while it receives or discharges students, and may not proceed until the bus moves again, the bus driver signals, or the visual signals stop.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: On what single highway type is oncoming traffic across a median excused from stopping for a school bus?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: Only on an interstate highway is traffic coming toward a school bus that is stopped on the other side of the median excused from stopping.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: Does the school-bus stop rule still apply on school grounds or private property?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: You must also stop for a stopped school bus that is receiving or discharging students on school property or on private property.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: What first-offense penalties hit drivers who pass a stopped school bus, and what if the driver cannot be identified?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: A first offense of passing a stopped school bus brings a minimum sixty-day license suspension and a minimum fine of five hundred dollars or jail for up to six months, later offenses carry heavier penalties, and when the driver cannot be identified the vehicle's owner or lessee is guilty of a misdemeanor subject to fines.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: Must traffic stop for a loading public transit bus, and what precautions still apply?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: Traffic does not have to stop for a public bus, but you should watch for passengers crossing the street as they get on and off, look out for children who may forget the rule, and use caution when passing a bus that is loading or unloading.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: Summarize where both directions must stop for a flashing-red school bus versus the sole exception?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: Traffic in both directions must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights on every kind of road, lot and driveway, and only on an interstate is oncoming traffic across the median excused.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: How does your legal duty behind a loading public transit bus differ from a school bus?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: Traffic does not have to stop for a public bus loading passengers, unlike a school bus, but must watch for passengers crossing and pass with caution.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.front: Recap the minimum license suspension, fine, and jail exposure for a first offense of passing a stopped school bus?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.expected_back: Passing a stopped school bus costs at least sixty days of suspension plus a minimum five hundred dollar fine or up to six months in jail on a first offense.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: Even with lighter traffic volume, how does the nighttime fatal crash rate compare with daytime driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: Although fewer miles are driven at night, the fatal crash rate for night driving is three times greater than for day driving.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: Under which three distance and street-lighting situations must you switch from high beams to low beams?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, two hundred ahead
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: Dim your headlights within five hundred feet of an approaching vehicle, within two hundred feet of the vehicle ahead of you, and when driving on well-lit streets.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: Which headlight setting works in fog, and where should you look and how should you pace against oncoming glare?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: Use low beams in fog because high beams reflect the light back into your eyes, avoid looking directly into oncoming headlights by looking toward the right edge of the road, and slow down when facing their glare.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: What night-stopping rule governs your speed, and when is using parking lights alone lawful?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: Make sure you can stop within the area lighted by your headlights, and use your parking lights only when you are parked.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: During what hours, weather conditions, and visibility distance must your headlights stay turned on?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.memory_hook: Sunset to sunrise, five hundred feet
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: Turn on your headlights from sunset to sunrise, in fog, smoke or rain, and at any other time when people and vehicles cannot be seen clearly at five hundred feet, remembering that when you have trouble seeing other vehicles they are probably having trouble seeing you, and keep headlights and taillights properly adjusted and clean.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: Contrast the high-beam dimming footage for an oncoming vehicle versus a vehicle you are following?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, two hundred rear
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: Headlights are dimmed within five hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle but within two hundred feet of a vehicle you are following.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: Pair the daytime visibility threshold that mandates headlights with the proper beam choice for fog?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: Headlights must be on whenever people and vehicles cannot be seen clearly at five hundred feet, and in fog the low beams are used because high beams reflect back.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: Roughly what share of traffic deaths involve pedestrians, where is extra care vital, and how may you warn walkers?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: Vehicle-pedestrian collisions account for nearly twenty percent of traffic fatalities, so drivers must use extreme care near special hazards such as school zones, bus stops, playgrounds and parks, and may sound the horn to warn pedestrians when necessary.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: In which three situations do pedestrians hold the legal right-of-way over vehicles?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when they are in a crosswalk, when they cross a sidewalk that crosses an alley entrance or driveway, and when a blind person crosses with a white or metal cane, with or without a red tip, or led by a guide dog.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: Which crossing, road-side walking, signal, and nighttime visibility duties apply to pedestrians?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: Pedestrians must use crosswalks at intersections, look both ways before crossing, walk on the left side facing oncoming traffic and on the shoulder if possible where there is no sidewalk, obey walk and don't walk signals, and at night wear white or light-colored clothing or carry a light.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: Where does West Virginia prohibit pedestrians from walking?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Pedestrians must not walk on interstate highways or in other areas where posted signs prohibit walking.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: At which blind road features and recreational areas should you stay alert for joggers?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: Be alert for joggers in unexpected places such as curves, hilltops and corners, and expect heavy jogging traffic near parks and jogging paths.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: Where do children create heightened roadway risk, and what driveway check is essential?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: Be extra careful in residential areas, school zones and wherever children are likely to be, teach your own children the rights and duties of pedestrians early, and watch for children who may have run behind the vehicle when backing in or out of a driveway.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: Which canes or assistance animals establish a blind pedestrian's right-of-way?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: A blind pedestrian has the right-of-way when crossing with a white or metal cane, whether or not it has a red tip, or when led by a guide dog.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: Why can motorcycles surprise car drivers, and how much lane width belongs to a motorcyclist?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: Motorcycles are hard to see, can often stop more quickly than cars and can dart in front of you without warning, so motorists should always expect motorcycles, give them space and time to maneuver, and remember that a motorcyclist is entitled to and will use the entire lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: What minimum following count applies behind a motorcycle, and when must you stretch it further?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: Keep a safe minimum three-to-four second following distance behind a motorcycle and increase it at night and in adverse weather, because a motorcyclist in a crash will almost certainly be badly hurt or killed.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: Why do drivers overlook motorcycles at street corners, and how do you counter that trap?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: At a corner a motorcycle is hard to see because parked vehicles and trees hide it and you are normally looking for cars and trucks, so check carefully as you leave the corner and keep looking all the way across the intersection.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: How do you follow and overtake a motorcycle safely on a multilane or two-lane road?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: When following a motorcycle stay farther back than you would behind a car because it can slow or stop much faster, and when passing go all the way into the other lane, since the rider has the legal right to the entire lane and may need to swerve, then wait until you are well down the road before moving back.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: What typical weight, fifty-five-mile-per-hour stopping multiple, turning room, and blind-spot traits define heavy trucks?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: Heavy trucks, which typically weigh eighty thousand pounds and are driven by trained specially licensed drivers, need three times a car's stopping distance when fully loaded at fifty-five miles per hour, are longer, heavier and harder to maneuver, need much more room to turn, and have larger blind spots.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: What is a truck's No-Zone, how long may you stay there, and what mirror test exposes it?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: A truck's blind spots, called the No-Zone, are dangerous because the truck driver cannot see vehicles there, the larger the vehicle the larger the blind spots, you should not stay in the No-Zone longer than needed to pass safely, and if you cannot see the driver's reflection in the truck's side mirror you are in a blind spot.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: Along with room for wide right turns and backing, how many seconds ahead of a passed truck do you wait before merging right?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: Truck safety practices include respecting the differences between trucks and cars, avoiding the No-Zone, giving trucks plenty of room including extra room for right turns and for backing up, allowing two seconds after passing before merging right in dry conditions and at least four to six seconds in wet conditions, and calling the authorities about unsafe truck driving.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: Name the six dangerous moves you must never make around a heavy truck?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: Never linger in the No-Zone, never underestimate a truck's size or speed, never slam on your brakes in front of a truck, never cut off a truck to reach an exit or turn, never tailgate a truck, and never pass a truck on the right during a turn.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: Compare the time cushion needed before merging back right ahead of a passed truck on dry versus wet roads?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: After passing a truck in dry conditions allow two seconds before merging back to the right, but in wet conditions allow at least four to six seconds.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: Pair a typical heavy truck's loaded weight with its stopping-distance multiple at fifty-five miles per hour?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: A fully loaded tractor-trailer at fifty-five miles per hour needs three times a car's stopping distance, and a typical heavy truck weighs eighty thousand pounds.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: Why do you trail a motorcycle farther back, and how do you complete a pass around one?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: You follow a motorcycle from farther back because it stops faster than a car, and when passing you move fully into the other lane and return only when well down the road.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: Which machinery displays the triangular slow-moving emblem, and how must regular traffic respond?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: Slow-moving vehicles such as farm vehicles and construction equipment are often driven on or along highways and must display the triangular slow-moving vehicle emblem, and regular traffic must allow for their slow speed and make sure a pass is safe before attempting it.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: Where may animal riders travel, what traffic rights apply, and what horn rule protects horses?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: Animal riders may use most public highways but not interstates, they have the same rights and duties as motor vehicle users, and a driver approaching a horse must take every precaution against frightening it and must never sound the horn near a horse.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: How should you pass a bicyclist by day or night, and during which daily hours is bike traffic heaviest?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: When passing a bicyclist slow down, make sure the rider is aware of you and leave plenty of room, wait for approaching traffic to pass if there is no room, dim your lights for an oncoming bicyclist at night, and take extra care in the morning and afternoon when bicyclists travel between home, work, school or play.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: Why must motorists always give a bicyclist the benefit of the doubt even if the rider makes a mistake?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: Bicyclists are expected to know and obey all traffic laws, but whether or not a bicyclist is riding lawfully you always give the rider the benefit of the doubt, because a bicycle is small and light and almost any collision will injure or kill the rider.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: Summarize West Virginia's rules for cyclists on signaling, riding two abreast, hitching rides, walkers, and flow direction?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: Bicyclists must signal turns and stops unless both hands are needed on the handlebars for balance, keep within a single lane when riding side by side without holding up traffic, never hang onto another vehicle, yield to pedestrians, obey the same rules as other drivers, and ride in the same direction as other vehicles.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: Under what seat and handlebar conditions may a bicyclist carry a passenger or a package?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: A bicyclist may carry a passenger only on an attached seat and may not carry anything that interferes with control of the bicycle or prevents keeping at least one hand on the handlebars.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: What reflector, brake performance, audible bell distance, banned sound devices, and night headlight visibility must every bike have?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: Every bicycle must have a red rear reflector, brakes strong enough to stop one wheel on dry, level, clean pavement, a bell or other device audible for at least one hundred feet with no siren or whistle permitted, and for riding after dark a white headlight visible at least five hundred feet to the front.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: What three progressive steps defuse a tailgater riding right on your rear bumper?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.memory_hook: Flash brake lights, slow, pull over
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: When your rear view mirror shows a tailgater, tap the brakes gently to flash the brake lights as a warning, slow down to encourage the vehicle to pass, and if all else fails pull over, stop and let it pass.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: Combine where animal riders are prohibited with the number-one sound rule around horses?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: Animal riders share the rights and rules of motor vehicle users on most public highways but are barred from interstates, and a driver must never sound the horn near a horse.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: Compare the required range for a bicycle's bell against its nighttime front headlight, plus banned sound gear?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: A bicycle's bell must be audible at one hundred feet while its night headlight must be visible at five hundred feet, and a siren or whistle is never permitted on a bicycle.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.front: Pair the lane rule for side-by-side cyclists with passenger-seat and handlebar-hand requirements?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.expected_back: Bicyclists riding side by side must stay within one lane, a passenger rides only on an attached seat, and at least one hand always stays on the handlebars.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: Which roadway enters an interstate, and why must you read its signs closely?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: You enter an interstate by an entrance ramp, paying careful attention to the signs because an exit ramp marked do not enter and wrong way often sits next to the entrance ramp, and advisory speed signs appear on ramps that curve sharply.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: What actions should you take about halfway along an interstate entrance ramp?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: About halfway along the entrance ramp check the interstate traffic with quick glances over your shoulder and to the side, watch the vehicles ahead of you entering the acceleration lane, use your turn signal, and look for a gap in approaching traffic while adjusting your speed to meet it.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: What speed and steering path should you use as you merge onto an interstate?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: As you merge make sure you are traveling at the same speed as the other traffic, and do not cut sharply to the left into the traffic stream but follow the lane, merge, and only then change lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.front: How should you handle a vehicle ahead in the acceleration lane, and where must you avoid stopping?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.expected_back: If another vehicle is ahead of you in the acceleration lane be prepared for it to slow or stop without warning, and do not stop on the ramp or in the acceleration lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.front: What last-resort option exists if no interstate traffic gap opens before the acceleration lane ends?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.expected_back: If no gap in traffic is available it may be necessary to drive onto the shoulder beyond the end of the acceleration lane and stop, but because entering the traffic stream from a stop is hazardous this maneuver is a last resort.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.front: Who holds the right-of-way when you enter an interstate, and what can you never assume?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.expected_back: Traffic already on the interstate has the right-of-way, and you cannot count on other drivers seeing you or moving over to give you room to enter.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.front: How should you prepare to take an interstate exit safely?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.expected_back: When exiting an interstate watch for the signs that show where your exit is and which lane to use, then signal and move into that lane well before the exit, because changing lanes at the last moment risks missing the exit or causing a crash.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.front: Where and how should you reduce your speed when leaving an interstate?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.expected_back: Most interstate exits have a deceleration lane for slowing before the exit ramp, so never slow down on the interstate itself but wait until you are in the deceleration lane and brake gently until your speed matches the posted exit ramp limit.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: Where does braking for an interstate exit belong, and what speed are you aiming for?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: Braking for an exit belongs in the deceleration lane, never on the interstate itself, and the target is the posted exit ramp speed.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: Where is the only last-resort place to stop if no interstate merge gap opens?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: When no gap appears, the last-resort stop is on the shoulder beyond the end of the acceleration lane, never on the ramp or in the acceleration lane itself.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: Who yields during an interstate merge, and what exact lane sequence must the entering driver follow?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: Traffic already on the interstate holds the right-of-way over entering traffic, so the entering driver matches speed, merges within the lane and only afterwards changes lanes rather than cutting sharply left.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: What crash risk have interstates largely eliminated, and what mental state do they still demand?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: Interstate and divided highways have largely removed the chance of head-on collisions, but interstate driving is very different and demands complete awareness of high-speed driving and constant alertness.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: How should you treat trucks and buses entering an interstate, and which lane belongs to slower traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: Trucks and buses entering an interstate may need extra time to adjust to the traffic pattern, so give them extra time and space, and slower traffic should drive in the right-hand lane except when passing.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.front: When may you use an interstate shoulder, and where do routine stops like driver swaps belong?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.expected_back: Interstate shoulders are only for disabled vehicles and must not be used for changing drivers, reading a map or other non-emergency purposes, which belong in a rest area or off the interstate.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.front: What is an exit gore, and why must you never stop inside it?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.expected_back: Do not stop in an exit gore, the triangular area between the through lane and the exit ramp, because a driver who missed the exit may try to cross the gore and strike your vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.front: Is parking allowed on interstate shoulders, and what can happen to a vehicle left there?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.expected_back: No parking is permitted on the shoulders of interstates, and parked vehicles may be towed.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.front: What maximum, minimum, and pacing rules govern speed on a West Virginia interstate?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.expected_back: Never drive faster than the legal speed limit, do not drive slower than fifty-five miles per hour on an interstate unless weather or road conditions are bad or a lower speed is posted, and always drive at a steady speed.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.front: Why is driving much slower than interstate traffic dangerous, and which lane must you use unless passing?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.expected_back: Driving much slower than other interstate drivers creates a hazard because others may be forced to change lanes abruptly, so always drive in the right-hand lane unless you are passing another vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.front: What lighting does West Virginia law require in adverse conditions, and how else must you adjust?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.expected_back: State law requires headlights to be turned on during adverse conditions, and in such conditions you should adjust your driving, keep an adequate following distance and adjust your speed to allow a safe stop.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: What are the interstate speed floor, speed ceiling, and default travel lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: The interstate floor is fifty-five miles per hour unless conditions are bad or a lower speed is posted, the ceiling is always the legal limit, and the right lane is the place to be unless passing.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: How does the rule for an interstate shoulder differ from the rule for an exit gore?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: The shoulder is for disabled vehicles only and never for parking, while the exit gore between the through lane and the ramp is a place never to stop at all.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: What colors mark an interstate shield, and which directions do even and odd route numbers indicate?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: Interstate highways are identified by distinctive red, white and blue shields, even-numbered interstates run east to west, and odd-numbered interstates run north to south.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: What is the difference between a three-digit interstate starting with an even digit versus an odd digit?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: A three-digit interstate number whose first digit is even identifies a beltway or bypass around a city, while a three-digit number whose first digit is odd identifies a spur route.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: Why should you map your route beforehand, and what five vehicle items should you inspect before an interstate trip?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: Because interstate entrances and exits can be far apart, plan your route in advance and check gas, water, oil and tires including the spare before leaving, since a breakdown on an interstate costs time and can be dangerous.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: Why are interstate interchange guide signs posted well ahead of the turnoff?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: On an interstate the first guide sign for an interchange is placed well before the point where you must turn off, giving time to change lanes and exit smoothly, so watch the guide signs to avoid hazardous last-minute maneuvers.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: How can you tell on an overhead guide sign when a through lane is about to end at a fork or exit?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: Where the number of through lanes changes, an added lane is usually obvious, while a removed lane usually ends at a fork or exit and is indicated by a black and yellow panel below the green and white overhead guide sign.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: How does an interchange let two highways cross without conflict, and what are the three common designs?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: An interchange is the intersection of two highways at different levels, over and under, with separate connecting roads that let vehicles cross, enter or leave either road without interfering with others, and the three most common types are cloverleaf, diamond and trumpet.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: Which compass directions correspond to even-numbered and odd-numbered interstate highways?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: An even interstate number means an east-west route while an odd number means a north-south route.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: In a three-digit interstate number, what does the first digit tell you about the route?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: A three-digit interstate number starting with an even digit is a beltway or bypass around a city, while one starting with an odd digit is a spur route.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.front: How does an overhead sign warn of a removed through lane compared with an added lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.expected_back: A removed through lane is announced by a black and yellow panel beneath the green and white overhead guide sign, whereas an added lane is usually obvious without one.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.front: What are the three common highway interchange layouts, and how do interchanges connect crossing roads?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.expected_back: Cloverleaf, diamond and trumpet are the three common interchange types, and every interchange joins two highways at different levels with connecting roads.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: Which two groups of people may legally use designated mobility impaired parking spaces in West Virginia?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: West Virginia law reserves designated parking spaces for mobility impaired citizens whose condition limits their ability to walk reasonable distances, and people who routinely transport mobility impaired persons may also use those spaces.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: What certification is needed for a mobility impaired placard or plate, and what transfer fee applies to the plate?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: To obtain a mobility impaired parking placard or license plate a doctor must certify the condition on a form the DMV provides, the DMV issues the placard or plate after approving the application, and the mobility impaired license plate carries a transfer fee of ten dollars and fifty cents.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: What must a vehicle display to park legally in a designated mobility impaired area?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: It is illegal to park a vehicle in a designated mobility impaired area unless it displays a mobility impaired parking placard or license plate.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: What should a license applicant include if a physical disability or medical issue might affect driving?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: About one in every ten people has some disability, no single set of rules can judge every person's ability to drive safely, and an applicant with a physical disability or medical problem that may interfere with driving should prepare a letter explaining the situation to accompany the license application.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: Which two West Virginia sources can give a driver a list of adaptive aid manufacturers like hand controls?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: A driver who needs adaptive aids such as hand controls can get a list of manufacturers from the driver's license examiner or from the Driver Education Department of the West Virginia Division of Rehabilitation Services.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: What four protections and services does the DMV provide under the Americans with Disabilities Act?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.memory_hook: Aids, policy flex, service animals welcome
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: Under the Americans with Disabilities Act the DMV does not discriminate on the basis of disability, generally provides aids and services for effective communication on request, makes reasonable modifications to its policies, and welcomes service animals in its offices even where pets are prohibited.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: How far in advance should you contact the DMV if you need an auxiliary aid or procedure modification?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: Anyone who needs an auxiliary aid or a modification of DMV procedures should contact the DMV no later than forty-eight hours before the scheduled arrival.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: What changes is the DMV not forced to make under the ADA, and may it charge extra for accommodations?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: The Americans with Disabilities Act does not require the DMV to fundamentally alter its programs or take on an undue financial or administrative burden, and the DMV will not place a surcharge on a person or group with disabilities to cover the cost of aids, services or modifications.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: Who handles DMV accessibility questions, and what is one example of a reasonable office modification?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: Questions or concerns about accessibility go to the DMV's ADA coordinator, and reasonable modifications include retrieving items from public locations that are not accessible to people who use wheelchairs.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.front: What medical step and plate transfer fee apply to mobility impaired parking, and when is parking there illegal?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.expected_back: A mobility impaired placard or plate requires a doctor's certification on the DMV form and the plate carries a ten dollar and fifty cent transfer fee, and parking in a designated space without displaying one is illegal.
