sec13-card-sec13-R10.front: What is the deadline for requesting a DMV accommodation, and how much can the DMV charge you for it?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.expected_back: An accommodation request to the DMV must arrive at least forty-eight hours before the visit, and the DMV may not charge the person with a disability for the aid or modification.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: What does West Virginia law require you to switch on during rain or reduced visibility?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: Turning on your headlights during rain or reduced visibility is required by law and increases your visibility to others.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: When is wet pavement slickest, and why does that happen?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: Wet pavement is most dangerous at the start of a light rain, when oil, dirt and water form a slippery film that weakens road contact on curves and lengthens stopping distance, so reduce your speed.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: What happens to tire grip on wet pavement up to thirty-five miles per hour, at thirty-five, and at fifty-five?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: On wet pavement tires wipe the road like a windshield wiper at speeds up to thirty-five miles per hour, a standard passenger vehicle begins to hydroplane partially at about thirty-five miles per hour, and at fifty-five miles per hour the tires ride entirely on the water film, leaving no friction to brake, accelerate or corner.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: In a severe rainstorm at fifty-five miles per hour, what small forces can trigger an uncontrollable skid?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: In a severe rainstorm tires lose all contact with the road at fifty-five miles per hour, and a gust of wind, a curve or a slight turn can then create an uncontrollable skid.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: Which driving and tire maintenance habits cut your risk of hydroplaning?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.memory_hook: Slow down, inflate, replace worn treads
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: To reduce hydroplaning slow down in rainstorms, on slushy roads and in standing water, keep tires properly inflated and replace them when the tread wear indicators show, because deep treads let water escape and can prevent complete hydroplaning at normal highway speeds.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: How little water can float smaller cars, and what depth sweeps most vehicles away?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.memory_hook: Six inches floats, two feet sweeps
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: Never drive across a flooded roadway, because as little as six inches of water can float some smaller vehicles and two feet of water will carry most vehicles away, after which the vehicle may roll and fill with water, trapping everyone inside.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: Roughly what share of American flash flood deaths happen in vehicles, and what hidden road hazard traps drivers?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: Motorists trapped in their vehicles account for nearly half of all flash flood deaths in the United States, victims often drive straight off the edge of an eroded road without knowing it is gone, and flooding is especially hard to recognize at night.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.front: What must you do immediately when your engine stalls in floodwater across a road?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.expected_back: If your vehicle stalls on a flooded roadway leave it immediately and seek higher ground, because it is better to be wet than dead.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: At what speed does partial hydroplaning start, and when do tires ride completely on water?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: Partial hydroplaning begins at about thirty-five miles per hour, while at fifty-five miles per hour the tires ride entirely on the water and lose all contact in a severe rainstorm.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: Compare the water depth that floats small cars with the depth that carries most vehicles away?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.memory_hook: Six inches floats, two feet carries
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: Six inches of water can float some smaller vehicles, whereas two feet of water will carry most vehicles away.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.front: How much longer can stopping take on snow or ice, and which road structures freeze first?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.memory_hook: Twelve times longer, bridges ice first
sec14-card-sec14-F27.expected_back: Keep snow tires or chains ready in winter but remember that neither allows safe driving on snow or ice at normal speeds, so slow down and keep a safe distance, since stopping on snow or ice can take up to twelve times the normal distance and bridges and overpasses may be icy when all other pavement is clear.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.front: What must be true of your windows, wipers, and defroster before you start driving in winter?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.expected_back: Keep every window clear of ice and snow, keep the windshield wipers and defroster in good working order, and never start driving until all windows are clear and completely defrosted.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.front: How does braking on ice or packed snow differ between anti-lock brakes and regular non-ABS brakes?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.memory_hook: Smooth ABS press, pump regular brakes
sec14-card-sec14-F29.expected_back: When stopping or slowing on ice or packed snow apply the brakes gently and smoothly, a vehicle with anti-lock brakes keeps its steering while braking, but in a vehicle without them you cannot steer unless you pump the brakes by applying and releasing them several times, and you release the brakes at the first hint that the wheels are slipping.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.front: How should you pull away from a stop on snow or ice, and how do you gauge road grip once moving?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.memory_hook: Ease throttle gently, test brakes slow
sec14-card-sec14-F30.expected_back: When starting on snow or ice keep engine speed low, accelerate slowly and smoothly, let out a manual clutch slowly and shift smoothly, and once moving test the brakes at low speed to learn how slippery the road is and adjust your speed to it.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.front: What roadway obstacles and vehicle control dangers come with strong winds and crosswinds?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.expected_back: Strong winds can down power lines and trees and blow debris into your path, and crosswinds can be strong enough to force your vehicle into the oncoming lane or off the roadway.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.front: Which beams and wipers belong on in fog or smoke, and what lights stay on if you must pull off and stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.memory_hook: Low beams, wipers, pull off flashing
sec14-card-sec14-F32.expected_back: Fog is extremely hazardous and smoke from factories, forest fires or burning leaves acts the same way, so in fog or dense smoke reduce speed, be ready for an emergency stop, use low-beam headlights and the wipers, and if your vision is impaired pull off the road, stop, leave the lights on and turn on the hazard lights.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: What is the worst-case stopping multiplier on snow or ice, and where can ice hide when roads look bare?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: Stopping on snow or ice can take up to twelve times the dry-pavement distance, and bridges and overpasses freeze while other pavement stays clear.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: Contrast how you keep steering control while braking on ice with anti-lock brakes versus without them?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.memory_hook: Gentle ABS, pump non-ABS, ease slip
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: With anti-lock brakes you brake gently and keep steering, but without them you must pump the brakes to steer and release them the moment the wheels start to slip.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.front: What settings do you use while driving through fog, and what do you switch on after pulling off the road?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.memory_hook: Low beams moving, flashers parked off-road
sec14-card-sec14-R11.expected_back: In fog or dense smoke you drive on low beams with the wipers running, and if vision is impaired you pull off and stop with both the lights and the hazard flashers on.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: How should you counter intense natural glare at sunrise, sunset, or off bright snow and chrome?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: Too much natural light, such as driving east at sunrise or west at sunset, calls for the sun visor, sunglasses, reduced speed and extra alertness, and sunglasses also help on bright summer or winter days against glare from other vehicles' glass and chrome or from snow.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: When should you turn on full headlights rather than parking lights?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.memory_hook: Full headlights at dusk or gloom
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: At night and on overcast or rainy days turn on your headlights, not just your parking lights, as soon as it begins to get dark or whenever fog, smoke or extreme cloudiness impairs visibility, because lighting up a little early helps other drivers see you, and keep the lighting system clean and in repair.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: What does the phrase over driving your headlights mean?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: Over driving your headlights means driving too fast to stop safely within the distance your headlights clearly light.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: Where should you look when meeting bright headlights at night, and at what two distances must you dim high beams?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: Looking directly into oncoming headlights causes momentary blindness, so when meeting a vehicle at night slow down, keep to the right of your lane and look well ahead at the right edge of the road, dimming your beams within five hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle and within two hundred feet of a vehicle you are following.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: How far away must you dim high beams for an oncoming vehicle compared with a vehicle ahead of you?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, two hundred behind
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: Headlight beams are dimmed within five hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle but within two hundred feet of a vehicle you are following.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: How does the hazard of over driving your headlights contrast with sunrise and sunset glare?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.memory_hook: Too little reach versus blinding glare
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: Over driving your headlights is a too-little-light problem of speed exceeding the lit distance, while sunrise and sunset glare is a too-much-light problem answered with the visor, sunglasses and lower speed.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: If your vehicle breaks down on an interstate, what three steps protect you and your passengers?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.memory_hook: Pull far off, flashers, everyone out
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: Be especially alert for stopped vehicles on an interstate, and if your own vehicle becomes disabled move as far off the road as possible, turn on the four-way flashers to show that you are stopped, and get everyone out of the vehicle and well away from the road.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: Where should you place two warning flares behind a disabled vehicle on an interstate?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.memory_hook: One car length, three hundred feet
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: Place one flare about one vehicle length behind a disabled vehicle and another about three hundred feet back, each on the shoulder near the edge of the through lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: What route choice may be wiser when fog on an interstate turns very dense?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: Fog in patches or as a haze reduces visibility, and when the fog is very dense it may be better to leave the interstate and finish the trip on slower roads.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: After a collision in heavy fog, why must you pull clear of the roadway immediately?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: After a crash in heavy fog get your vehicle as far off the road as possible, because leaving it on the road until the police arrive invites further crashes.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: How must you turn around on an interstate, and who is allowed to use median crossovers?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: Never make a U-turn on an interstate but go to the next exit to turn around, because the gravel or paved crossovers in highway medians are only for police and emergency vehicles.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: What controls must you obey in an interstate work zone, and when should you merge for a closed lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: Construction and maintenance zones on interstates and expressways frequently close one or more lanes and slow or stop traffic, so obey the special speed limits, traffic control signs and flaggers, and when lane-closure signs appear well in advance move to the open lane as soon as possible rather than at the last minute.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: What physical changes inside a construction zone make cautious, courteous speed essential?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.memory_hook: Shifted lanes, rough pavement, close crews
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: In a construction zone the route is often different, the road rougher, and large equipment and busy workers are close to your vehicle, so those workers count on you to drive cautiously and courteously and to follow the signs and flaggers that set the right speed for the conditions.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: What are the exact two positions for warning flares behind a disabled interstate vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.memory_hook: One length back, three hundred feet
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: The first flare goes about one vehicle length behind the disabled vehicle and the second about three hundred feet back, both on the shoulder beside the through lane.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: Why must an interstate driver continue to the next exit to turn around instead of using a median crossover?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: Turning around on an interstate means driving to the next exit, because a U-turn is never allowed there and the median crossovers belong to police and emergency vehicles.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: What is defensive driving built on, and when should those habits start and apply?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: Defensive driving means being prepared through the practice of good driving habits, which are as easy to form as bad ones and should begin the moment you step into the vehicle and be used on every trip, short or long.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: Which five personal traits produce bad driving habits that a safe driver must recognize and fix?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: Bad driving habits come from laziness, impatience, inattention, arrogance and aggressiveness, and a driver who shows any of them must evaluate and adjust that behavior to drive safely.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: What mirror, head-check, and turn-signal shortcuts mark a lazy driver?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: A lazy driver looks only in the rear view mirror instead of turning the head to look behind before changing lanes, pulling away from the curb or getting out on the traffic side, and failing to signal before turning, changing lanes or leaving the curb is a related bad habit that can cause a serious crash.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: What stop rule applies even on right turns, and what three traffic habits show an impatient driver?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: Regardless of traffic you must come to a complete stop at a stop sign or red light even when turning right, and an impatient driver who speeds from stop to stop, weaves through traffic and tailgates disrupts traffic and raises the chance of a crash without realizing it.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: How does an attentive driver sit and hold the wheel compared with an inattentive driver?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: A good driver sits up straight with a firm grip on the wheel, knows where the vehicle is and watches developing traffic problems, because a driver who leans back, loosens the grip and lets attention wander lets the vehicle wander too, and driving with an arm out the window, chatting, gesturing or ignoring the traffic flow marks an inattentive driver.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: How does an arrogant or aggressive driver differ from someone who is merely impatient, and how should you react?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: While the impatient driver is simply in a hurry, the arrogant or aggressive driver is purposely in a hurry, treats the vehicle as an extension of the ego, shows little respect for traffic laws or the rights of others, and should neither be imitated nor competed with.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: Why must you avoid daydreaming, window shopping, scenic staring, or distracting talk at the wheel?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: Concentration is one of the most important elements of safe driving, so the driver's seat is no place for daydreaming, mental napping, window shopping, scenic viewing or distracting conversation, because driving an automobile is a full-time job.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: Do empty cross streets or cars behind you ever excuse skipping a complete stop when turning right?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: Pressure from vehicles behind and an empty cross street tempt the impatient driver merely to slow for a stop sign, yet a complete stop is required at every stop sign or red light even for a right turn.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.front: What separates an impatient driver from an arrogant or aggressive driver?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.expected_back: The impatient driver is simply in a hurry, whereas the arrogant or aggressive driver is purposely in a hurry and treats the vehicle as an extension of the ego.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.front: Which construction and surface features make up the road conditions a defensive driver watches for?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.expected_back: Road conditions to consider are mainly matters of construction such as curves, hills, pavement width, multiple lanes, road surfaces, poorly marked or unmarked roads, shoulders and drop-offs.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.front: How often must a West Virginia vehicle pass official safety inspection, and what rule governs its windshield sticker?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.memory_hook: Inspect every two years, keep sticker
sec14-card-sec14-F34.expected_back: You cannot safely drive ten feet or ten miles in an unsafe vehicle, so West Virginia requires every vehicle to be inspected every two years at a station displaying the official state inspection sign, and the windshield sticker showing the month and year of the next inspection must never be removed.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.front: What schedule and sticker rule apply to West Virginia's vehicle safety inspection?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.expected_back: A state inspection is due every two years and its windshield sticker shows the month and year of the next one, and removing that sticker is against the law.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.front: What exact steering, gas, and brake steps keep a vehicle controlled during a tire blowout?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.memory_hook: Grip tight, ease gas, delay braking
sec16-card-sec16-F07.expected_back: A blowout is the sudden collapse of a tire that can throw the vehicle out of control, so hold the steering wheel tightly, steer straight ahead, ease up on the accelerator, do not brake until the vehicle is under control, and then pull all the way off the road into a safe area.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.front: What should you do if no safe pull-off exists right after a blowout, and what tire neglect causes most blowouts?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.memory_hook: Creep with flashers, prevent low pressure
sec16-card-sec16-F08.expected_back: If you cannot get off the road immediately after a blowout, keep driving slowly with the emergency flashers on, and remember that under-inflated tires are one of the most common causes of blowouts.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.front: What four actions help slow and stop your vehicle if the regular brakes fail?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.expected_back: If your brakes fail, pump the brake pedal quickly, shift to a lower gear while looking for a place to slow down and stop off the roadway, use the horn and lights to warn other drivers, and use the parking brake while holding its release so you can ease off if the rear wheels lock and skid.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.front: When your vehicle starts to skid, what is the rule on braking and where should your focus stay?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.expected_back: If the vehicle begins to skid stay calm, do not use the brakes unless you are in danger of hitting something, and concentrate on steering out of trouble.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.front: Which way do you turn the steering wheel to recover from a rear-wheel skid, and how do you stop a counter-skid?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.memory_hook: Ease gas, steer toward rear slide
sec16-card-sec16-F12.expected_back: To steer out of a skid take your foot off the gas and turn the wheel in the direction of the skid, turning right if the rear is sliding right and left if it slides left, then if the vehicle starts to skid the other way turn again toward where you want to go and straighten the wheels to regain control.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.front: If the gas pedal sticks down and will not pop free with your foot, how do you stop the car safely?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.memory_hook: Shift neutral, brake, shut off parked
sec16-card-sec16-F13.expected_back: If the gas pedal sticks, concentrate on steering with your eyes on the road, try to free the pedal with your foot, and if that fails push in the clutch or shift into neutral, use the brakes, stop at the nearest safe place and turn off the ignition.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.front: How do you safely bring your tires back onto the road after running off onto a low shoulder?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.expected_back: If your wheels run off the road, grip the wheel tightly, stay on the shoulder, ease off the accelerator, brake gently and slow gradually, then after slowing check behind and ahead for traffic, turn the wheels sharply onto the pavement, and the moment the wheels hit the pavement edge turn them the other way so the vehicle does not shoot across the highway.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.front: After losing steering control, when should you brake gently versus braking hard with maximum pressure?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.expected_back: If you suddenly lose steering control ease up on the accelerator, and if the vehicle stays in its lane wait until it slows and then brake gently to avoid changing direction, but if it heads off the road or toward a pedestrian or another vehicle brake quickly with maximum pressure.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.front: How does your response to failed headlights change on a lighted highway, a dark highway, or when every light dies?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.memory_hook: Pull off lit, try backup lights
sec16-card-sec16-F16.expected_back: If your headlights fail on a lighted highway get onto the shoulder or other available space as soon as safely possible, on a dark highway try the parking lights, direction signals or emergency flashers and get off the roadway, and if all lights fail stay on the roadway and slow enough to pull off safely.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.front: If smoke pours from under the hood, how should you fight a small fire, why skip water, and how far back do you retreat?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.memory_hook: Smother with dirt, retreat hundred feet
sec16-card-sec16-F17.expected_back: If smoke comes from under the hood get off the roadway and turn off the ignition, smother the fire with dirt or sand when no chemical extinguisher is available, never use water because burning gasoline floats on it and spreads, and if the fire gets out of control move at least one hundred feet away because the gas tank may explode.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.front: What should you do if an oncoming vehicle enters your lane, and why must you never swerve left into its lane?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.memory_hook: Move right, honk, flash, never left
sec16-card-sec16-F18.expected_back: If a vehicle comes toward you in your lane, move to the right, slow down, then sound your horn and flash your headlights, and do not turn into the lane the other vehicle left because its driver may realize the mistake and swing back.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.front: What must you do if stalled on railroad tracks with a train coming, or if the oil pressure light illuminates?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.memory_hook: Abandon tracks, kill engine for oil
sec16-card-sec16-F19.expected_back: If your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks look both ways for trains, and if a train is coming get out of the vehicle and go to a safe location, while if the oil pressure light comes on get off the road, turn off the engine immediately, check the oil level and add oil if needed.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.front: Contrast your brake and gear actions during a skid with those for a stuck accelerator?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.memory_hook: Skids steer unbraked, stuck gas neutral
sec16-card-sec16-R01.expected_back: In a skid you steer in the direction the rear is sliding and stay off the brakes unless a collision looms, whereas with a stuck gas pedal you shift to neutral or push in the clutch, brake and shut off the ignition.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.front: What three mechanical steps slow a vehicle when the service brakes fail?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.memory_hook: Pump fast, downshift, modulate parking brake
sec16-card-sec16-R02.expected_back: In a brake failure you pump the pedal quickly, drop to a lower gear and apply the parking brake while holding its release so a rear-wheel lock can be eased off.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.front: What household material smothers an engine fire instead of water, and what is the minimum retreat distance?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.expected_back: An engine fire is smothered with dirt or sand, never water, and once it is out of control you retreat at least one hundred feet because the tank may explode.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.front: Faced with an oncoming driver in your lane, which four moves are right and which lane choice is forbidden?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.memory_hook: Escape right, warn loudly, avoid left
sec16-card-sec16-R04.expected_back: Faced with a vehicle in your lane you move right, slow, sound the horn and flash the lights, but you never swing into the lane the other driver left.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.front: When do failed headlights require staying briefly in the lane while slowing instead of pulling off immediately?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.memory_hook: Stay and slow when totally dark
sec16-card-sec16-R05.expected_back: When headlights fail you leave the road at once if it is lighted, try the parking lights, signals or flashers if it is dark, and stay on the roadway only when every light has failed, slowing enough to pull off safely.

sec16-card-sec16-R13.front: What decides whether you brake gently or slam maximum brake pressure after steering fails?
sec16-card-sec16-R13.expected_back: When steering fails you ease off the gas and brake gently if the vehicle holds its lane, but brake hard if it heads off the road or toward people or another vehicle.

sec16-card-sec16-F24.front: Roughly how many people are hurt in crashes yearly, and when is the only time you should move an injured victim?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.memory_hook: Two million hurt, never move needlessly
sec16-card-sec16-F24.expected_back: About two million people are injured in traffic crashes each year and many of those injuries end in death because proper first aid was not given, so stay calm, do not move the victim unless there is danger of further injury, and try to judge how seriously the victim is hurt.

sec16-card-sec16-F25.front: In what exact four-step priority order should emergency first aid be given at a crash scene?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.expected_back: First aid is given in the order control bleeding, restore breathing, treat for shock, then protect broken bones, keeping the victim lying down and comfortable, and you give it when a delay in emergency care could mean death or further injury.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.front: Who does West Virginia's Good Samaritan law protect from civil damages at a crash scene, and on what two conditions?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.memory_hook: Good-faith unpaid helpers face zero liability
sec16-card-sec16-F26.expected_back: Under the Good Samaritan law no one, including a licensed physician or dentist, who in good faith gives emergency care at a crash scene without pay is liable for civil damages from any act or omission in giving that care.

sec16-card-sec16-F27.front: What immediate safety, warning, aid, and emergency-call steps must you take if involved in a crash?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.memory_hook: Stop, cut ignition, warn, render aid
sec16-card-sec16-F27.expected_back: If you are involved in a crash stop immediately, turn off the ignition to prevent fire, protect the scene with flares, a flagman or other means, render aid without moving the injured unless absolutely necessary, send for an ambulance or law enforcement, and keep spectators away from the injured.

sec16-card-sec16-F28.front: Which crashes must be reported to law enforcement, and what four details should involved drivers exchange?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.expected_back: A crash that injures or kills anyone or causes property damage of one thousand dollars or more must be reported to the nearest law enforcement agency, and the people involved should exchange names, addresses, license plate numbers and motor vehicle insurance information.

sec16-card-sec16-F29.front: When should a passing driver stop at a crash, and what must you do if you strike an unattended vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.memory_hook: Keep moving uninvolved, leave full note
sec16-card-sec16-F29.expected_back: Do not stop at a crash scene unless you are involved or can render assistance, because unnecessary stopping creates additional hazards, and if you strike an unattended vehicle try to find the owner or leave a written notice with your name, address, license plate number, insurance information and the circumstances.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.front: Name the four crash first-aid priorities in order and the default body position for the victim?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.memory_hook: Bleed, breathe, shock, bones, lying down
sec16-card-sec16-R07.expected_back: First aid runs bleeding first, breathing second, shock third and broken bones fourth, and the victim stays lying down unless danger requires a move.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.front: What triggers a mandatory crash report to police, and what rule applies to uninvolved passersby?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.expected_back: A crash with injury, death or property damage of one thousand dollars or more must be reported to law enforcement, yet a passerby should not stop at a crash at all unless involved or able to help.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.front: When testing your brake pedal, what do a firm halfway stop, a spongy feel, and a ten-second sinking pedal mean?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.memory_hook: Halfway firm, spongy air, sinking leak
sec16-card-sec16-F01.expected_back: When checking the brakes the pedal should go no more than halfway to the floor and should feel as if it is hitting something hard, a spongy pedal may mean air bubbles in the brake line, and if the pedal keeps sinking while you push and count to ten the braking system may have a leak.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.front: How can you check whether your parking brake needs adjustment?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.memory_hook: Set firmly, test gentle gear pull
sec16-card-sec16-F02.expected_back: Check the parking brake by setting it firmly, and if the vehicle still moves easily in drive or first gear the parking brake needs adjustment.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.front: Which fluid puddles and under-hood components should you check regularly, and what safety rule applies around the radiator and battery?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.expected_back: Check under the vehicle frequently for oil, coolant, brake fluid or transmission leaks, check under the hood the battery, engine oil, radiator only when it is cool, power steering, brake master cylinder, belts and hoses, and never smoke or use a flame while doing so.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.front: How often, at what tire temperature, and against what reference number should you check tire pressure?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.expected_back: Tire crashes are preventable, since under-inflated or over-inflated tires and low tread cause safety problems, so check tire pressure monthly with a gauge while the tires are cold against the pressure number on the sticker inside the door jamb, letting air out if the reading is too high and inflating if it is too low.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.front: How do you place a penny into tire tread, and what visual sign tells you the tire must be replaced?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.memory_hook: Head first, full head means replace
sec16-card-sec16-F05.expected_back: To check tread depth hold a penny by Lincoln's body and place his head first into the deepest-looking groove, and if you can see all of his head the tires are too worn to drive on and must be replaced.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.front: How often should you inspect exterior lights and wiper blades, and what two related checks go with them?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.memory_hook: Lights monthly, wipers yearly, full washer
sec16-card-sec16-F06.expected_back: Check all exterior lights once a month, check the wiper blades at least once a year while keeping the washer fluid container full, and make sure every interior warning light works properly.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.front: How can you help cool an engine in slow traffic, and what must you do if the temperature warning triggers?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.memory_hook: Neutral rev stopped, never open hot
sec16-card-sec16-F10.expected_back: In slow traffic you can prevent overheating by shifting into neutral and racing the engine briefly during stops to speed up the fan and water pump, and if the warning light or gauge shows overheating pull off the road, turn off the engine and leave the radiator cap alone until the engine has cooled.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.front: Match a firm half-travel brake pedal, a spongy pedal, and a sinking ten-count pedal to what each tells you?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.memory_hook: Firm healthy, spongy air, sinking leak
sec16-card-sec16-R10.expected_back: A healthy brake pedal stops firmly within half its travel, a spongy pedal suggests air in the line, and a pedal that keeps sinking through a ten count suggests a leak.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.front: Pair the immediate response to a blowout with the monthly maintenance habit that prevents most of them?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.memory_hook: Steer straight unbraked, check cold monthly
sec16-card-sec16-R11.expected_back: After a blowout you steer straight and ease off the gas without braking until control returns, and because under-inflation causes most blowouts tire pressure is checked monthly while the tires are cold.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.front: After prepping battery vents and turning accessories off, where do the positive and negative jumper cable clamps attach?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.memory_hook: Positive to positive, negative to block
sec16-card-sec16-F20.expected_back: To jump start a dead battery remove the vent caps from both batteries and cover the open vent wells with a cloth, turn off the lights, heater, air conditioner and radio, connect the positive post of the dead battery to the positive post of the live battery, and connect the negative post of the live battery to the engine block or frame of the vehicle with the dead battery.

sec16-card-sec16-F21.front: How should the cars be positioned, started, and disconnected during a jump-start, and how do you treat spilled acid?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.memory_hook: Cars apart, disconnect reverse, rinse acid
sec16-card-sec16-F21.expected_back: Make sure the two vehicles are not touching, start the vehicle giving the jump and let it run a few minutes before starting the other, remove the jumper cables in the opposite order and replace the vent caps, and wash any battery acid off skin, eyes or vehicles immediately with water.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.front: What survival, signaling, repair, and fire items belong inside a basic automobile emergency kit?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.memory_hook: Flares, cables, spare, chemical extinguisher, water
sec16-card-sec16-F22.expected_back: A basic automobile emergency kit holds a battery-powered radio and flashlight with extra batteries, a cell phone charger, jumper cables, signal flares, blankets, critical prescription medications, a basic tool kit, a chemical fire extinguisher, a properly inflated spare tire and jack, quick energy snacks, maps of the area, a compass, a multi-tool and bottled water.

sec16-card-sec16-F23.front: Which wound-care, protective, and basic medication items belong in a vehicle first-aid kit?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.expected_back: A basic first aid kit holds safety pins, triangular bandages, sterile gauze pads, self-adhesive bandages, scissors, tweezers, hand sanitizer, common pain relievers, antacids, latex gloves, sunscreen, petroleum jelly, mild soap, peroxide and moistened towelettes.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.front: Why must the live battery's negative cable clamp to the dead car's engine block or frame instead of its negative post?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.memory_hook: Clamp engine block, cars never touch
sec16-card-sec16-R06.expected_back: Jumper cables join positive post to positive post, but the live battery's negative goes to the dead vehicle's engine block or frame rather than to the dead battery's negative post, and the two vehicles must not touch.

sec16-card-sec16-F30.front: Who operates the West Virginia Courtesy Patrol, and what roadside help does it provide?
sec16-card-sec16-F30.memory_hook: Highways team clears hazards, helps stranded
sec16-card-sec16-F30.expected_back: The West Virginia Courtesy Patrol, run through the Division of Highways, employs and trains former welfare recipients as operators and dispatchers, assists stranded motorists, removes roadway hazards to reduce secondary crashes, provides gas or directions, changes flat tires, and works alongside the State Police, nine one one centers and other emergency personnel.

sec16-card-sec16-F31.front: What three personal safety steps should you follow when waiting on the roadside for assistance?
sec16-card-sec16-F31.memory_hook: Pull far off, lock doors, watch
sec16-card-sec16-F31.expected_back: If you need roadside assistance pull off the highway as far as possible, keep your doors locked and watch who pulls up behind you, and store the Courtesy Patrol number on your cell phone for emergencies.

sec16-card-sec16-F32.front: What truck markings, light bar, uniform, badge, and approach side identify a genuine Courtesy Patrol operator?
sec16-card-sec16-F32.expected_back: Courtesy Patrol drivers use white pickup trucks with blue and gold reflective logos and a flashing orange bar light, carry identification badges, wear a reflective orange or green vest over a blue and gold trimmed uniform, and approach your vehicle on the passenger side whenever possible.

sec16-card-sec16-F33.front: What fine range, jail term, cleanup hours, and license consequence can result from a littering conviction?
sec16-card-sec16-F33.memory_hook: Up to thousand, jail, cleanup, points
sec16-card-sec16-F33.expected_back: Littering any public or private roadway or property violates West Virginia law, and a conviction brings a fine of fifty to one thousand dollars, up to sixty days in the county jail or at least thirty hours of removing litter, and points may be assessed against the driving record.

sec16-card-sec16-F34.front: Which four vehicle wastes threaten the environment most, and how much water can a single oil change ruin?
sec16-card-sec16-F34.expected_back: Dirty motor oil, old tires, antifreeze and batteries are the vehicle wastes that most threaten the environment, because the roughly one gallon of oil from a single oil change can ruin a million gallons of water, stockpiled tires collect water, attract mosquitoes and tempt arsonists, antifreeze is a listed hazardous waste and old batteries hold large amounts of lead and sulfuric acid.

sec16-card-sec16-F35.front: Where can you properly recycle used motor oil, old tires, antifreeze, and vehicle batteries?
sec16-card-sec16-F35.memory_hook: Retailers and shops recycle all four
sec16-card-sec16-F35.expected_back: All of those vehicle wastes can be recycled, since many auto part retailers and service stations take used oil free, tire retailers dispose of old tires properly, some repair shops recycle antifreeze for a small fee, and battery retailers must by law recycle old batteries on request.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.front: Recap the fine range, jail cap, minimum cleanup hours, and license impact of West Virginia littering?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.memory_hook: Fifty to thousand, sixty days, thirty
sec16-card-sec16-R09.expected_back: A littering conviction can cost fifty to one thousand dollars, up to sixty days in jail or at least thirty hours of litter removal, with points possible as well.

sec16-card-sec16-R12.front: What visual truck clues and driver habit confirm a Courtesy Patrol stop is legitimate?
sec16-card-sec16-R12.memory_hook: Blue-gold white truck, badge, passenger side
sec16-card-sec16-R12.expected_back: A genuine Courtesy Patrol vehicle is a white pickup with blue and gold logos and a flashing orange bar light, and its badged driver approaches on the passenger side.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: What convictions and details does the point system record, and what can repeated moving violations trigger?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: The DMV point system identifies and controls problem drivers by recording every traffic conviction with its date, nature and court, assigning points to in-state and out-of-state moving violations by seriousness, and repeated convictions can build a record that leads to suspension.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: How long do assessed points remain active on your West Virginia driving record?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: Points remain on your driving record for two years from the conviction date.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: What action happens when your record reaches six points versus twelve points?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: At six or more points the DMV sends a letter of caution urging careful and lawful driving, and at twelve points your driver's license is subject to suspension.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: How many points can an approved eight-hour defensive driving class remove, how often, and what timing trap blocks credit?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.memory_hook: Minus three yearly after points post
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: Completing an approved eight-hour defensive driving class removes three points, but only once every twelve months, only for courses the DMV approves, and not if the class is taken without approval or before the points appear on the record.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.front: How many points does fleeing from a law-enforcement officer add to your record?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.expected_back: Fleeing from an officer carries eight points, the highest value on the point scale.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.front: Which four serious violations each carry six points on the West Virginia scale?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.expected_back: Six points are assessed for speeding in a school zone, reckless driving, hit and run meaning leaving the scene or failing to reveal identity, and speeding twenty miles per hour or more over the limit.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.front: How many points attach to speeding fifteen to nineteen miles per hour over versus eleven to fourteen over?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.expected_back: Speeding fifteen to nineteen miles per hour over the limit carries five points, while speeding eleven to fourteen miles per hour over carries three points.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.front: How many points apply to repeat wireless offenses, bad passes, yield or signal failures, left-of-center driving, and lost control?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.expected_back: Three points are assessed for three or more wireless communication device violations, a passing violation, failure to yield, failure to obey a traffic light or a stop sign, hazardous driving, driving left of center, driving too fast for conditions and failure to maintain control of the vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-F38.front: How many points apply to careless driving, wrong-way streets, littering, lane or safety-zone violations, and disobeying police?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.expected_back: Three points also apply to careless or hazardous driving, driving the wrong way on a one-way street, littering, an improper lane violation, failure to observe a safety zone, failure to follow a police officer's instructions and driving on the wrong side of the road.

sec04-card-sec04-F39.front: Which everyday errors and unlisted moving violations carry two points on the scale?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.expected_back: Two points are assessed for following too closely, more than three passengers in the front seat, improper turning, improper backing, an improper signal or no signal, and every other moving violation not listed on the scale.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: How does the state's response at six points differ from reaching twelve points?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: Six points on the record bring only a letter of caution, whereas twelve points make the license subject to suspension.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: How often may you use the three-point defensive driving deduction compared with how long points stay on file?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.memory_hook: Class yearly, points last two years
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: The approved defensive driving class removes three points and may be used once every twelve months, while points themselves stay on the record for two years from conviction.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: How do the three speeding brackets step up from eleven miles per hour over past twenty over?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: The speeding point tiers climb from three points for eleven to fourteen miles per hour over, to five points for fifteen to nineteen over, to six points for twenty or more over the limit.

sec04-card-sec04-R13.front: Which violation sits alone at the eight-point top of the scale, and which sit at the two-point bottom?
sec04-card-sec04-R13.expected_back: Fleeing from an officer is the only eight-point offense on the scale, while following too closely and improper turning sit at the bottom with two points.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: What happens if your vehicle lacked required West Virginia liability coverage on the date of a crash?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: If your vehicle was not covered by the required West Virginia liability insurance on the date of a crash, your vehicle registration and your driving privilege will be suspended.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: What insurance coverage must every motorist carry when driving on West Virginia public roads?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Every motorist driving on West Virginia public roads is required by state law to carry West Virginia motor vehicle liability insurance meeting the minimum coverage set by law.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: How long must liability coverage stay active on a registered car, and what must you do if insurance cancels?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: When you obtain or renew a vehicle registration you must prove West Virginia liability insurance and keep it for the full registration year, and if the insurance is cancelled for any reason you must surrender the registration plate to the DMV.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: Does a digital insurance image on your phone count, and when must you show proof alongside registration?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: A certificate of insurance or other proof of West Virginia liability insurance must be carried in the vehicle at all times with a valid registration card, an image on a wireless communication device counts as valid proof, and you must present the proof to an investigating officer after a crash and at any vehicle inspection.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: How can West Virginia verify your insurance mid-year, and what happens if you fail to prove coverage?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: The DMV may verify insurance at any time during the registration year, including directly and electronically with insurance companies, and failing to provide proof of West Virginia liability insurance suspends both the driver's license and the vehicle registration with reinstatement or penalty fees.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: What follows a ticket or crash report showing no insurance, and how do you reinstate?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: A ticket or crash report showing no West Virginia liability insurance can suspend your license and registration plate, repeat offenses lengthen the license suspension, and reinstatement requires current proof of insurance plus mandatory reinstatement fees.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: What administrative and criminal penalties punish filing false or fraudulent insurance information?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.memory_hook: Ninety-day suspension, thousand fine, year jail
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: Filing false or fraudulent insurance information brings an additional ninety-day license suspension, revocation of the vehicle registration, and possible prosecution carrying a fine of not more than one thousand dollars and jail time of not more than one year.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: Which three loss categories make up West Virginia's mandatory minimum liability insurance structure?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: State law sets minimum liability coverage categories for one death or injury, for two deaths or injuries, and for property damage.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: When may an adult use an electronic communications device while driving, and how much does wireless use cut concentration?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.memory_hook: Hands-free only, focus drops a third
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: Using any electronic communications device while driving on a public street or highway is prohibited unless the use is accomplished with hands-free equipment, and the handbook notes that a driver's concentration drops twenty to thirty-three percent when using a wireless device.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: What makes equipment hands-free, and which gadgets beyond cell phones fall under the electronic-device law?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: A hands-free device has a feature that lets the user engage it without either or both hands, and electronic communications devices include cell phones, personal digital assistants, mobile data devices, laptops, pagers, broadband personal communication devices, two-way messaging devices, electronic games and portable computers.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: Which calling, viewing, gaming, or messaging actions on a non-hands-free device break West Virginia law?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.memory_hook: Any handheld call text browse game
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: Using a device that is not hands-free to make a call, view or transmit images or data, play games, or compose, send, read, view, access, browse, transmit, save or retrieve e-mail, text messages or other electronic data violates the law.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: What fines and license points apply to first, second, and third-or-later handheld-device offenses?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.memory_hook: One hundred, two hundred, three-hundred three-points
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: The electronic-device fines are one hundred dollars and zero points for a first offense, two hundred dollars and zero points for a second offense, and three hundred dollars and three points for a third or later offense.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: Which emergency reports and official responders are exempt from the electronic-device ban?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: Using an electronic communications device to report a fire, traffic crash, serious road hazard or emergency to the authorities is not a violation, and neither is use by a law-enforcement officer, firefighter, emergency medical technician, paramedic or authorized emergency vehicle operator performing official duties.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: On which offense number do driving-record points first attach to electronic-device violations?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: The first and second electronic-device offenses carry rising fines but zero points, and only the third and later offenses add three points to the record.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: What single distinction separates lawful adult electronic-device use from a violation while driving?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: Hands-free use of an electronic device is allowed while driving, but any call, image, game or message handled on a device that is not hands-free is a violation.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: Which homicide, graduated-driver, false-statement, or hit-and-run convictions force mandatory license revocation?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.memory_hook: Vehicular homicide, teen repeats, injury hit-and-run
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: The DMV must revoke a license upon final conviction of manslaughter or negligent homicide from operating a motor vehicle, two or more moving violations as a graduated driver, providing false information to the DMV, or leaving the scene of a crash that results in death or personal injury.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: Which reckless-driving streak, street-racing, suspended-driving, or civil-judgment failures force mandatory revocation?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.memory_hook: Three reckless, racing, suspended, unpaid judgment
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: Mandatory revocation also follows three reckless driving convictions within twenty-four months, racing on streets or highways, driving while suspended or revoked, and failing to satisfy a civil judgment arising from an automobile crash.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: Which impaired-driving, fuel-theft, or felony convictions trigger mandatory license revocation?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.memory_hook: Any-state impaired, second gas-skip, vehicle felony
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: Mandatory revocation further follows a conviction in any state for driving under the influence of alcohol, controlled substances or drugs, a second conviction for failing to pay for gasoline, and any felony committed using a motor vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: How do penalties compare between driving while suspended for non-alcohol reasons versus driving while revoked for impaired driving?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: Driving while your license is suspended or revoked for a non-DUI reason may cause a ninety-day suspension, while driving while revoked for DUI carries a mandatory minimum jail sentence of thirty days to six months and a further six-month revocation of the driving privilege.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: What suspension penalty hits someone who lies on an application, lends or borrows a license, shares identity papers, or shows a fake card?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: Giving false information on any license application is illegal, as is using someone else's license, letting another person use yours, letting someone use your identity documents to get a license, or displaying a fictitious license, and the penalty is a ninety-day suspension.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: What separates the penalty for driving on a general suspension from driving while revoked for impaired driving?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.memory_hook: Mandatory thirty-day-to-six-month jail plus six-month revoke
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Driving while suspended for a non-DUI reason may bring a ninety-day suspension, whereas driving while revoked for DUI brings mandatory jail of thirty days to six months plus a six-month revocation.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: How many reckless-driving convictions in twenty-four months or moving violations as a graduated driver trigger mandatory revocation?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.memory_hook: Three reckless in twenty-four, two graduated
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: Mandatory revocation triggers include three reckless driving convictions within twenty-four months and two or more moving violations as a graduated driver, so the count and the time window both matter.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: Which crashes must be reported, within how many days, and to which police agency inside versus outside city limits?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.memory_hook: Injury death thousand-damage within five days
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: A crash causing injury or death to any person or property damage over one thousand dollars must be reported by the quickest means, oral or written, within five days to the local police department if it happens inside a municipality, and otherwise to the county sheriff or the nearest State Police office.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: How does the Driver License Compact treat moving violations and revocations from other states?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: Under the Driver License Compact, traffic violations in other states become part of your West Virginia record with points assessed when warranted, an out-of-state conviction that is grounds for suspension or revocation can suspend or revoke your West Virginia license, and other states may restrict your privilege to drive there.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: What two-way deal does the Non-Resident Violator Compact create when you receive a ticket in another member state?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.memory_hook: Drive onward now, ignore suspends home
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: Under the Non-Resident Violator Compact a driver may accept a citation for certain violations and continue on, and each member state agrees to suspend its own citizens who fail to comply with the terms of a violation committed in another state.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: What happens to your driver's license if you fail to appear or comply with any municipal, magistrate, or circuit court order?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: Municipal, magistrate and circuit courts must notify the DMV when you fail to appear or fail to comply with any ticket, court order or decision, even a non-traffic matter, and the DMV suspends your license until you prove compliance and pay all penalty fees.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: What family-court financial failure requires West Virginia to suspend a driver's license?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: State law also requires the DMV to suspend your driver's license if you fail to maintain child support payment obligations, so tickets and citations should be handled promptly.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.front: Through which three channels are West Virginia suspension, revocation, and reinstatement transactions handled?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.expected_back: All suspension, revocation and reinstatement transactions are handled in person at the Division of Motor Vehicles in Charleston, by mail to its post office box, or online through the DMV self-service site.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.front: What can you check for free on the online services portal, and what does buying your driving record cost?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.expected_back: The DMV Online Services page lets you check your license status, your total points and your commercial medical certification date, view and buy a driving record for twelve dollars and fifty cents, and pay license reinstatement fees.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: What dollar threshold of property damage triggers mandatory five-day crash reporting when nobody is hurt?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.memory_hook: Over one thousand within five days
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: The crash-reporting duty is triggered by injury, death or property damage over one thousand dollars, and the report is due within five days to the local police inside a municipality or otherwise to the sheriff or State Police.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: How do the Driver License Compact and the Non-Resident Violator Compact split out-of-state enforcement?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.memory_hook: License posts convictions, Violator enforces unpaid
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: The Driver License Compact brings out-of-state convictions and points onto your record, while the Non-Resident Violator Compact lets you accept a citation and drive on but has your home state suspend you if you fail to comply.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.front: Which two obligations outside moving traffic stops still force West Virginia to suspend your license?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.memory_hook: Any court default or child support
sec04-card-sec04-R11.expected_back: Failing to appear or comply with any court ticket or order, even a non-traffic one, and failing to maintain child support both lead the DMV to suspend the license.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: Who bears responsibility for your actions behind the wheel and knowing how to keep your West Virginia driving privilege?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: The privilege to drive carries many responsibilities, you and only you are responsible for your actions, and a license holder must know the requirements that keep the privilege of driving in West Virginia.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: How does West Virginia restrict a minor's license after excessive unexcused school absences, and how are full privileges restored?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.memory_hook: Work medical school church until cleared
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: If your school notifies the DMV that you are not attending or have excessive unexcused absences, the DMV restricts your license to work, medical, educational and religious purposes until you turn eighteen or present a reinstatement authorization form from the school and pay the reinstatement fee.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: How can someone refer an immediate family member who can no longer drive safely, and who else may report?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: To refer an immediate family member who can no longer drive safely, write a detailed explanation to the DMV Medical Section giving the person's name, address, date of birth and license number if possible, and law enforcement or the person's physician may also submit such information.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: What evaluations and licensing actions can follow an unsafe-driver referral?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.memory_hook: Reexamine skills or doctor, restrict revoke
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: After an unsafe-driver referral the DMV may reexamine the person's driving skills or request updated medical information from the doctor, and may then issue a restricted license or revoke the driving privilege for everyone's safety.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: When can the Commissioner order medical, written, or road retesting, and what happens if you refuse?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: You may be required to take a medical, written or driving examination when the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles has good cause to believe you are incompetent or otherwise not qualified, the result may be suspension, revocation or a restricted license, and refusing the examination is itself grounds for suspension or revocation.

sec04-card-sec04-R12.front: How do family unsafe-driver referrals and refusing a required re-examination connect?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.expected_back: A referral about an unsafe family member can lead the DMV to reexamine that driver, and refusing a required re-examination is by itself grounds for suspension or revocation.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: What is West Virginia's legal drinking age, and what happens if a younger driver has measurable alcohol?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: The legal drinking age in West Virginia is twenty-one, and under the zero tolerance law a driver under twenty-one found with any measurable amount of alcohol in the system will lose the driver's license.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: How does West Virginia law treat concentrations above point zero five versus point zero eight or higher?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: In West Virginia a blood alcohol concentration above point zero five percent and below point zero eight percent is relevant evidence to presume that the driver's ability is impaired, a concentration of point zero eight percent or more creates a presumption of driving under the influence, and the license can be revoked even when the concentration is below point zero eight percent.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: What does the handbook's eleven-thirty-to-four-morning example prove about drinking faster than one drink hourly?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Drinking more than one drink per hour builds the blood alcohol level, and the handbook's example shows the level still rising after a last drink at eleven thirty at night and remaining above point zero six percent at four in the morning, enough for a DUI arrest.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: What fine, jail rule, and minimum license revocation apply to a first zero-tolerance violation?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: A first zero tolerance offense by a driver under twenty-one with any measurable alcohol carries a fine of twenty-five to one hundred dollars, no jail, and a minimum revocation of thirty days.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: What fine, jail time, and revocation length hit a driver on a second zero-tolerance offense?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: A second zero tolerance offense carries a fine of one hundred to five hundred dollars, twenty-four hours in jail, and a minimum revocation of sixty days or until the eighteenth birthday, whichever is greater.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: How do the legal meanings of above point zero five, point zero eight, and underage measurable alcohol compare?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: A blood alcohol concentration above point zero five percent and below point zero eight percent is only evidence of impairment, point zero eight percent or more is presumed DUI, and for a driver under twenty-one any measurable alcohol at all triggers zero tolerance.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: How do jail time and minimum revocation escalate from a first zero-tolerance offense to a second?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: A first zero tolerance offense brings a thirty-day minimum revocation and no jail, while a second brings twenty-four hours in jail and sixty days or until the eighteenth birthday, whichever is greater.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: What penalties apply to a first DUI below point one five or knowingly letting an impaired person drive?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: A first DUI with alcohol or drugs at a blood alcohol concentration below point one five, or knowingly permitting DUI, carries a fine of one hundred to five hundred dollars, jail of up to six months, and a minimum revocation of fifteen days.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: What fine, jail range, and minimum revocation apply when a first DUI reaches point one five or higher?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: A first DUI at a blood alcohol concentration of point one five or more carries a fine of two hundred to one thousand dollars, jail of two days to six months, and a minimum revocation of forty-five days.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: What penalties apply when a driver commits DUI with child endangerment?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: DUI with child endangerment carries a fine of two hundred to one thousand dollars, jail of forty-eight hours to twelve months, and a minimum revocation of sixty days.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: What fine, jail range, and minimum revocation follow a DUI involving bodily injury?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: DUI with bodily injury carries a fine of two hundred to one thousand dollars, jail of twenty-four hours to twelve months, and a minimum revocation of sixty days.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: How severe are the fine, prison range, and revocation for a DUI causing serious bodily injury?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: A DUI involving serious bodily injury carries a fine from one thousand to three thousand dollars, two to ten years in jail, and at least a sixty-day license revocation.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: How is a DUI resulting in death classified, and what prison term and license penalty follow?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: DUI with death is a felony carrying jail of five to thirty years and a lifetime revocation.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: What fine, jail sentence, and minimum revocation apply to a second DUI offense?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: A second DUI offense carries a fine of one thousand to three thousand dollars, jail of six to twelve months, and a minimum revocation of one year.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: What fine, incarceration term, and minimum revocation hit a third or subsequent DUI offender?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: A third or subsequent DUI offense carries a fine of three thousand to five thousand dollars, jail of one to three years, and a minimum revocation of one year.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: How long does license revocation last when a driver under eighteen commits a DUI?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: A DUI offense by a driver under eighteen results in revocation until the age of eighteen or for the applicable statutory period, whichever is longer, and until all other requirements are met.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: What program must every driver revoked or suspended for DUI finish before getting a license back?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: Whenever a license is revoked or suspended for DUI, the driver must complete a prescribed Safety and Treatment program before becoming eligible for reinstatement.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: How does minimum license revocation change between a first DUI below point one five and one at or above it?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: A first DUI below a point one five concentration carries a fifteen-day minimum revocation, whereas a first DUI at point one five or more carries forty-five days.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: What stays the same and what increases between second and third DUI offenses?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: Both second and third or subsequent DUI offenses carry a one-year minimum revocation, while jail increases from six to twelve months to one to three years and the fine rises from one thousand to three thousand dollars up to three thousand to five thousand dollars.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: Which penalty detail separates DUI with child endangerment from DUI with bodily injury?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: DUI with child endangerment and DUI with bodily injury share the same fine range and sixty-day revocation, but the child endangerment jail minimum is forty-eight hours while the bodily injury minimum is twenty-four hours.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.front: What two hurdles stand between an under-eighteen DUI offender and license reinstatement?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.expected_back: A DUI by a driver under eighteen revokes the license until eighteen or for the statutory period, whichever is longer, and every DUI revocation requires the Safety and Treatment program before reinstatement.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: Which chemical check have arrested DUI suspects already consented to, and what penalty hits refusal?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: A driver arrested for DUI is subject to the implied consent law and is deemed to have consented to the designated breath test for alcohol content, and refusing that test brings revocation of the driving privilege for one year and up to life.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: How does West Virginia's implied consent law protect both sober motorists and the general public?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: The implied consent law does not mean a fine or jail for having alcohol on the breath, rather it protects a driver who has not been drinking because the test gives a medically accepted measure, and it safeguards the public by arresting those who refuse to be tested.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: What driving restriction and mechanical safeguard define West Virginia's Interlock Program after an alcohol DUI?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: A DUI or DUI-related event places a revocation on the driving record, and when alcohol was involved the driver may join the Interlock Program, which allows legal driving only in a vehicle fitted with an ignition interlock device that prevents an intoxicated person from starting the car.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: When does joining the Interlock Program stop being optional and become mandatory?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: Interlock participation is an option for some DUI offenders and mandatory for others depending on the offense, and a driver revoked for two or more DUI or related offenses within a ten-year period must participate.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: How does getting Interlock approval before your scheduled revocation start date change your downtime?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: A driver whose Interlock application is approved before the scheduled revocation begins does not serve a minimum revocation period and can install the device immediately, while a driver who applies late may have to serve the minimum revocation and still complete the program.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: How does implied-consent breath refusal relate to underlying DUI court penalties?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: Refusing the breath test after a DUI arrest revokes the driving privilege for one year and up to life, a consequence of the implied consent law that is separate from any DUI penalty.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: What repeat-offense count mandates Interlock, and what filing timing avoids sitting out minimum revocation?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: Interlock participation is optional for some offenders but mandatory after two or more DUI revocations within ten years, and applying before the revocation begins is what avoids the minimum revocation period.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: Roughly what percentage of recent West Virginia fatal crashes involved alcohol-impaired drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Alcohol mixed with driving is one of the greatest factors in highway crashes, and studies cited by the handbook show that about twenty-eight percent of recent fatal crashes in West Virginia involved drivers who had been driving under the influence of alcohol.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: Are drivers twenty-one and older the only group involved in alcohol-related fatal crashes?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: Adults are not the only drivers responsible for alcohol-related fatal crashes, because drivers under twenty-one years of age are involved in them as well.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: Which three core driving abilities does alcohol degrade right away?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: Alcohol reduces alertness, interferes with judgment and impairs vision.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: Why can the exact same drink hit the same person harder on one day than another?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: Alcohol affects a person differently at different times, because physical and emotional conditions, other drugs or even the amount of food in the stomach can change its effect.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: What actually lowers alcohol impairment when someone tries coffee, cold showers, exercise, or fresh air?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: Physical exercise, black coffee, fresh air, cold showers and other home remedies do not effectively sober a person up, and time is the only sobering influence.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: How does the pure alcohol content compare across a one-ounce hundred-proof shot, six-ounce wine, and twelve-ounce beer?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: A one-ounce shot of one-hundred-proof whiskey, a six-ounce glass of wine and a twelve-ounce can of beer all contain the same amount of alcohol.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: Why can a person who has been drinking not trust their own decision that they are fine to drive?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: Drinking affects judgment, so decisions made under the influence of alcohol reflect impeded judgment.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: What defines a true designated driver, and when should the group choose that person?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: A designated driver, the most reasonable, safe and practical way to avoid drinking and driving, is a selected or volunteer companion who will not drink alcohol while responsible for driving friends home, and should be appointed before any activity involving alcohol begins.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: How can prescription or over-the-counter drugs affect driving, especially when mixed with alcohol?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: Driving while using drugs is very dangerous with effects like those of drinking, because drugs, even prescribed or bought over the counter, can cause drowsiness, loss of coordination, hallucinations or total body malfunctions, and alcohol combined with drugs can be deadly.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: How much do black coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers change bloodstream alcohol concentration?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: Only time sobers a drinker, so coffee, exercise, fresh air and cold showers change nothing about the blood alcohol level.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: Why do a twelve-ounce beer, six-ounce wine, and one-ounce whiskey shot hit with equal alcohol?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: The whiskey shot, the six-ounce glass of wine and the twelve-ounce beer are equal in alcohol content even though they differ greatly in volume.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: After roughly how many hours awake do driving skills drop to alcohol- or drug-impaired performance?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: Drowsy driving is impaired driving, because after being awake for about eighteen hours driving skills become comparable to those of someone under the influence of drugs or alcohol, reaction time slows and crash risk rises.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.front: In what five ways does drowsiness degrade a driver's performance at the wheel?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.expected_back: A drowsy driver responds more slowly to road and traffic conditions, struggles to process complex information from several places at once, grows careless in driving decisions, has trouble paying attention and may fall asleep at the wheel.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.front: What should you do when drowsiness hits on the road, and how short a nap helps?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.expected_back: The best way to reduce drowsiness is more sleep, and a drowsy driver should not drive but pull over to a safe area for a short nap, since as little as ten to twenty minutes of sleep can make a big difference.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.front: During which three daily windows do drivers commonly feel sleepy, and what ride alternatives help?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.expected_back: Drivers should avoid driving at the times they feel sleepy, often early morning, late afternoon or night, and should let a well-rested person drive, carpool, use public transportation, call a taxi or ask a family member or friend to drive.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.front: Which vehicle movements and driver posture clues warn that another motorist nearby is drowsy?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.expected_back: Another driver may be drowsy when the head nods or drops, the vehicle drifts out of the lane, crosses edge or center lines or hits rumble strips, there are near misses especially rear-end, speed varies erratically with weaving, or the vehicle rear-ends another, hits one head-on or strikes a stationary object.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.front: Which physical and memory warning signs prove you yourself are too drowsy to keep driving?
