sec05-card-sec05-F35.expected_back: Signs that you yourself are drowsy include falling asleep at stop lights, yawning, rubbing the eyes, watery eyes, heavy eyelids, not remembering the last few miles, missing road signs or exits, unplanned lane changes, head nodding and driving off the road or onto the rumble strips.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: How do the eighteen-hour wakefulness danger point and the effective roadside nap length compare?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: About eighteen hours awake impairs driving like alcohol or drugs, yet a nap of only ten to twenty minutes can make a big difference when drowsiness strikes.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: Which movements does a circular green signal permit, and to whom must a left-turning driver yield?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: A driver facing a circular green signal may enter the intersection and go straight, turn right or turn left unless signs or pavement markings prohibit a movement, every turn follows the right-of-way rules, and a left turn on circular green must yield to oncoming vehicles.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: What movement does a lighted green arrow authorize, and what is usually true on a left-turn green arrow?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: A green arrow, shown alone or with other indications, lets drivers enter the intersection to make the movement the arrow shows, and a green arrow in a left-turn signal usually means that opposing traffic is stopped.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: What do steady circular yellow and yellow arrows warn, and when is driving through yellow appropriate?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: A steady circular yellow means the green is ending and will change to red, you should drive through a yellow only if your vehicle is already within the intersection clearance, and a yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending and will change to red.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: What must drivers facing a steady circular red do, and what two exceptions allow movement?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: Traffic facing a steady circular red must stop unless making a movement permitted by a green arrow, and must remain stopped until another indication allows it to proceed, the only exception being a permitted turn on red.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: Under what street layouts and conditions may West Virginia drivers turn right or left on red?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: A driver may turn right on red at the intersection of two-way streets, or turn left on red from a one-way street onto another one-way street, but only after yielding to all other traffic and pedestrians and only where no sign prohibits the turn.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: Where must you stop for a steady red arrow, and how long must you hold?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: A steady red arrow requires a complete stop before the intersection, stop line or crosswalk for the direction the arrow shows, and the driver must remain stopped as long as the arrow is red.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: How does turning permission differ between a steady circular red and a steady red arrow?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: A steady circular red still allows a permitted turn on red after yielding, whereas a steady red arrow means remaining stopped for that direction as long as the arrow stays red.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: How does oncoming traffic behave during a circular-green left turn versus a green-arrow left turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: A left turn on a circular green must yield to oncoming vehicles, while a left-turn green arrow usually means the opposing traffic is stopped.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: How do the street requirements compare for turning right on red versus turning left on red?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: Turning right on red is allowed at an intersection of two-way streets, but turning left on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, both after yielding and absent a prohibiting sign.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: What three jobs do pavement markings perform, and how do white and yellow lines differ?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: Pavement markings warn, regulate and inform traffic like highway signs, white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction, and yellow lines separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: What traffic does a broken yellow line divide, and when does it allow passing?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: Broken yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, and when the broken yellow line is on your side of the road you may pass when it is safe.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: What does a solid yellow stripe on your side forbid, and where does solid yellow mark the left pavement edge?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: Solid yellow lines also separate opposing traffic, a solid yellow line on your side of the road means you must not pass, and on interstates, one-way streets and divided four-lane roads a solid yellow line marks the left edge of the pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: How are multilane same-direction roads striped, why is black sometimes added, and what straddling rule applies?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: On roadways with more than one lane moving in the same direction the lanes are separated by broken white lines, sometimes with broken black lines added for visibility, and you drive within the lines and never straddle them except when changing lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: What does a solid white stripe mark at the road edge versus between same-direction lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: Solid white lines mark the edge of the pavement and help you stay on the road at night or in bad weather, and where solid white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction you do not change lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: What is the sole legal use of a center left-turn lane, and how are its yellow lines arranged?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: Center left-turn lanes are reserved exclusively for left turns from either direction rather than through travel or passing, and they are marked by solid yellow lines beside the through lanes with broken lines inside them.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: How are reversible lanes striped on both sides, and what normal yellow-line rule do they uniquely allow?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: Reversible lanes, used where traffic is heavy at certain times of day, are marked on both sides by a double broken yellow line, and this is the only case in which a driver may drive for any distance to the left of a yellow line.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: How does a broken yellow line on your side compare with a solid yellow line on your side?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.memory_hook: Broken allows safe pass, solid bans
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: A broken yellow line on your side permits passing when safe, but a solid yellow line on your side forbids passing entirely.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: How do broken white lines and solid white lines between same-direction lanes differ?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: A broken white line between same-direction lanes allows a lane change without straddling, whereas a solid white line between same-direction lanes means do not change lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: How do the yellow markings and legal uses separate a reversible lane from a center left-turn lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: A reversible lane marked on both sides by a double yellow broken line is the sole case where a driver may travel any distance left of a yellow line, whereas a center left-turn lane has solid yellow outer lines and broken inner lines for left turns only.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: Why are intersection flashers hung at certain corners, and what two color setups can they display?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: At certain intersections flashers supplement or replace stop signs, showing circular flashing red in all directions or circular flashing yellow for the through traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: What driver response is required at a circular flashing yellow versus a circular flashing red?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: A driver facing a circular flashing yellow may proceed through the intersection with caution, while a circular flashing red is the same as a stop sign and requires a complete stop and yielding to all other traffic and pedestrians.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: Under what two circumstances do regular signals switch to flashing mode, and what rules apply then?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: When traffic control signals are not needed or are out of order they may be placed in flashing operation, and they then work the same as intersection flashers.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: What do a green downward arrow, a yellow X, and a red X directly over a lane each mean?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.memory_hook: Green open, yellow vacate, red closed
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: Lane use control signals show a green downward arrow when traffic may use the lane under it, a yellow X when the lane is about to close or reverse direction and you should move out as soon as you can, and a red X when the lane is closed or carrying opposing traffic and must not be used.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: On what kind of streets are special overhead lane signals installed, and what do they show?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: Special lane signals are used where the direction of a street or of certain lanes changes during the day, and they indicate how each lane may be used.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: What is the core legal contrast between circular flashing yellow and circular flashing red?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: A circular flashing yellow means proceed with caution, but a circular flashing red is treated exactly like a stop sign with a complete stop and yielding.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: How does your required action under an overhead yellow X differ from an overhead red X?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.memory_hook: Leave yellow soon, never enter red
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: A yellow X over a lane warns that the lane is about to close or reverse so you should leave it soon, while a red X means the lane is already closed or carrying opposing traffic and must not be used.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: Which yellow shapes and white crossbuck design mark rail crossings, and when is a track-count plaque added?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Railroad crossing signs may be round or diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols, or black letters on white bars in the shape of an X called a crossbuck, and a sign below the crossbuck gives the number of tracks when there are two or more.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: What three electrical devices warn of approaching trains, who holds priority, and what penalty hits ignoring them?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Some railroad crossings have electrical devices such as bells, flashers and automatic gates to signal an approaching train, you must yield to all trains, and failing to stop when the lights are flashing or a barrier is down results in a citation.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: What two hazards must you guard against at multi-track crossings and behind slow traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: Where there are two or more tracks you must be alert for a second train on the other set of tracks, and you should not enter a crossing until the vehicle ahead has moved far enough that you can clear the tracks, or you may be trapped and hit by another vehicle or a train.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: How do advance yellow rail signs, white crossbucks, and multi-track plaques fit together?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: Railroad crossing signs appear either as round or diamond-shaped yellow signs bearing black symbols or as white X-shaped crossbucks bearing black letters, with an added sign below the crossbuck showing the track count when there are two or more.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: What do the hand or DON'T WALK display and the walking figure or WALK display command pedestrians to do?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: Crosswalk signals are traffic signals for pedestrians who must obey them, a hand symbol or the words don't walk means pedestrians are not to cross, and a walking figure or the word walk means they may cross inside the crosswalk lines.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: What do intersection and school-zone crosswalks signal to approaching motorists?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: Crosswalks at intersections and in school zones signal a high pedestrian traffic zone, and being especially alert for pedestrians there reduces the risk of crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: Where on West Virginia roads does a blind pedestrian with a service animal or white cane hold right-of-way?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: A blind person on foot who uses a guide dog or other service animal or carries a white cane or walking stick has the right-of-way on any highway, street or road whether or not in a crosswalk.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: Which three special travel modes are designated by white diamond shapes painted inside a lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: White diamond shapes painted in a lane tell drivers the lane is designated for car pools, bicycles or buses.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: How do marked and residential unmarked crosswalks look, and what must your car never do on one?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: Many crosswalks are marked by solid white lines running all the way across the pavement at intersections and sometimes between them, some crosswalks especially in residential areas are unmarked, and you must not block a crosswalk with your car.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: What do wide white stop lines mark, and where do you stop when neither a stop line nor crosswalk exists?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: Stop lines are wide white lines painted across the traffic lanes to mark where you must stop at an intersection, keeping you clear of pedestrians and cross traffic, and where there is no stop line or crosswalk you stop before entering the intersection where you can see traffic from all directions.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: How do pedestrian walk signals contrast with the rule for a blind pedestrian using a cane or guide dog?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: The hand symbol or don't walk indication forbids pedestrians to cross while the walking figure or walk indication permits it, yet a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane has the right-of-way everywhere regardless of a crosswalk.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.front: How do wide white stop lines differ in function from solid white crosswalk lines?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.memory_hook: Stop bar halts, crosswalk stays clear
sec08-card-sec08-R11.expected_back: Wide white stop lines mark exactly where to stop at an intersection, whereas solid white crosswalk lines run fully across the pavement and mark a space a car must never block.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.front: Who makes sure passengers buckle up, and which two exceptions exist under West Virginia's safety belt law?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.expected_back: Everyone in a passenger vehicle must wear a federally approved safety belt, the driver is responsible for seeing that all passengers are buckled, the only legal exception is a person eighteen or older riding in the back seat, and a medical exception may be issued with proof of the condition.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.front: By what percentage does a safety belt cut injury or death risk, and where must the lap and shoulder belts rest?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.memory_hook: Cuts risk near half, low hips
sec15-card-sec15-F17.expected_back: Wearing a safety belt cuts the chance of injury or death in a collision by forty-five to fifty percent because the belt spreads crash forces over the strongest parts of the body and helps occupants ride down the crash, the lap belt fitting snugly over the lower hips and the shoulder belt worn with it for upper-body protection.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.front: How does a properly worn safety belt help you both in crashes and on bumpy or winding roads?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.expected_back: Properly used safety belts keep you from being thrown forward or out of the vehicle and hold you in the proper driving position on bumpy or twisting roads.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.front: When must a child under eight use a federally approved safety device, and what height allows a regular belt?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.expected_back: A driver transporting a child under eight in a passenger automobile, van or pickup truck not operated for hire must secure the child in a child passenger safety device that meets federal standards while the vehicle moves on a street or highway, but a child under eight who is at least four feet nine inches tall may be protected by a safety belt alone.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.front: Compare the age-and-seat exception for adult safety belts with the height exception for children under eight?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.expected_back: The only legal safety belt exception is a person eighteen or older in the back seat, while a child under eight needs a child safety device unless the child is at least four feet nine inches tall.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.front: How much does wearing a safety belt reduce crash injury or death risk, and how should the lap strap fit?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.expected_back: Wearing safety belts cuts the risk of collision injury or death by forty-five to fifty percent, and the lap belt should fit snugly and comfortably across the lower hips.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.front: Where is a rear-facing infant seat strictly forbidden, and where do children twelve and under belong?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.expected_back: A rear-facing infant seat never goes in front of a passenger air bag, and children twelve and under belong buckled in the rear seat.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.front: What injury do head restraints help prevent, and where should an adjustable restraint sit?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.expected_back: Head restraints reduce the chance of whiplash injury in rear-end collisions and, when adjustable, should fit against the back of the head rather than the neck.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.front: How must you brake and steer during a quick stop with anti-lock brakes, and why must you never pump them?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.expected_back: The anti-lock brake system prevents wheel lockup during a quick stop so the driver keeps control, and with anti-lock brakes the driver must keep steering while pushing hard on the brake, because pumping anti-lock brakes reduces the system's ability to stop and can lose all brake force.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.front: At best, how much do anti-lock brakes shorten a sudden stop compared with ordinary brakes?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.expected_back: It is a misconception that anti-lock brakes stop a vehicle much shorter than regular brakes, since in a sudden stop they improve performance by only about ten percent at best, they are not super brakes that stop on a dime, and drivers should not take extra risks because of them.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.front: In what years did dual air bags become required on passenger cars and on new light trucks?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.expected_back: Dual air bags were required on all passenger vehicles beginning in nineteen ninety-eight and on all new light trucks in nineteen ninety-nine to protect the driver and front passenger in a crash, and while they are credited with saving thousands of lives, precautions are needed so they do not cause serious or fatal injury.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.front: With an air bag in the wheel, why must you buckle up, where do your hands go, and how should front seats sit?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.memory_hook: Buckle up, grip four-and-eight, tilt back
sec15-card-sec15-F24.expected_back: With air bags the driver and every passenger should keep their seat belts secured because most people killed by air bags were unbelted, the driver should hold the wheel from the side with the right hand at four o'clock and the left at eight o'clock so the arms are not between the bag and the body, and both front seats should be tilted slightly back as far from the air bag as possible.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.front: What rules govern rear-facing infants, unavoidable front-seat child riders, and children twelve and under around air bags?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.memory_hook: Never rear-facing front, slide seat back
sec15-card-sec15-F25.expected_back: An infant in a rear-facing safety seat must never ride in the front passenger seat of a vehicle with a passenger-side air bag, and when there is no other way a child there must be in a forward-facing seat, properly secured, with the passenger seat pushed all the way back, while all children twelve and under should ride buckled in the rear seat with younger children in child safety seats.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.front: Why does old-school brake pumping backfire in a vehicle equipped with anti-lock brakes?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.expected_back: With anti-lock brakes you press hard and keep steering, because pumping, the old advice for ordinary brakes, can cost all braking force in an anti-lock vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.front: Since anti-lock brakes trim sudden stops by roughly ten percent at most, what is their true main benefit?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.memory_hook: Steering control beats small distance gain
sec15-card-sec15-R06.expected_back: Anti-lock brakes shorten a sudden stop by only about ten percent at best, so their real benefit is steering control rather than stopping distance.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.front: What clock positions hold the steering wheel safely around an air bag, and what did most air-bag fatalities lack?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.expected_back: Around an air bag the hands sit at four and eight o'clock on the wheel, and most people killed by air bags were not wearing seat belts.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.front: Against which part of your body must an adjustable head restraint rest to reduce whiplash?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.expected_back: An adjustable head restraint fits against the back of the head, not the neck, because its job is to limit whiplash in a rear-end collision.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.front: Who is responsible for safe vehicle condition, and which nine equipment defects commonly cause crashes?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.memory_hook: Driver maintains tires, brakes, lights, belts
sec15-card-sec15-F01.expected_back: Keeping the vehicle in proper driving condition is the driver's job, and the common defects that cause crashes are faulty tires, brakes, lights, windshield wipers, defrosters, mufflers and exhaust systems, horns, mirrors and unusable seat belts.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.front: Which four common physical or mental driver conditions undermine safe vehicle operation?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.expected_back: Make sure you are physically and mentally ready to drive, because the most common driver conditions that affect safe operation are fatigue, alcohol, emotional state, and defective eyesight or hearing.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.front: How does fatigue hurt driving, and what should you do when tired alone versus with licensed passengers?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.expected_back: Fatigue from lack of sleep or driving too long dulls the mind and slows reaction time, so a tired driver who is alone should pull off the road and rest, and when other licensed drivers are aboard drivers should change as soon as one becomes tired.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.front: How often and for how long should you rest on a long trip, where should you spend that break, and what fights monotony?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.memory_hook: Ten minutes outside every two hours
sec15-card-sec15-F04.expected_back: On a long trip take a ten-minute rest break at least every two hours and spend it outside the vehicle, and rolling the window down, turning the radio on or singing can reduce the monotony of driving.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.front: What should you do if anger, worry, or fear hits before you get behind the wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.expected_back: Emotional states such as anger, worry or fear should be brought under control, and the driver should regain self-control before driving.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.front: What is the exact timing and location rule for rest breaks on a long road trip?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.memory_hook: Every two hours, ten minutes outside
sec15-card-sec15-R01.expected_back: The long-trip rest rule is a ten-minute break at least every two hours, and the break counts only when spent outside the vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.front: Because the vehicle ahead can brake suddenly without warning, what three habits protect you from rear-ending it?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.memory_hook: Stay alert, anticipate stops, keep space
sec15-card-sec15-F09.expected_back: The vehicle ahead may stop suddenly and without warning, so stay alert, anticipate a sudden stop and keep a safe following distance to avoid a crash.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.front: What duty do you owe a tailgating driver behind you whenever you slow down, stop, or turn?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.expected_back: You have a responsibility to a tailgating driver behind you to signal whenever you change your driving pattern, because what you do affects that driver, especially if you slow down or stop suddenly.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.front: What common errors or emergencies might send an oncoming vehicle across the centerline into your lane?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.expected_back: An oncoming driver may cross into your lane because of sleep, drink, distraction, recovering from a drop off the pavement, turning, trying to pass, avoiding a pedestrian or obstacle, or simply while rounding a curve.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.front: Where do you encounter vehicles approaching at an angle, and what keeps those conflict points safe?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.expected_back: A vehicle at an angle to yours is the situation at intersections, driveways and parking lot entrances and exits, so learn the traffic laws and obey the signs and signals that control those places.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.front: How should you react when another driver starts passing you?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.memory_hook: Ease off, hug right, zero ego
sec15-card-sec15-F13.expected_back: Being passed should never be taken as a challenge, because many sideswipe and run-off-the-road crashes result from it, so check the rear view mirror often, know what is going on around you, slow down and keep as close to the right side of the road as possible to make passing easy.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.front: May you exceed the posted speed limit to pass, and what does needing extra speed tell you?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.expected_back: Passing is acceptable when done legally, smoothly, skillfully and with consideration, but it adds wear and fuel consumption and can involve you in a head-on, sideswipe or run-off-the-road crash, exceeding the speed limit to pass is illegal, and if you must speed to pass you probably do not need to pass.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.front: Walk through the key checks, warnings, and mirror cue in West Virginia's ten-step safe passing sequence?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.memory_hook: Check, signal, warn, see both headlights
sec15-card-sec15-F15.expected_back: The ten steps to passing safely are to keep a safe following distance, check oncoming traffic, check the traffic behind, signal before the lane change, move to the left lane, accelerate, warn other drivers with the horn or by flashing the lights, signal the lane change back, merge right when the passed vehicle's headlights appear in your rear view mirror, and maintain a safe legal speed.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.front: What is your job when being passed versus the speed-limit rule when you are the one passing?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.memory_hook: Slow right when passed, obey limit
sec15-card-sec15-R09.expected_back: When another vehicle passes you, slow down and keep right rather than treating it as a challenge, and when you pass, exceeding the speed limit is illegal.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.front: In the ten passing steps, how do you alert the driver ahead and when is it safe to merge back right?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.memory_hook: Tap horn or lights, mirror headlights
sec15-card-sec15-R10.expected_back: In the ten passing steps the warning to the other driver comes by horn or flashing lights, and the merge back right waits until the passed vehicle's headlights show in your rear view mirror.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.front: What are the usual weekday morning inbound and afternoon outbound metro rush hours, and when do industrial areas peak?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.expected_back: Rush hours bring congested traffic and hurried drivers, usually inbound to metropolitan areas between seven and nine in the morning and outbound between four and six in the afternoon, while rush hours in industrial areas follow the changes of work shifts.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.front: How does traffic risk shift from weekday commutes to weekends, summer vacations, and holiday weekends?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.memory_hook: Longer trips bring tired, impaired drivers
sec15-card-sec15-F07.expected_back: Rush-hour traffic is heaviest on weekdays, weekends bring drivers making longer trips and driving longer hours, and summer vacation travel and holiday weekends increase traffic volume along with tired, hurried and drunk drivers.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.front: Contrast typical rural driving hazards with urban ones, and what shared challenge do heavy trucks and buses add?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.memory_hook: Tractors and deer versus city stops
sec15-card-sec15-F08.expected_back: Rural driving brings slow-moving farm machinery, stray livestock, game animals and motorists at higher speeds, urban driving brings more pedestrians, bicycles, intersections and stop-and-go traffic, and a defensive driver always notes the heavy trucks and buses that complicate passing and slow traffic on hills.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.front: What four personal safety habits apply to doors, windows, hitchhikers, and phones before and during a drive?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.memory_hook: Lock doors, skip hitchhikers, hands-free phone
sec15-card-sec15-F26.expected_back: Keep the doors locked and the windows up while driving or parked, avoid hitchhikers however innocent or needy they appear, learn your vehicle's controls and safety equipment, and turn off your wireless communication device or enable its hands-free function before driving.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.front: Where should you lock valuables, and where should you go instead of stopping on the roadside if lost?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.memory_hook: Hide valuables, check maps somewhere busy
sec15-card-sec15-F27.expected_back: Lock purses, wallets, luggage and valuables in the trunk or glove compartment, and if you become lost do not study a map on the roadside but drive to a well-lit, populated public place such as a service station or restaurant, locking the vehicle and taking the keys.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.front: What safety checks belong when walking up to your parked car, and what should you do if someone follows you?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.memory_hook: Keys ready, check car, dial nine-one-one
sec15-card-sec15-F28.expected_back: Always park in well-lit areas with your keys in hand as you approach, check inside and underneath the vehicle before entering, and if you feel you are being followed drive to a well-lit populated area and call the police, which in most areas means dialing nine one one.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.front: Which two-hour windows mark metro inbound morning rush hour and outbound afternoon rush hour?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.expected_back: Metropolitan rush hour runs inbound from seven to nine in the morning but outbound from four to six in the afternoon.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: What does blood alcohol concentration measure, and what unlawful limits apply to drivers over twenty-one versus under twenty-one?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Even one drink can push an underage driver past point zero two percent long before reaching the adult threshold.
sec01-card-sec01-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Point zero eight over, zero-two under

visual_sync.text_span: Point zero eight over, zero-two under

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: What substances and vehicles fall under West Virginia's definition of driving under the influence?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Many test-takers assume impairment laws target only liquor in cars, forgetting prescriptions and drugs in any motor vehicle.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: What test agreement binds every licensed West Virginia driver when charged with impaired driving, and what happens if you refuse?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Holding a license automatically commits you to chemical testing, so saying no triggers at least a full-year privilege loss.
sec01-card-sec01-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Refusing chemical test suspends one year

visual_sync.text_span: Refusing chemical test suspends one year

sec01-card-sec01-F31.question_text: What happens to your driver's license and renewal rights when West Virginia revokes your driving privilege?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.teaching_text: Unlike a temporary hold, revocation wipes out the existing credential so regaining privileges requires applying fresh when permitted.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.question_text: How does West Virginia define a suspension of a driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.teaching_text: Driving during that temporary withdrawal window is still completely illegal until the state restores your highway privileges.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: What is the core difference between a license suspension and a license revocation?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Exam questions pair these two definitions to see who spots temporary withdrawal versus permanent termination without renewal.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: Which age group faces the point zero two percent alcohol limit, and which faces point zero eight percent?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Test choices frequently flip these two percentages, so anchor the tiny point zero two figure to underage drivers.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.question_text: What specific act does implied consent penalize on its own, and for at least how long?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.teaching_text: Even before a court rules on intoxication, turning down the chemical test triggers its own minimum one-year suspension.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: Whom does the West Virginia handbook define as a driver?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Sitting behind the wheel in physical control on a public lot counts as being a driver even before rolling.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: What does a state-issued driver's license authorize, and what conditions shape that permission?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Holding a standard license never authorizes every rig on the road unless your class, endorsements, and restrictions match.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.question_text: Which three roles qualify someone as an operator of a motor vehicle on a highway?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.teaching_text: Guiding the wheel of a disabled car being pulled down a highway makes you an operator under state law.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: Who counts as a commercial driver on West Virginia public streets or highways?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Notice the catchphrase for any purpose, meaning an empty errand run on public pavement still counts as commercial driving.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: How many phases make up West Virginia's graduated driver's license program, and what age span does it cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Stepping teens through three structured stages builds real traffic habits before granting full solo nighttime and passenger privileges.
sec01-card-sec01-F16.must_match_memory_hook: Three phases ages fifteen to eighteen

visual_sync.text_span: Three phases ages fifteen to eighteen

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: Besides the motorist powering the front vehicle, who else counts as an operator during a highway tow?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Steering a dead car behind a tow strap requires the exact same sober, licensed care as driving under power.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: How much space does the legal term highway cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Because highway spans boundary to boundary, traffic laws reach shoulders and ditches alongside the paved lanes.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.question_text: Which portion of a highway counts as the roadway, and what is left out?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.teaching_text: Keeping the shoulder outside the roadway definition explains why passing or cruising on the berm breaks lane rules.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: What three features can separate opposing roadways on a divided highway?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Painted yellow lines alone do not create a divided highway unless physical space, curbing, or a barrier splits directions.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: How does an interchange move traffic between two or more roadways?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Bridges and ramps let high-speed freeway traffic switch routes smoothly without stopping at flat cross-traffic lights.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: What shared highway area forms an intersection, even when one road ends without crossing through?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: T-junctions count as full intersections for right-of-way and parking rules even though the side road stops there.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: What does an acceleration lane let an entering driver do beside a high-speed highway?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Stopping dead at the end of an entrance lane creates rear-end danger instead of matching freeway flow.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: Why is a deceleration lane placed beside regular highway travel lanes?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Braking hard while still in the main freeway lane risks a high-speed rear-end crash before your exit.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: What movement does the term merging traffic describe?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Drivers often look only right for ramps, forgetting left-side merges where adjacent lanes blend into main flow.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.question_text: How does the handbook define right-of-way?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.teaching_text: Notice it is called a privilege rather than an absolute guarantee, so never force your way into a crash.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: How do acceleration lanes and deceleration lanes split entering and leaving highway duties?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Pairing each ramp lane with its speed change keeps through lanes moving smoothly at highway pace.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: Does the berm or shoulder belong to the roadway, the highway, or both?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Test writers love asking whether shoulders sit inside the roadway, so remember roadway covers travel lanes alone.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: How does an interchange differ structurally from an intersection?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Overpasses and ramps eliminate flat right-angle crossings where T-bone collisions happen most often.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: Which weight rating, passenger capacity, or cargo requirement makes a vehicle a commercial motor vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Watch that extra single pound above twenty-six thousand, plus counting the driver inside the sixteen-passenger threshold.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: What passenger capacity and transport purpose define a bus in West Virginia?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Both pieces matter on the exam since carrying at least eight riders and hauling for compensation go together.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.question_text: Who can own a school bus, and what transport job defines it?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.teaching_text: Privately contracted school buses command the exact same stop-arm respect as county-owned yellow fleets.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: What wheel count, pedal feature, horsepower, engine size, and top-speed limits define a moped?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: Exceeding two horsepower, fifty cubic centimeters, or thirty miles per hour bumps a two-wheeler out of moped rules.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: How does West Virginia define a motorcycle by seating, vehicle exclusion, and wheel count?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.teaching_text: Three-wheeled trikes qualify as motorcycles when built with a rider seat, whereas farm tractors are expressly excluded.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: What maximum engine size defines a motor-driven cycle, and how are scooters and mopeds treated?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.teaching_text: Motor scooters up to two hundred fifty cubic centimeters fit here, while pedal-equipped mopeds sit in their own class.
sec01-card-sec01-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Up to two-fifty cc, no mopeds

visual_sync.text_span: Up to two-fifty cc, no mopeds

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: What two traits define a motor vehicle in the handbook?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.teaching_text: Leaving out rail cars and trains keeps highway vehicle laws focused on road-going powered machines.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: What makes a four-wheeled vehicle a true low-speed vehicle, and do modified golf carts or all-terrain vehicles qualify?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Bolting headlights onto a golf cart or four-wheeler never turns it into a street-legal low-speed vehicle.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: On which roads and maximum speed zones may a low-speed vehicle operate?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Mixing slow neighborhood pods onto faster county highways invites severe rear-end collisions.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: How old must a West Virginia antique vehicle be, and how may its owner use it?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Using antique tags for daily work or school commuting violates the collector-only restriction.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: What work is a farm tractor designed and mainly used to perform?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Slow-moving tractors pulling wide field gear on rural two-lanes need extra patience and wide passing clearance.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: How does the handbook define an implement of husbandry?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Specialized harvesters, wagons, and sprayers adapted for crop work fall under agricultural equipment rules.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: How do the engine ceilings of a moped and a motor-driven cycle compare?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Memorize fifty versus two hundred fifty cubic centimeters because exam questions pair these two small-bike definitions.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: Why doesn't counting two or three wheels tell you whether a machine is a motorcycle or a moped?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Since both categories permit up to three wheels, pedals, horsepower, and engine displacement decide the class.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: What separates West Virginia's school bus definition from its general bus definition?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: School bus status hinges on hauling students to or from school regardless of public or private ownership.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: How do the passenger thresholds differ between a commercial motor vehicle and a general bus?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Keep sixteen including the driver distinct from more than seven for pay when reading passenger-van questions.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: Why do modified golf carts and all-terrain vehicles fail West Virginia's low-speed vehicle definition?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.teaching_text: Only four-wheelers designated as low-speed vehicles right on the manufacturer's certificate of origin qualify.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.question_text: What separates a farm tractor from an implement of husbandry?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.teaching_text: Think of the tractor as the powered tow unit and implements as the agricultural machinery designed for farm tasks.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: What are blind spots around your vehicle, and how must you check them?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Mirrors alone leave dangerous side pockets big enough to hide motorcycles or compact cars during lane changes.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: How does the handbook define following distance?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Keeping generous room in front buys reaction time when brake lights flare unexpectedly on slick mountain grades.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: Which four responder fleets does the handbook specifically name as authorized emergency vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Chartered rescue squads hold the exact same yield-right-of-way authority as police cruisers, fire trucks, and ambulances.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.question_text: Who counts as a pedestrian under the handbook's definitions?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.teaching_text: Every person walking near curbs, crosswalks, or rural shoulders lacks metal crash protection and depends on alert drivers.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.question_text: What two categories make up a wireless communications device?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.teaching_text: Text-messaging gadgets without voice service still count under West Virginia's distracted-driving rules.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: What must every non-exempt West Virginia resident hold and carry when driving on public roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Leaving your plastic card on the kitchen counter violates the carry rule even when your privilege is valid.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: When is someone in the United States armed services exempt from needing a West Virginia driver's license?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Driving a military vehicle under official orders waives state licensing, whereas personal off-duty cars follow normal rules.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: Which nonresident visitors may drive without a West Virginia license, and for how many days per calendar year?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Out-of-state visitors must be at least sixteen with a valid home license and cannot exceed ninety days yearly.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: When is an out-of-state college or university student exempt from getting a West Virginia license?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Full-time campus life stretches past ninety days, so out-of-state students keep driving legally on valid home-state cards.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: How can habitual alcohol use or narcotic drug addiction affect license eligibility?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Chronic substance dependence creates ongoing highway danger long before any single roadside arrest occurs.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: Can someone suspended or revoked in another state or foreign jurisdiction get a West Virginia license right away?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Moving across state lines never wipes a bad driving record clean while another jurisdiction's hold remains active.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: When may the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles deny an applicant on public-safety grounds?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Broad safety authority lets the Commissioner keep demonstrably hazardous operators off public streets before tragedy strikes.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: What educational failure allows West Virginia to deny a driver's license to an applicant under eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Dropping out of approved schooling before eighteen without a diploma can block teen driving privileges completely.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: Does the ninety-day calendar-year limit apply to general nonresident drivers or to nonresident college students?

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: Which four proof categories must every first-time applicant bring, and what happens to your original papers?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: Clerks scan your original certificates securely into your file and hand them right back at the counter.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.question_text: How many identity proofs and residency proofs must new, transfer, and expired-license applicants bring alongside Social Security and name-change records?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.teaching_text: Showing up with only one utility bill sends you home empty-handed because residency always demands two physical-address proofs.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.question_text: Which three groups does the handbook treat as first-time applicants?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.teaching_text: Letting your West Virginia card sit expired past three years drops you right back into the first-time bucket.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.question_text: Why must your full legal name match Social Security Administration files when presenting your one identity proof?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.teaching_text: Automated database checks flag unrecorded marriage or court name changes immediately and halt issuance at the window.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: When does an expired West Virginia license or an expired out-of-state license trigger full retesting?

sec02-card-sec02-F21.question_text: Which United States birth certificates prove identity, and which two records are rejected?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.teaching_text: Decorative hospital footprint sheets and census printouts fail verification because only government vital-records certificates carry legal authority.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.question_text: Which United States passport credentials count as acceptable proof of identity?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.teaching_text: An unexpired passport book or wallet-sized passport card satisfies your single identity proof cleanly.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.question_text: Which valid, unexpired federal documents let a foreign-born applicant prove identity?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.teaching_text: Unexpired green cards, work permits, naturalization certificates, consular birth reports, or visa-stamped passports with arrival records all work.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.question_text: What happens if your name or birth date conflicts with Social Security Administration records?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.teaching_text: Licensing clerks cannot override federal Social Security typos, so update Social Security first before testing.
sec02-card-sec02-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Fix mismatch before any card issues

visual_sync.text_span: Fix mismatch before any card issues

sec02-card-sec02-F26.question_text: What must an applicant submit if legally ineligible for a Social Security number?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.teaching_text: Certain visa holders cannot receive a number, so a formal letter from Social Security satisfies the requirement.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.question_text: Which original tax or payroll records prove your Social Security number besides the card itself, and what copy is rejected?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.teaching_text: Original Wage and Tax Statements, detailed pay stubs, or ten ninety-nine forms work, whereas photocopied tax forms fail.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.question_text: When must you bring legal name-change proof, and why does the state require it?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.teaching_text: Even if an earlier marriage ended years ago, licensing records must trace an unbroken chain from birth.
sec02-card-sec02-F28.must_match_memory_hook: Link every legal name ever used

sec02-card-sec02-F29.question_text: Which official records prove a legal name change, and which ceremonial wedding papers are rejected?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.teaching_text: Keepsake church certificates signed by a minister look official in scrapbooks yet lack courthouse filing authority.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: How do State Department and military birth certificates compare with hospital certificates and census records?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Americans born overseas on bases or embassies use State Department or military records rather than hospital keepsakes.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: How can an original Wage and Tax Statement cover two requirements, and what age cap or copy rule applies?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: One crisp original form within eighteen months proves both your Social Security number and one West Virginia address.
sec02-card-sec02-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Original under eighteen months counts twice

visual_sync.text_span: Original under eighteen months counts twice

sec02-card-sec02-F30.question_text: What four rules govern your two West Virginia residency proofs regarding boxes, bill age, and married spouses?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.teaching_text: Post office boxes never prove where you actually live, while a marriage certificate lets spouses share household bills.
sec02-card-sec02-F30.must_match_memory_hook: Two physical, ninety days, spouse allowed

visual_sync.text_span: Two physical, ninety days, spouse allowed

sec02-card-sec02-F31.question_text: Which household bills, registrations, financial papers, and employer stubs count toward West Virginia residency, and what utility or paystub traps fail?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.teaching_text: Shutoff termination notices and handwritten addresses on paychecks get rejected at the licensing window.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.question_text: Which school, emergency-address, postal, benefit, tax, or residential-facility letters also prove West Virginia residency?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.teaching_text: Students, shelter guests, nursing-home residents, and rural homeowners with newly assigned street numbers still have valid pathways.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.question_text: Why does West Virginia refuse to issue any license or identification card without an in-state physical address?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.teaching_text: State credentials certify actual West Virginia residency, so mailing drops without a physical home cannot qualify.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.question_text: May a former West Virginia resident who now lives in another state renew a West Virginia card?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.teaching_text: Once you move your home out of state, you must license where you live unless you move back.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.question_text: Once your two residency documents are scanned on file, when must you bring two residency proofs again?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.teaching_text: Staying at the same street address makes routine renewals quick without gathering fresh utility bills.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: How does the freshness deadline on recurring bills compare with a Wage and Tax Statement used for residency?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: Monthly utilities come out year-round, whereas annual tax forms only arrive once each winter.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: Why does one Post Office address fail residency while another Post Office letter passes?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: Renting a lobby mail box proves nothing about your home, whereas a postal letter assigning a new street address does.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.question_text: Besides first-time proofs, what credential or record must an out-of-state transfer applicant hand over, and how fresh must a record be?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.teaching_text: If you lost your plastic out-of-state card during the move, a certified driving record dated within thirty days substitutes.

sec02-card-sec02-F41.question_text: Which steps and screenings let a new resident transfer a valid, unexpired out-of-state license without road testing?
sec02-card-sec02-F41.teaching_text: Completing the brief alcohol awareness course and vision check lets valid newcomers skip repeating written and road exams.

sec02-card-sec02-F42.question_text: Within how many days of establishing residency must a newcomer apply to drive, and how does a motorcycle endorsement transfer?
sec02-card-sec02-F42.teaching_text: Remember thirty days for new state residents versus twenty days for moving within West Virginia.

sec02-card-sec02-F43.question_text: What happens if a newcomer's out-of-state license is expired over three years or cannot be physically produced?
sec02-card-sec02-F43.teaching_text: Producing a certified prior-state driving record waives testing when your valid wallet card went missing.

sec02-card-sec02-F44.question_text: What blocks a newcomer whose out-of-state license is suspended or revoked, and may they drive in West Virginia meanwhile?
sec02-card-sec02-F44.teaching_text: Driving anywhere in West Virginia while suspended in another state is unlawful until Problem Driver Point System clearance arrives.

sec02-card-sec02-F47.question_text: What happens when renewing any West Virginia license, including commercial, expired three years or more?
sec02-card-sec02-F47.teaching_text: Letting any license lapse three full years erases renewal shortcuts and requires full testing plus fresh identity proofs.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: In what year did West Virginia adopt the two-thousand-five federal licensing standards, and what is that program's goal?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Uniform document checks nationwide stop identity fraud and strengthen the integrity of state-issued cards.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: How does the thirty-day deadline for new state residents compare with the deadline for reporting an in-state move?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: New state residents get thirty days to apply, while existing drivers get twenty days in writing after moving.
sec02-card-sec02-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Thirty days new resident, twenty move

visual_sync.text_span: Thirty days new resident, twenty move

sec02-card-sec02-R11.question_text: When does transferring from another state waive exams, and when must the newcomer take every first-time test?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.teaching_text: Either a valid card or a certified record waives testing, unless the card expired past three years.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.question_text: Which national registry screens every West Virginia license applicant and renewing driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.teaching_text: Every issuance and renewal pings this interstate database to catch unpaid tickets or active suspensions nationwide.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.question_text: What must you do about pending citations or suspensions in another jurisdiction before getting or renewing a West Virginia license?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.teaching_text: State law bars licensing anyone carrying unresolved violations elsewhere, even from a vacation ticket years ago.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.question_text: How does West Virginia notify and penalize you when another state reports an unpaid citation, and how do you reinstate?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.teaching_text: Ignoring that certified letter suspends your West Virginia privilege until you bring official proof the court was satisfied.

sec02-card-sec02-F39.question_text: After paying off an overdue citation, should you expect the court to notify motor vehicle records automatically?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.teaching_text: Waiting around for an out-of-state court clerk to clear your file leaves your license suspended unnecessarily.

sec02-card-sec02-F45.question_text: How quickly must you report an address change in writing, what penalties apply, and does a Post Office forward work?
sec02-card-sec02-F45.teaching_text: Postal mail-forwarding neither updates state driver files nor forwards official licensing notices, risking missed suspension letters.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: What notice precedes suspension for an unpaid out-of-state ticket, and whose proof restores the license?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: Keep your address updated so certified warnings reach you before suspension hits, then hand-carry your payment receipt.
sec02-card-sec02-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Certified mail first, driver's proof restores

visual_sync.text_span: Certified mail first, driver's proof restores

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: What does a gold star printed on a West Virginia license or identification card signify?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: That gold star shows you completed full federal verification for domestic air travel and secure federal buildings.
sec02-card-sec02-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Approved for airports and federal sites

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: How long does a permanent license take to arrive by mail, and what lets you drive meanwhile?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Secure central printing ships cards to your verified address while your counter-issued temporary credential covers legal driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: No changes means just your current card and form, whereas moving takes two residency proofs and name changes need legal proof.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.question_text: Where can you request a duplicate for a lost, stolen, or destroyed license, and when are extra proofs needed?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.teaching_text: Unchanged info lets you replace a missing wallet card online, while name or address updates need fresh proofs.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.question_text: What documents must an applicant provide for a For Federal Use renewal or duplicate?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.teaching_text: Gold-star federal cards carry stricter verification rules than standard Not For Federal Use renewals.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.question_text: How much extra does a For Federal Use card cost, and how is it delivered?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.teaching_text: Budget an extra ten-dollar federal surcharge on top of standard fees while driving on your temporary paper receipt.

sec02-card-sec02-F46.teaching_text: Missing Social Security entries must be supplied and non-citizens must present current legal-status, identity, and residency papers.

sec02-card-sec02-F49.teaching_text: Permanent Resident Cards, translated temporary-resident stamps, or valid re-entry permits verify lawful permanent status.

sec02-card-sec02-F50.question_text: What passport, arrival, status, and school or work verification must a non-immigrant applicant bring alongside residency and Social Security items?

sec02-card-sec02-F51.question_text: Which arrival, assurance, and sponsor documents must a refugee with an approved sponsoring organization present?
sec02-card-sec02-F51.teaching_text: Written identity and residency verification from an approved sponsoring agency pairs with federal refugee arrival papers.

sec02-card-sec02-F52.question_text: What documents qualify an unsponsored refugee or asylum seeker alongside two residency proofs and Social Security or denial letter?
sec02-card-sec02-F52.teaching_text: Without a sponsoring agency letter, employment authorization documents pair with the refugee-or-asylee arrival record.
sec02-card-sec02-F52.must_match_memory_hook: Stamped arrival record plus work authorization

visual_sync.text_span: Stamped arrival record plus work authorization

sec02-card-sec02-R12.question_text: Which non-citizen applicant groups may substitute a Social Security denial letter, and which list requires the number itself?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.teaching_text: Permanent immigrants qualify for Social Security numbers, whereas certain non-immigrants and refugees may substitute official denial letters.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: What minimum age, written consent, and front-seat supervision rules govern a Level One graduated instruction permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Every practice drive requires a licensed driver at least twenty-one sitting right beside you in the front passenger seat.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: Which tests qualify a fifteen-year-old for a Level One permit, and what replaces parental consent for a married minor under eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Passing vision and knowledge exams unlocks the permit, while a certified marriage certificate stands in for parental signatures.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: Which two official credentials must you present every single time you apply and test for a Level One permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Even on a retake visit, forgetting your certified vital-records birth certificate or Social Security number stops testing cold.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: Between which daily hours may a Level One permit holder operate a vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Unlike intermediate drivers, instruction-permit teens have zero late-night driving allowance past ten at night.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: Besides the supervising licensed adult, how many non-family passengers may ride with a Level One permit holder?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Packing extra friends into the back seat multiplies cabin noise right while a beginner is learning traffic timing.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: What happens to a Level One instruction permit if the holder racks up two convictions?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Losing your permit for ninety days freezes practice hours and pushes back your intermediate road test.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: What blood alcohol standard and occupant restraint duty bind a Level One permit holder?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Any measurable trace of alcohol breaks zero tolerance, and every single rider in the car must buckle up.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: How much does each knowledge test attempt cost, and what is the printed fee here for the Level One permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Rushing into the exam unprepared charges another seven dollars and fifty cents on every single retake.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: Under what single emergency circumstance may a Level One permit holder use a wireless communication device while driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Even hands-free Bluetooth chats are off-limits for teen permit holders unless dialing emergency dispatch.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: Can a Level One permit be renewed, and what three things happen if you surrender it for any reason?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Handing back your permit wipes out accrued clean time, forcing fresh exams, fresh proofs, and one hundred eighty clean days.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: When does a Level One permit expire, and why does a thirty-day grace period follow?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: That extra thirty days past turning eighteen gives you breathing room to finish your road skills test.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: How do late-night driving rules between ten at night and five in the morning change from Level One to Level Two?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Stage one parks completely at ten, whereas intermediate teens can drive overnight when a twenty-one-plus adult rides along.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: How does reaching your eighteenth birthday on a Level One permit compare with surrendering it early?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Turning eighteen grants thirty days for road testing, while surrendering resets exams and one hundred eighty clean days.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: How does the Level Two limit on non-family passengers under twenty change after the first six months?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Solo focus comes first for six months before adding even a single non-family teen friend.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: How does the thirty-day birthday grace period for updating card color at eighteen or twenty-one differ from the Level One grace period?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Watch what the thirty days accomplish since swapping vertical red or blue cards differs from finishing road skills.
sec03-card-sec03-R10.must_match_memory_hook: Card color swap versus road exam

visual_sync.text_span: Card color swap versus road exam

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: What age span, clean-driving streak, and exam unlock a Level Two intermediate license?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Every single day of the preceding one hundred eighty days at Level One must stay completely conviction-free.
sec03-card-sec03-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Sixteen-to-eighteen, one-eighty clean days, road test

visual_sync.text_span: Sixteen-to-eighteen, one-eighty clean days, road test

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: What practice-hour log or school course qualifies a Level Two applicant, and what phone rule still applies?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Completing approved school driver education substitutes for the parent-certified fifty-hour log, while wireless bans stay strict.
sec03-card-sec03-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Fifty hours ten night, or driver-ed

visual_sync.text_span: Fifty hours ten night, or driver-ed

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: During which hours may a Level Two driver go solo, and when must a licensed adult twenty-one or older ride along?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Daytime and evening commutes run solo, while high-risk late hours from ten to five keep adult supervision.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: Which four trips let a Level Two driver operate past ten at night without a supervising adult?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Late restaurant shifts, varsity games, church events, and urgent injury-preventing emergencies are excused, whereas casual hangouts never qualify.
sec03-card-sec03-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Work school religion or life-saving emergency

visual_sync.text_span: Work school religion or life-saving emergency

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: Which non-family passengers are restricted during the first and second six-month halves at Level Two?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Crash statistics spike sharply with each young peer aboard, which is why household family members are treated differently.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: Which two safety mandates carry straight over from Level One into Level Two?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Earning solo daytime keys never relaxes West Virginia's zero-alcohol rule or whole-car seat-belt requirement.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: What happens if a driver under eighteen surrenders a Level Two intermediate license for any reason?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Surrendering before eighteen drops you all the way back to a beginner instruction permit.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: Which four items must you present each time you apply and test for a Level Two license?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Keep your fifty-hour log alongside your vital-records birth certificate, Social Security number, and licensing proofs for every attempt.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: How many conviction-free months are needed to move from Level One to Level Two, and what does a conviction do?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: One moving or phone conviction at month five wipes your streak and restarts a fresh six-month countdown.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: After two convictions revoke a Level One permit for ninety days, how do you get back on the road?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: Your permit does not automatically reactivate on day ninety-one because you must reapply and pass testing again.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.question_text: How long must a Level Two holder drive conviction-free to reach Level Three, and what happens after a conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.teaching_text: Advancing to full Class E privileges at seventeen demands an unbroken full year without a single conviction.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.question_text: What consequences hit after a first conviction versus a second moving-violation conviction at Level Two?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.teaching_text: Skipping driver improvement freezes you at Level Two until eighteen, while a second moving violation revokes until eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.question_text: How does a non-emergency wireless-device citation under age eighteen affect graduation clocks at Level One or Level Two?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.teaching_text: Checking a text resets six clean months at Level One or a full twelve months at Level Two.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.question_text: Must a seventeen-year-old who qualifies for Level Three upgrade right away?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.teaching_text: Eligible teens may either step up to Level Three at seventeen or stay on Level Two until turning eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.question_text: What age and clean-driving record unlock Level Three, and where must you apply?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.teaching_text: Graduating to Level Three requires visiting a Regional Office or Testing Center in person after twelve clean months.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: How do the required conviction-free windows compare between Level One and Level Two?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: Notice the clean-driving streak doubles once you start driving solo at the intermediate stage.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: How does the revocation penalty for two convictions at Level One compare with a second moving violation at Level Two?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Repeat violations while driving solo carry harsher consequences, revoking privileges all the way until age eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: Once a seventeen-year-old finishes twelve conviction-free months at Level Two, what two choices exist?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Families who want curfews and guest limits in place until eighteen can simply keep the Level Two card.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: Which electronic items are barred from the testing room, and who is allowed inside?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Phones, smart glasses, and Bluetooth earbuds stay completely out, and friends or parents wait outside the exam room.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: Who conducts official vision and knowledge exams, and what happens once you pass?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Passing both screenings with a designated driver examiner clears your paperwork for counter issuance.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: What minimum visual acuity in at least one eye qualifies an applicant for a West Virginia license?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Corrective glasses or contacts can bring you to twenty-forty, adding a lens restriction code to your card.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: Does passing the online written knowledge test give you immediate permission to drive?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Driving home with only an online test printout is unlicensed driving until an office processes your permit.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: What permit does an applicant eighteen or older earn after passing vision and knowledge exams, and who must ride up front?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Even adult learners holding a regular Class E permit need a licensed driver twenty-one or older up front.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: How long does a regular instruction permit stay valid, and what happens if it expires?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Letting six months slip past without passing your road test forces a full redo of vision and knowledge exams.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: How long must an adult permit holder never licensed at Level Two hold the instruction permit before road testing?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: First-time adult learners cannot walk out of the written exam and take the road test the same afternoon.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: For a regular adult instruction permit, how does total validity compare with the minimum wait before road testing?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Keep those two timelines distinct so you schedule road skills between day thirty and month six.
sec03-card-sec03-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Valid six months, wait thirty days

visual_sync.text_span: Valid six months, wait thirty days

sec03-card-sec03-R13.question_text: How does the online Know to Drive test differ from testing with a designated driver examiner?
sec03-card-sec03-R13.teaching_text: Online testing completes only one step from home, whereas office processing and vision checks activate real privileges.

sec03-card-sec03-F38.question_text: Under West Virginia's Drive for Five program, in which years does a driver's license expire?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.teaching_text: Tying renewals to ages like twenty-five, thirty, and thirty-five keeps standard licenses on a clean five-year rhythm.
sec03-card-sec03-F38.must_match_memory_hook: Expires when age divides by five

visual_sync.text_span: Expires when age divides by five

sec03-card-sec03-F39.question_text: For how many years may an initial license run when aligning a driver's age with the five-year cycle?
sec03-card-sec03-F39.teaching_text: Issuing between three and seven years lines your next renewal right onto an age divisible by five.

sec03-card-sec03-F40.question_text: On what exact calendar day do modern West Virginia licenses expire, and which two birthdays add a thirty-day color grace period?
sec03-card-sec03-F40.teaching_text: Do not assume you have until month's end, because expiration hits right on your birthday.
sec03-card-sec03-F40.must_match_memory_hook: Expires on birthday, eighteen twenty-one grace

visual_sync.text_span: Expires on birthday, eighteen twenty-one grace

sec03-card-sec03-F41.question_text: What per-year rate sets renewal fees, and what does a twenty-one-year-old pay through age twenty-five?
sec03-card-sec03-F41.teaching_text: Four years from twenty-one to twenty-five times five dollars per year equals a twenty-dollar renewal.
sec03-card-sec03-F41.must_match_memory_hook: Five dollars yearly, twenty at twenty-one

visual_sync.text_span: Five dollars yearly, twenty at twenty-one

sec03-card-sec03-F42.question_text: Which male applicants can register with Selective Service on the back of a license, permit, or photo card form?
sec03-card-sec03-F42.teaching_text: Checking the application box handles federal Selective Service registration automatically during routine licensing.

sec03-card-sec03-F43.question_text: Which three health or hearing conditions can an applicant print on a card by marking the back of the application?
sec03-card-sec03-F43.teaching_text: Alerting paramedics or officers right on your card prevents dangerous confusion during medical emergencies or stops.

sec03-card-sec03-F44.question_text: How do you update organ-donor registry status online versus changing the donor symbol printed on your physical card?
sec03-card-sec03-F44.teaching_text: Online registry edits take effect anytime, whereas reprinting the plastic card itself requires buying a replacement.

sec03-card-sec03-F45.question_text: Which discharge, military card, or license-plate records verify honorable discharge for a veterans designation?
sec03-card-sec03-F45.teaching_text: Honorable discharge forms, military identification cards, or verified military plate registrations confirm eligibility cleanly.

sec03-card-sec03-F47.question_text: On the printed fee table, what fees apply to Level One at fifteen, Level Two at sixteen, and Level Three at seventeen versus eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F47.teaching_text: Notice the fee table lists five dollars on the first two stages, then two-fifty yearly at seventeen versus five at eighteen.
sec03-card-sec03-F47.must_match_memory_hook: Five, five, then two-fifty or five

visual_sync.text_span: Five, five, then two-fifty or five

sec03-card-sec03-F48.question_text: What fees apply to an adult permit, Class E yearly plus expired fee, Class F yearly, a duplicate, and a knowledge test?
sec03-card-sec03-F48.teaching_text: Group the three seven-fifty flat fees together, keep Class E at five yearly, and Class F at two-fifty yearly.

sec03-card-sec03-F49.question_text: How much extra does it cost to obtain, renew, or duplicate a For Federal Identification card?
sec03-card-sec03-F49.teaching_text: That ten-dollar surcharge applies not only at initial issuance, because renewals and duplicates add ten dollars too.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: Why can your very first license under Drive for Five run anywhere from three to seven years instead of exactly five?
