sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Adjusting the first term once puts every future renewal squarely on birthdays divisible by five.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: Why do two drivers pay different renewal totals even though the five-dollar yearly rate stays identical?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: Paying strictly for the exact number of years until your next divisible-by-five birthday keeps pricing fair.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.question_text: How does the per-year fee for a Level Three license change if first issued at seventeen versus eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.teaching_text: Waiting until eighteen doubles the yearly rate on the fee table from two dollars and fifty cents to five dollars.
sec03-card-sec03-R11.must_match_memory_hook: Two-fifty at seventeen, five at eighteen

visual_sync.text_span: Two-fifty at seventeen, five at eighteen

sec03-card-sec03-F34.question_text: When must a teen under eighteen transferring from out of state take both knowledge and road skills tests like a brand-new applicant?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.teaching_text: Out-of-state permits or jurisdictions without equivalent graduated standards require full West Virginia testing.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.question_text: How does bringing a current prior-state driving record help an under-eighteen transfer applicant?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.teaching_text: Documented months held elsewhere count toward your Level One holding window and merge into your West Virginia record.
sec03-card-sec03-F35.must_match_memory_hook: Credits prior time toward Level One

visual_sync.text_span: Credits prior time toward Level One

sec03-card-sec03-F36.question_text: Where do restriction codes and explanations appear on a West Virginia license, and what can breaking one cause?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.teaching_text: Driving without required glasses or outside restricted hours is a serious violation risking suspension or revocation.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.question_text: Which vision, vehicle-equipment, time-of-day, or medical restrictions appear on the handbook's list?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.teaching_text: Tailored restrictions let drivers with corrective lenses, hand controls, or daylight-only limits operate safely.

sec03-card-sec03-F46.question_text: To whom must you produce your license on demand, what offense is failing, and how do you avoid conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-F46.teaching_text: Forgetting your wallet is a misdemeanor stop, yet presenting a license valid at arrest clears the conviction.
sec03-card-sec03-F46.must_match_memory_hook: Show valid license later avoids conviction

visual_sync.text_span: Show valid license later avoids conviction

sec03-card-sec03-F50.question_text: Along with your driver's license, which two vehicle documents must stay aboard and be shown during a moving-violation stop?
sec03-card-sec03-F50.teaching_text: Check that current registration and West Virginia insurance proof sit in the car before borrowing any family vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.question_text: When does a misdemeanor charge for failing to produce your license end with zero conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.teaching_text: Only an already-valid license qualifies, so getting licensed after the traffic stop will not erase the charge.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: At least how many items appear on West Virginia's knowledge screening, and what topics do they cover?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Every prompt pulls from core driving rules, regulations, road signs, and pavement markings covered in the manual.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: How many of twenty-five knowledge items must be right to pass, and how are timed-out blanks scored?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Automated terminals run a strict countdown, so leaving items blank when time expires docks your score directly.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: Who may use the headphone audio version, what may DMV staff never do, and why might you wait?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Limited headsets serve reading-impaired applicants under identical rules where counter staff cannot explain or rephrase prompts.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: How do the twenty-five minimum count, nineteen passing mark, and countdown timer interact?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Pacing yourself keeps easy points from turning into automatic misses if the clock runs out.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: Why are DMV employees barred from reading, rewording, or explaining prompts on both audio and printed versions?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Holding headphone and screen applicants to uniform standards ensures every permit holder proves independent comprehension.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: What visual acuity must new and renewing applicants meet, and what three extra visual traits may be checked?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Alongside twenty-forty clarity with or without standard glasses, examiners may check depth, color, and side vision.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: May applicants wear bi-optic or telescopic lenses to pass West Virginia's visual acuity standard?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Conventional glasses or contacts are permitted, whereas mounted telescopic or bi-optic optics cannot satisfy state acuity.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: When is a corrective-lenses restriction added, and how can an applicant with sight in one eye pass?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Relying on contacts or frames adds a mandatory lens code, while a single functioning eye passes at twenty-forty.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: What steps follow when an applicant falls short of twenty-forty acuity or shows a serious visual defect?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: When standard lenses cannot reach twenty-forty, a licensed eye doctor must detail the condition and safe restrictions.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: Which body may review a vision specialist's statement at the Commissioner's discretion before licensing?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Complex visual impairments receive medical-board evaluation before the Commissioner approves a restricted permit or card.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: How does West Virginia's twenty-forty standard treat two eyes, one eye, and bi-optic or telescopic optics?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Either binocular sight or a single strong eye passes at twenty-forty provided only conventional lenses are worn.
sec06-card-sec06-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Two or one twenty-forty, no telescopic

visual_sync.text_span: Two or one twenty-forty, no telescopic

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: What separates getting a simple corrective-lenses code from needing a specialist's statement and possible board review?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Glasses that achieve twenty-forty earn a routine restriction code, whereas uncorrectable sight requires specialist documentation.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: Which legal standards and documents must your road-skills vehicle meet, and what can defects cause?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Showing up with expired stickers, missing insurance proof, or broken equipment can end your driving evaluation immediately.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: If a minor vehicle issue turns up before driving, what may the examiner allow and what swap is barred?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Replacing a bulb on the spot can save your appointment, whereas borrowing a second car that day is prohibited.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: What happens if an applicant cannot locate and demonstrate every safety control, including the parking brake?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Fumbling for wipers, defrosters, lights, or the emergency brake proves you are not ready for solo traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: Which flashing colors, noise devices, window items, and extra spotlights count as illegal vehicle equipment?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Red or blue flashers, sirens, cutout mufflers, unauthorized glass decals, or two-plus spotlights violate state equipment law.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: What limits govern side cowl lights, backup lamps, forward-lit reverse lights, and cargo past fenders?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Overhanging cargo on the driver's left clips oncoming traffic, while white reverse lamps lit forward confuse followers.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: Which windshield, window-tint transmission, lens, and body or door defects make a vehicle illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Tint darker than thirty-five percent light transmission, cracked glass, body rust holes, or jammed doors fail inspection.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: How do fixing a minor car defect and switching to another vehicle on the same date differ?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Inspecting tires, brake lamps, and paperwork before leaving home avoids losing your scheduled driving slot.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: What are the maximum legal counts for spotlights, side cowl lamps, and backup lights, plus reverse-light behavior?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Capping auxiliary lamps and keeping white backup bulbs dark while moving forward prevents blinding glare.
sec06-card-sec06-R05.must_match_memory_hook: One spot, two cowl, two reverse

visual_sync.text_span: One spot, two cowl, two reverse

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: Why do left-side and right-side cargo overhang limits differ at zero inches versus six inches past fenders?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Left-side cargo juts toward fast oncoming mirrors on two-lane roads, whereas right-side clearance faces the shoulder.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: What minimum light percentage must window tint pass, and does legal tint excuse cracked glass or broken lenses?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Even factory-clear windows fail equipment rules if the windshield is cracked or lamp lenses are shattered.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: Which five driver qualifications does West Virginia's licensing evaluation measure against state standards?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Screening eyesight, sign and law mastery, and live traffic handling ensures new drivers protect everyone sharing highways.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: What is the examiner watching during your drive, and why shouldn't a clipboard mark rattle you?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Staring at the score sheet steals focus from traffic when routine tallies do not automatically mean mistakes.
sec06-card-sec06-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Focus driving, marks aren't always errors

visual_sync.text_span: Focus driving, marks aren't always errors

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: How well does the West Virginia DMV ask every licensed motorist to drive once licensed?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Dropping safe habits the afternoon you pass turns licensing day from a baseline into a hazard.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: Who must complete the short DUI awareness course after road skills, and how is completion recorded?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Even incoming out-of-state motorists who previously held a West Virginia card need the course card or application stamp.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: Does holding a West Virginia license years ago exempt an incoming out-of-state driver from DUI awareness?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Both brand-new drivers and returning out-of-state transfers complete the brief DUI awareness step after passing skills.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: Why must drivers memorize traffic sign shapes and colors rather than relying on printed words alone?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Snow, heavy rain, fog, or night glare can blur lettering while outer silhouettes and colors stay recognizable.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: Which sign uses the eight-sided octagon exclusively, and what two actions does it require?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Locking your wheels briefly is only step one because walkers and cross-street cars still hold priority.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: Where do you halt at a stop sign when a crosswalk exists versus when no markings or crosswalk exist?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Halting behind marked or unmarked walkways protects pedestrians, while unmarked corners require stopping before entering with clear sightlines.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: What right-of-way duty does an upside-down triangular traffic sign impose?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Pointing downward sets yield panels apart from every other shape so cross-street drivers know who gives way.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: What roadway restriction begins right at a pennant-shaped traffic sign?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Sideways yellow pennants warn overtaking drivers early that sightlines ahead drop below safe passing distance.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: What hazard ahead is announced by a circular yellow-and-black road sign?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Spotting the round yellow warning early lets you quiet the cabin, listen for horns, and cover the brake.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: What does a five-sided pentagon sign mark, and how far along abutting streets does a West Virginia school zone reach?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: West Virginia school speed rules begin one hundred twenty-five feet outside campus grounds along bordering roads.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: What is West Virginia's maximum school-zone speed limit, and under what two triggers does it apply?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Dropping down to fifteen whenever students are present or posted hours apply gives stopping margin for darting kids.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: Which two vehicle situations are marked by an upright triangle with a red border and fluorescent orange center?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Closing at highway pace on farm gear or a roadside breakdown demands immediate braking when orange-and-red appears.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: How does the required driver action differ between an eight-sided octagon and an upside-down triangle?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Rolling through an octagon gets ticketed even on an empty street, whereas an inverted triangle requires yielding conflicts.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: Which two high-risk zones are separated by round yellow-and-black signs versus five-sided pentagon signs?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Keeping circular rail warnings distinct from house-shaped school pentagons sharpens instant hazard recognition in fog.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: How does a sideways no-passing pennant differ from an upright red-bordered orange triangle?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Roadside pennants govern overtaking sightlines, while vehicle-mounted orange triangles flag slow or emergency-stopped rigs.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: How do the hundred-twenty-five-foot school boundary and the fifteen-mile-per-hour speed cap work together?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Slowing to fifteen before crossing the hundred-twenty-five-foot campus buffer keeps you legal from the very edge.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: What do square and rectangular signs regulate, and how do white, solid red, and diagonal-bar red designs differ?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Black-on-white posts routine speed or lane rules, white-on-red shouts critical commands, and red slashes forbid actions.
sec07-card-sec07-F10.must_match_memory_hook: White regulates, red urgent, slash bans

visual_sync.text_span: White regulates, red urgent, slash bans

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: Where does a No U-Turn sign forbid turning your vehicle around?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Looping around across busy lanes or tight corners blocks oncoming traffic from both directions.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: What do No Right Turn and No Left Turn signs prohibit, and at what two intersection setups are they placed?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Engineers post turn bans wherever turning would send you wrong-way down a one-way street or across blind conflicts.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: What danger awaits any motorist who drives past Wrong Way or Do Not Enter signs?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Entering off-ramps or one-way lanes against posted red warnings puts oncoming traffic straight ahead of your hood.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: How is a highway lane beneath a Dual Turn Lane sign shared, and what maneuver is strictly prohibited inside it?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Opposing traffic enters the same middle bay for left turns, turning any overtaking attempt into a head-on collision.
sec07-card-sec07-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Both ways turn left, zero passing

visual_sync.text_span: Both ways turn left, zero passing

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: Where along divided highways stand lane direction signs, and what mistake do they prevent?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Signs inside median breaks keep turning drivers from accidentally steering onto the wrong half of a divided highway.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: What does a One Way sign reveal about a cross street, and how are consecutive downtown blocks usually arranged?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Knowing adjacent city blocks typically alternate directions helps you plan legal turns without circling blind.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: How do white highway speed-limit signs differ from black-on-yellow ramp advisory speed signs?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: White boards set legal maximums or minimums for ideal roads, while yellow ramp plaques warn of tight exit curves.
sec07-card-sec07-F17.must_match_memory_hook: Optimal legal max versus ramp advice

visual_sync.text_span: Optimal legal max versus ramp advice

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: How do black-on-white, white-on-red, and red-circle-with-bar regulatory panels rank urgency and bans?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Color coding lets your eyes separate standard speed caps from urgent stop-or-wrong-way bans in split seconds.
sec07-card-sec07-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Routine law, urgent alert, flat ban

visual_sync.text_span: Routine law, urgent alert, flat ban

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: What separates a regulatory speed-limit sign from a black-on-yellow ramp advisory sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Regulatory white limits state maximum legal speed under ideal conditions, while yellow ramp numbers prevent curve rollovers.
sec07-card-sec07-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Legal cap versus recommended ramp pace

visual_sync.text_span: Legal cap versus recommended ramp pace

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: How does an overhead Dual Turn Lane sign differ in purpose from a lane direction sign at a median opening?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Dual-turn plaques govern shared center left-turn bays, whereas divider-opening plaques keep crossers out of wrong-way lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: How are standard diamond warning signs styled, and which two hazard types may use yellow-green instead?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Wordless black pictograms on yellow read fast at highway pace, while fluorescent yellow-green spotlights schools and walkers.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: What does a curve or sharp-turn warning tell you about regular highway speed, and what plaque may sit below it?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Carrying open-highway speed into a tight mountain bend pushes tires wide, so match any attached advisory plaque.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: What traffic movement must you watch for at a crossroads or side-road warning sign?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Unseen cars pulling out or slowing abruptly to turn off rural highways create sudden rear-end and T-bone risks.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: How do lane-ending, added-lane, and merge warning diamonds differ in what happens ahead?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Knowing whether traffic gets its own fresh lane or squeezes into yours tells you when to adjust speed.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: What roadway flow does a two-way traffic warning sign announce?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Transitioning off a divided highway onto an undivided two-lane road puts oncoming headlights directly beside your lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: What specific hazards and responses match hill, low-clearance, and slippery-when-wet warning signs?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Slowing before steep West Virginia grades, checking roof height at bridges, and easing speed on slick stretches prevents wrecks.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: What duties follow a pedestrian-crossing warning versus a signal-ahead warning?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Scanning curbs for people on foot and easing speed before blind intersections stops sudden panic braking.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: Which two specific warning subjects switch from standard yellow diamonds to yellow-green with black markings?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Fluorescent yellow-green stands out in dawn, dusk, and rainy shade wherever children or walkers cross streets.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: What shapes and basic background color identify construction and maintenance work-zone signs?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Bright orange immediately signals temporary work hazards where lanes narrow, surfaces roughen, and crews walk nearby.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: Which five channeling devices steer traffic through work zones, and what helps drivers see them after dark?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Mounted steady-burn or flashing lamps outline temporary lane shifts clearly through nighttime highway work.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: What two messages do large flashing or sequencing arrow panels deliver day and night in work zones?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Bright sequential arrows give long-range notice to merge smoothly out of a closed highway lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: How do diagonal stripes on a work-zone barricade or vertical panel show which side to pass on?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Imagine rolling a ball down the stripes—sloping down right means bear right, and down left means bear left.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: What high-visibility clothing and handheld tools do work-zone flaggers use to control traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Spotting orange vests, shirts, or jackets with red-orange flags or STOP-SLOW paddles means obey crew instructions.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: Which way do you steer when barricade stripes slope downward right versus downward left?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Misreading barricade diagonals steers tires straight onto closed shoulders or open pavement trenches.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: How can you still decode an unfamiliar road sign that never appeared in the driver handbook?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Standardized colors, outer shapes, and intuitive symbols make even brand-new roadside signs understandable on sight.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: What navigation questions do guide signs answer, and what four subtypes belong in the guide family?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Knowing your current road, location, services, and mileage keeps long trips smooth without phone distractions.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: Which background colors pair with white lettering for directional guides, motorist services, and parks?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Color-coded guide boards let drivers filter exit ramps for directions, fuel, or recreation at seventy miles hourly.
sec07-card-sec07-F32.must_match_memory_hook: Green direction, blue services, brown parks

visual_sync.text_span: Green direction, blue services, brown parks

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: What details appear on intersection guide signs, interstate exit signs, and advance interstate signs?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Reading advance exit numbers and distances early lets you move into the deceleration lane without cutting traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.question_text: What helpful details do highway distance signs and amenity or rest-area guide signs display?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.teaching_text: Knowing how far the next town or designated rest stop sits helps fatigued drivers plan safe breaks.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: How do West Virginia and U.S. highway route markers differ in color from interstate shields?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: Distinguishing black-and-white U.S. or state shields from tricolor interstate shields prevents taking the wrong numbered corridor.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: What travel categories correspond to white-on-green, white-on-blue, and white-on-brown signs?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Matching green to routes, blue to food or hospitals, and brown to parks locks down easy written points.
sec07-card-sec07-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Directions green, services blue, parks brown

visual_sync.text_span: Directions green, services blue, parks brown

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: What color difference separates state and U.S. route markers from interstate route markers?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Identical route numbers can exist across state, federal, and interstate networks, so shield colors confirm your highway.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: What speed standard does West Virginia enforce alongside posted signs, and which road types receive statutory defaults?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Rain, fog, or heavy traffic can make driving the posted number unlawful whenever current conditions demand slower travel.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: What are West Virginia's four default speed limits for interstates, open county highways, business or residential streets, and active school zones?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Memorizing this four-step ladder covers the core statutory speed questions on the West Virginia knowledge exam.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: What property and how much adjoining street distance make up a legal West Virginia school zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Drivers who wait until passing the school building to slow down are already well inside the legal enforcement boundary.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: Under what three conditions may an authorized emergency vehicle exceed posted speed limits?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Active sirens and strobes never grant responders a blank check to endanger surrounding motorists or pedestrians.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: How does West Virginia's unposted interstate speed limit compare with an open county highway?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Two-lane county routes carry unmarked curves, farm entrances, and oncoming traffic absent from divided interstates.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How does the designated speed limit drop when moving from business or residential streets into a school zone with children present?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Shaving ten miles per hour when students walk near the curb dramatically shortens stopping distance if a child darts out.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: Which vehicles alone may legally exceed a posted limit, and what safeguards still bind them?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Private drivers rushing to personal emergencies never share statutory speed exemptions reserved for equipped duty responders.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: What assumption do surrounding motorists make about your path, and how do turn signals protect you?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Early blinking gives nearby drivers crucial seconds to ease off the gas or hold their lane before you move.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: Before which five everyday maneuvers must you activate your turn signal?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Drivers often forget that pulling away from a curb or easing onto a shoulder requires the exact same signal discipline.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: How far ahead must you signal a turn, and why must you cancel the blinker afterward?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Cruising down the road with a forgotten blinker tricks cross-street drivers into pulling out right across your bow.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: What happens if you signal too early or too late for a turn located right past an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Waiting until you enter or clear the cross street prevents waiting side-street cars from assuming you will turn early.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: Which left-arm positions communicate slow or stop, right turn, and left turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Knowing manual arm cues keeps you communicating if a bulb burns out and helps you read cyclists ahead.
sec09-card-sec09-F15.must_match_memory_hook: Down stop, up right, straight left

visual_sync.text_span: Down stop, up right, straight left

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: Why must you balance the one-hundred-foot signal rule carefully when turning into an entrance right past an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Blinking before the crossroad convinces side-street traffic you are turning early, luring them directly into your path.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: Match left-arm down, left-arm up, and left-arm straight out to their exact meanings?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Permit tests routinely scramble arm-up and arm-down choices to catch applicants who guess instead of visualizing.
sec09-card-sec09-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Down slow, up right, out left

visual_sync.text_span: Down slow, up right, out left

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: Why must every driver both obey posted speed limits and adapt speed to changing conditions?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Excess velocity magnifies crash energy exponentially while stealing precious margin from everyone sharing the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: At which four roadway features and under what visibility or traction conditions should you reduce speed?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Cresting blind hills or rounding tight mountain bends at full speed leaves nowhere to stop if hazards block the lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: How does climbing speed shrink your ability to handle your own mistakes or another driver's error?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Faster travel compresses the seconds available to spot danger, gauge closing rates, and steer or brake cleanly.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: How does the West Virginia manual sum up its simple safety rule for speed?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Combining sign compliance with real-time weather and traffic judgment keeps stopping distance inside your clear view.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: Where on the roadway should you position your vehicle whenever moving slower than normal traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Staying near the right edge opens clear sightlines and passing room so faster traffic does not bunch aggressively behind you.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: What must you do when driving below the designated speed on a two-lane road with no clear passing lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Stacking frustrated drivers behind a slow vehicle on winding West Virginia two-lanes provokes reckless blind-curve passes.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: Where should your left and right hands grip the steering wheel, and what two benefits does that placement give?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Holding high at ten and two risks broken wrists or facial injuries if a steering-hub airbag deploys in a crash.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: Why can you still receive a speeding citation while driving below the posted number?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Slick snow, dense fog, or backed-up traffic lowers the legal prudent speed well underneath dry-weather sign numbers.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: How do right-edge positioning and safe turnouts work together when you drive slower than traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Keeping right handles multilane roads while pulling into turnouts clears bottlenecks on narrow mountain two-lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: Which clock positions mark West Virginia's recommended steering grip, and what safety device drives that lower placement?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Keeping forearms below the center horn pad lets an inflating front airbag cushion your chest unimpeded.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: Aside from traffic conflicts or officer orders, which five everyday spots forbid stopping, standing, or parking, including hydrant footage?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Even sitting behind the wheel idling inside fifteen feet of a hydrant or across a sidewalk breaks West Virginia law.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: What no-parking distances apply at corner crosswalks, stop signs or signals, and railroad rails, plus curb cuts?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Setbacks keep corner sightlines open and ensure wheelchair ramps and rail crossings stay completely unobstructed.
sec10-card-sec10-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Twenty crosswalk, thirty sign, fifty rail

visual_sync.text_span: Twenty crosswalk, thirty sign, fifty rail

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: Where is parking banned around street work, curb-parked cars, bridges or tunnels, and daily-delivery mailboxes?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: West Virginia specifically protects twenty feet around carrier-served mailboxes so postal vehicles can reach boxes cleanly.
sec10-card-sec10-F15.must_match_memory_hook: No work zones, bridges, twenty-foot mail

visual_sync.text_span: No work zones, bridges, twenty-foot mail

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: Where on highways is parking prohibited, and what curb paint color signals a no-parking zone?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Controlled-access shoulders serve breakdowns only, and yellow curb paint warns drivers away even before spotting a post sign.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: List the four climbing no-parking distances from fire hydrant to corner crosswalk, stop sign, and railroad rail?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Grouping all four numbers in ascending order makes West Virginia distance-setback test items effortless to recall.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: What mailbox buffer, elevated or enclosed structures, highway class, and curb color all forbid parking?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Exam writers love pairing the twenty-foot rural mailbox rule alongside yellow curbs and controlled-access highways.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: Why must every motorist master proper turning procedures, and who suffers most in turn crashes?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Pedestrians and bike riders share corner crosswalks and curb lanes with zero steel cage to absorb a careless swing.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: Instead of diving late, what three checks come before moving into a turning lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Cyclists and faster curb-lane cars sit right inside side-mirror blind zones when drivers veer abruptly toward a corner.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: How far ahead must you signal a turn, and when should your braking happen?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Shedding speed in a straight line keeps tire grip balanced, whereas braking mid-corner can trigger a front-wheel slide.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: What traffic and pedestrian checks precede a turn, and where must the maneuver end?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Finishing squarely inside the proper corresponding lane prevents sideswiping adjacent drivers turning or cruising nearby.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: What must you do when turning left if oncoming traffic will reach the intersection around the same moment?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Trying to beat straight-through traffic across the box causes high-energy T-bone impacts on your passenger side.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: Why must your front wheels stay pointed straight ahead while stopped waiting to turn left?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: A distracted rear-end tap pushes straight wheels forward in your lane instead of launching you into oncoming traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: When are right turns on red and left turns on red permitted in West Virginia?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Left on red works only when leaving a one-way street onto another one-way street with no prohibitory sign.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: Where do curves, hill crests, visibility distance, and signs make turning your vehicle around unlawful?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Blocking both lanes mid-turnaround inside a blind dip or curve leaves approaching highway traffic zero room to stop.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: How much clear visibility in both directions is required to turn around near a curve or hill crest?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Even with clear sightlines, posted no-U-turn signs still override and forbid turning around at busy intersections.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: Combine wheel angle and oncoming-traffic timing for waiting safely to turn left?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Holding straight tires protects you from rear impacts while patient yielding clears fast opposing traffic cleanly.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: How far out from parked cars do you line up to angle park on the right, and when do you cut in?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Staying at least five feet out gives your right rear fender room to clear the neighboring bumper cleanly.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: What three precautions apply when backing out of a visibility-blocked angle parking stall?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Adjacent pickups block cross-aisle sightlines, and backing across the street's center line puts you into opposing traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: Which way do you turn front wheels when parking downhill, uphill with a curb, and uphill without a curb?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Only uphill beside a raised curb turns left so the tire catches the curb; every other slope turns right.
sec10-card-sec10-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Down in, up-curb out, curbless right

visual_sync.text_span: Down in, up-curb out, curbless right

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: Along with setting the parking brake on a grade, which gear holds an automatic versus a manual car?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Choosing the gear opposite gravity locks engine compression behind the parking brake if cables stretch.
sec10-card-sec10-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Park automatic, reverse down, first up

visual_sync.text_span: Park automatic, reverse down, first up

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: Within how many inches of the curb must parallel-parked wheels rest, and how must the vehicle sit?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Centering inside the stall within eighteen inches keeps doors and fenders clear of passing traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: Where do you stop beside the front car to start parallel parking, and which way do wheels turn first?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Looking directly over your shoulder while backing slowly prevents clipping the parked car's rear corner.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: When do you swing the wheel full left during parallel parking, and what ideal versus maximum curb gap applies?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Counter-steering once your front bumper clears their rear bumper tucks the nose neatly about six inches off the curb.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: What two steps are mandatory every time you leave a parallel parking stall?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Parked cars start from zero velocity, so pulling out without a blinker and clear gap invites immediate sideswipes.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: Contrast front-wheel direction for downhill, uphill with a curb, and uphill without a curb?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Permit exams love testing uphill without a curb because turning left there would roll a car across center.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: What starting side gap, ideal finished curb distance, and legal maximum curb distance frame parallel parking?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Keeping those three measurements straight nails both the written permit test and the road-skills parallel box.
sec10-card-sec10-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Two feet, six ideal, eighteen max

visual_sync.text_span: Two feet, six ideal, eighteen max

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: What minimum clearance starts an angle-parking entry, and what line must your exit never cross?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Wide entry setup prevents scraping parked bumpers going in, and staying on your half prevents head-on hits backing out.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: Which transmission position backs up the parking brake on downhill versus uphill grades for manual and automatic cars?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: Manual drivers who leave stick shifts in neutral lose engine braking completely if the handbrake slips.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: Which space zone is easiest to control, what crash type stems from tailgating, and what shapes safe distance?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: You cannot force a tailgater back directly, whereas lifting your right foot expands your front stopping cushion instantly.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: How do you measure the three-to-four second following rule using a roadside landmark?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: Reaching the signpost or overpass before finishing one-thousand-three proves your stopping buffer is dangerously short.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: How many seconds of following distance should you keep in darkness or rain versus on ice or snow?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: Frozen pavement multiplies stopping distance while glare and spray delay spotting brake lights ahead.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: Compare minimum following counts for normal conditions, darkness or rain, and ice or snow?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Time-based cushions automatically add extra footage as highway speeds climb, adapting smoothly across every road.
sec10-card-sec10-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Three-to-four normal, four wet, six icy

visual_sync.text_span: Three-to-four normal, four wet, six icy

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: What walk-around and head-turn habits apply before and during backing?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Rearview mirrors leave wide low blind zones right behind the trunk where toddlers, pets, or shopping carts sit.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: What is the sole acceptable reason to reverse in a traffic lane, and where is backing strictly forbidden?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Reversing after missing a turn shocks trailing drivers who expect every car in a travel lane to roll forward.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: How must a parked car face and clear the roadway, and how does West Virginia treat double parking?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Crossing oncoming lanes to park left-wheels-to-curb on a two-way street creates head-on conflicts going in and out.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: What four steps secure a parked car when leaving, and what must you scan before opening a street-side door?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Swinging a driver door open blindly can knock a passing cyclist or motorcyclist under moving traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: What convenience tip applies to parking meters, and how should you protect yourself when sitting parked in busy areas?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Staying alert with doors locked prevents opportunistic carjacking or theft while waiting inside busy urban lots.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: Contrast the one acceptable live-lane backing move against the two backing moves banned everywhere?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: If you overshoot an exit or corner, drive around the block rather than reversing across active lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: How should you respond when another motorist ignores right-of-way rules, and why?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Insisting on your turn against an aggressive or distracted driver trades two seconds of patience for twisted sheet metal.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: Who must yield when pulling onto a public road out of a driveway, private lane, or alley?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Main-road motorists expect uninterrupted flow and lack stopping margin when vehicles nose out from side aprons.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: Who yields when two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection or a four-way stop together?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Giving priority to the vehicle on your right breaks four-way standoffs cleanly without hesitant lurching.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: What speed and right-of-way duties apply as you approach an intersection controlled by a yield sign?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Easing off the gas ahead of the triangle sign lets you stop smoothly if cross traffic fills the box.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: Which stream of traffic holds right-of-way whenever you prepare to turn left?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Cutting across opposing lanes forces straight-through drivers into emergency braking inside the intersection box.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: What complete sequence applies when an ambulance, fire rig, or police cruiser approaches with siren and lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Keeping your foot on the brake lights your tail lamps so the responder sees immediately that your car stays put.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: Is yielding to a funeral procession law or courtesy in West Virginia, and when may you pass one?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Once the lead escort clears an intersection, staying out of the line keeps mourners together while multilane expressways allow passing.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: What happens when a police officer's hand directions conflict with a posted sign, signal, or lane marking?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Live officers see crash debris, utility hazards, or emergency routes that automated signal timers cannot detect.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: How should you treat a driver parallel parking ahead of you, and what simple rule guides right-of-way?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Crowding a bumper blocks the angle needed to back into a curb stall, trapping both of you in traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: Compare who yields in an uncontrolled or four-way tie versus at a posted yield sign?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: A red-and-white triangle assigns full yielding duty to your approach regardless of which side cross traffic comes from.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: Contrast your legal duty toward an emergency vehicle running siren and lights against a funeral procession?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Exam questions test that emergency vehicles mandate pulling right and stopping, whereas funeral lines rely on courtesy.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: Pair the authority that overrides every traffic control with the core mindset of right-of-way?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Following live officer cues and surrendering contested space willingly prevents intersection standoffs and crashes.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: Who yields when pulling from a driveway, alley, or private road, and who yields on a left turn?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Both maneuvers cross active straight-through lanes whose drivers carry full roadway speed and priority.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: Where do blind sightlines and intersections prohibit overtaking?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Cross-street turns and hidden oncoming traffic inside hills or bends leave zero escape path in the opposing lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: Within what distance of bridges, viaducts, tunnels, underpasses, or railroad crossings is passing banned?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Narrow bridge decks, dark tunnel portals, and active rail tracks strip away shoulder room right when passing cars need space.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: Which four traffic, sign, pedestrian, and centerline situations also forbid passing?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Swinging around a car stopped at a corner often strikes the hidden pedestrian stepping across its hood.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: Compare the distance buffer for bridges, tunnels, and rail crossings with the rule for a solid yellow line in your lane?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Even far away from bridges or tracks, a solid yellow stripe on your side forbids crossing center anywhere along it.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: What zone, following cushion, and speed question should you check before passing on a two-lane highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: If overtaking requires breaking the speed limit, the car ahead is already moving fast enough to stay behind.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: Where must you look, what roadside hazards should you spot, and when do you signal before passing?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: A pickup pulling out of a hidden farm road or narrow bridge ahead can close an open passing lane mid-maneuver.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: How do you warn the driver ahead as you pull left to pass during daylight versus at night?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: A brief horn tap or quick beam flash prevents the overtaken driver from drifting left unexpectedly.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: When is it safe to signal back into your lane after passing, and when is passing on the right allowed?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Using unpaved shoulders to pass on the right kicks up gravel and collides with right-turning traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: Which three sight, oncoming-gap, and vehicle-capability conditions must all hold to pass safely?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Heavily loaded cars climbing steep West Virginia grades often lack brisk acceleration to clear long trucks in time.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: Which side is standard for overtaking, and what sole roadway feature allows passing on the right?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Drivers expect faster traffic on their left and rarely check right shoulders before easing toward an entrance.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: Contrast how you alert a vehicle you are overtaking in daylight versus after dark?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Flashing beams briefly after dark catches rearview-mirror attention cleanly inside closed cabins.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: Why isn't clearing the passed car's front bumper enough to pull back right, and what mirror cue confirms clearance?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Cutting right as soon as bumpers pass leaves inches of margin and forces the overtaken driver to brake hard.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: List the mirror, shoulder, adjacent-lane, signal, and speed steps of a proper lane change?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Side mirrors never eliminate rear-quarter blind spots, making an over-the-shoulder glance indispensable before steering over.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: At which two types of crossings must you never change lanes?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Cross-street turns and multi-track sightlines create high-risk conflict zones where weaving catches nearby drivers off guard.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: Combine the two visual checks needed for every lane change with the two crossings where lane changes are banned?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Pairing blind-spot head checks with straight-through discipline at intersections and tracks prevents classic sideswipes.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: Where must both directions stop for a flashing-red school bus, and which three cues allow proceeding?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: West Virginia extends school-bus stopping duties beyond public streets into parking lots, private roads, and driveways.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: On what single highway type is oncoming traffic across a median excused from stopping for a school bus?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Be careful on the exam because ordinary divided boulevards or four-lane non-interstates still require oncoming traffic to stop.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: Does the school-bus stop rule still apply on school grounds or private property?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Campus pickup loops and apartment complexes pack distracted kids around bus doors, requiring full stops off public pavement too.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: What first-offense penalties hit drivers who pass a stopped school bus, and what if the driver cannot be identified?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Holding registered owners or lessees liable for misdemeanor fines closes the loophole when stop-arm cameras catch plates.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.question_text: Must traffic stop for a loading public transit bus, and what precautions still apply?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.teaching_text: Riders stepping off city transit buses sometimes hurry across in front of the bumper expecting school-bus protection.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: Summarize where both directions must stop for a flashing-red school bus versus the sole exception?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: West Virginia's interstate-only exception is stricter than many neighboring states, making it a favorite permit-test item.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: How does your legal duty behind a loading public transit bus differ from a school bus?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Slowing and scanning around city bus stops prevents hitting commuters stepping into live lanes from behind the coach.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.question_text: Recap the minimum license suspension, fine, and jail exposure for a first offense of passing a stopped school bus?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.teaching_text: Losing your license for at least two months plus facing hundreds in fines or jail underscores student-crossing stakes.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: Even with lighter traffic volume, how does the nighttime fatal crash rate compare with daytime driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Reduced sight distance, glare, fatigue, and impaired drivers combine after sunset to triple per-mile fatality risk.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: Under which three distance and street-lighting situations must you switch from high beams to low beams?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: High beams reflected in a lead car's rearview mirror blind that driver nearly as badly as oncoming glare.
sec12-card-sec12-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, two hundred ahead

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred oncoming, two hundred ahead

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: Which headlight setting works in fog, and where should you look and how should you pace against oncoming glare?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Tracking the white right fog line keeps your car centered without staring into blinding oncoming high beams.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: What night-stopping rule governs your speed, and when is using parking lights alone lawful?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Driving on dim parking lamps at dusk makes your car nearly invisible while overdriving beams hides hazards until impact.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: During what hours, weather conditions, and visibility distance must your headlights stay turned on?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Turning low beams on in rain or smoke illuminates your taillights too so trailing traffic spots you early.
sec12-card-sec12-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Sunset to sunrise, five hundred feet

visual_sync.text_span: Sunset to sunrise, five hundred feet

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: Contrast the high-beam dimming footage for an oncoming vehicle versus a vehicle you are following?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Dropping to low beams early prevents blinding oncoming eyes at five hundred feet and mirrors at two hundred.
sec12-card-sec12-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, two hundred rear

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred oncoming, two hundred rear

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: Pair the daytime visibility threshold that mandates headlights with the proper beam choice for fog?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: High beams bounce off suspended water droplets straight back into your windshield, turning fog into a white wall.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: Roughly what share of traffic deaths involve pedestrians, where is extra care vital, and how may you warn walkers?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Nearly one in five roadway deaths strikes an unprotected walker, making schools, parks, and bus stops high-alert zones.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: In which three situations do pedestrians hold the legal right-of-way over vehicles?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Drivers turning into alleys or driveways cross public sidewalks where walkers and blind cane users hold clear priority.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: Which crossing, road-side walking, signal, and nighttime visibility duties apply to pedestrians?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Walking on the left shoulder when sidewalks end lets pedestrians see approaching headlights and step clear early.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: Where does West Virginia prohibit pedestrians from walking?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: High-speed controlled-access corridors lack safe walkways, so stranded motorists should remain safely clear of live lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.question_text: At which blind road features and recreational areas should you stay alert for joggers?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.teaching_text: Runners wearing earbuds along winding park roads may not hear tyres approaching around a blind crest or corner.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.question_text: Where do children create heightened roadway risk, and what driveway check is essential?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.teaching_text: Small children playing near garages sit completely below trunk height when vehicles back in or out of driveways.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: Which canes or assistance animals establish a blind pedestrian's right-of-way?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Notice the manual specifies that a white or metallic cane grants priority with or without a red tip.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: Why can motorcycles surprise car drivers, and how much lane width belongs to a motorcyclist?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Crowding into the same lane beside a motorcycle robs the rider of room to swerve around potholes or gravel.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: What minimum following count applies behind a motorcycle, and when must you stretch it further?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: Without bumpers or airbags around a rider, even a low-speed rear-end tap causes severe injury or death.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: Why do drivers overlook motorcycles at street corners, and how do you counter that trap?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: Drivers subconsciously scan only for wide car grilles, letting narrow single-headlight bikes hide behind parked SUVs.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: How do you follow and overtake a motorcycle safely on a multilane or two-lane road?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: Moving completely into the passing lane and waiting well ahead before returning shields riders from wind buffeting.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: What typical weight, fifty-five-mile-per-hour stopping multiple, turning room, and blind-spot traits define heavy trucks?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: Fully loaded tractor-trailers need three times a passenger car's braking footage, making abrupt cut-ins impossible to absorb.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: What is a truck's No-Zone, how long may you stay there, and what mirror test exposes it?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Hovering alongside trailer tandems or tucked behind rear doors hides your entire car from the trucker's glass.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: Along with room for wide right turns and backing, how many seconds ahead of a passed truck do you wait before merging right?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Rain slicks pavement and sprays windshields, requiring at least four to six seconds before pulling in front of eighty thousand pounds.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: Name the six dangerous moves you must never make around a heavy truck?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: Squeezing up a truck's right side during a turn traps your car when the trailer swings wide then tracks tight.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: Compare the time cushion needed before merging back right ahead of a passed truck on dry versus wet roads?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Giving extra seconds in wet weather keeps your bumper clear of extended air-brake stopping distances and tire spray.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: Pair a typical heavy truck's loaded weight with its stopping-distance multiple at fifty-five miles per hour?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Massive kinetic energy explains why loaded semis cannot match passenger-car emergency stops even with professional drivers.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: Why do you trail a motorcycle farther back, and how do you complete a pass around one?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Lightweight motorcycles shed speed rapidly without warning, and lane-splitting passes crowd riders dangerously.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: Which machinery displays the triangular slow-moving emblem, and how must regular traffic respond?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: Closing at highway speed on a tractor crawling fifteen miles per hour shrinks gap distance startlingly fast.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: Where may animal riders travel, what traffic rights apply, and what horn rule protects horses?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: A sudden horn blast can spook a horse into bolting sideways directly into your windshield.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: How should you pass a bicyclist by day or night, and during which daily hours is bike traffic heaviest?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: Morning and afternoon commute and school hours put student and commuter cyclists onto neighborhood shoulders daily.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: Why must motorists always give a bicyclist the benefit of the doubt even if the rider makes a mistake?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Winning a legal argument means nothing when steel bumpers meet an unprotected rider on a twenty-pound frame.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: Summarize West Virginia's rules for cyclists on signaling, riding two abreast, hitching rides, walkers, and flow direction?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: Cyclists ride with traffic flow and may balance with both hands when rough pavement makes signaling unsafe.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: Under what seat and handlebar conditions may a bicyclist carry a passenger or a package?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Balancing friends on pegs or cradling bulky boxes blocks steering leverage and emergency brake levers.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.question_text: What reflector, brake performance, audible bell distance, banned sound devices, and night headlight visibility must every bike have?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.teaching_text: Strong brakes, a bell heard one hundred feet away without sirens, and a five-hundred-foot headlight keep night riders visible.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: What three progressive steps defuse a tailgater riding right on your rear bumper?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Letting an aggressive driver pass puts the hazard safely ahead of your windshield instead of glued to your trunk.
sec12-card-sec12-F09.must_match_memory_hook: Flash brake lights, slow, pull over

visual_sync.text_span: Flash brake lights, slow, pull over

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: Combine where animal riders are prohibited with the number-one sound rule around horses?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Slowing quietly with wide lateral room keeps mounted animals calm along rural West Virginia two-lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: Compare the required range for a bicycle's bell against its nighttime front headlight, plus banned sound gear?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Whistles and sirens belong to emergency responders and officials, so bicycles use bells audible at one hundred feet.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.question_text: Pair the lane rule for side-by-side cyclists with passenger-seat and handlebar-hand requirements?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.teaching_text: Staying inside a single lane without impeding traffic and keeping a hand on the bars preserves rider stability.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: Which roadway enters an interstate, and why must you read its signs closely?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: Entering an adjacent exit ramp by mistake puts you nose-to-nose with fast traffic, while missing a sharp curve sign invites a rollover.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: What actions should you take about halfway along an interstate entrance ramp?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Spotting a gap early gives you room to time your merge while still watching vehicles ahead in the acceleration lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: What speed and steering path should you use as you merge onto an interstate?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: Darting sharply left across lanes surprises high-speed traffic that expects merging cars to blend smoothly into the first lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.question_text: How should you handle a vehicle ahead in the acceleration lane, and where must you avoid stopping?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.teaching_text: Hesitant drivers ahead often panic-brake at the merge point, and stopping behind them leaves both cars exposed to rear-end collisions.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.question_text: What last-resort option exists if no interstate traffic gap opens before the acceleration lane ends?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.teaching_text: Pulling into seventy-mile-per-hour traffic from a dead stop requires huge clear space, making that maneuver strictly an emergency fallback.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way when you enter an interstate, and what can you never assume?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.teaching_text: Assuming freeway drivers see your blinker or have room to slide left is a classic merge mistake on test day.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.question_text: How should you prepare to take an interstate exit safely?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.teaching_text: Diving across lanes at the last second either forces you past your ramp or triggers a high-speed sideswipe.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.question_text: Where and how should you reduce your speed when leaving an interstate?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.teaching_text: Slowing in an active freeway travel lane catches fast traffic behind you off guard while ramp curves still demand lower speed.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: Where does braking for an interstate exit belong, and what speed are you aiming for?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Test questions pair location and target speed to make sure you keep highway pace until safely inside the exit lane.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: Where is the only last-resort place to stop if no interstate merge gap opens?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: Halting on the ramp or inside the merge lane blocks every vehicle behind you from building safe freeway speed.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: Who yields during an interstate merge, and what exact lane sequence must the entering driver follow?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Respecting mainline priority and finishing the first merge before moving left keeps multi-lane freeway traffic predictable.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: What crash risk have interstates largely eliminated, and what mental state do they still demand?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: High speeds shrink reaction windows so quickly that highway hypnosis or daydreaming turns minor surprises into major pileups.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: How should you treat trucks and buses entering an interstate, and which lane belongs to slower traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Heavy vehicles build speed slowly on ramps, and camping slowly in left lanes clogs passing flow behind you.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.question_text: When may you use an interstate shoulder, and where do routine stops like driver swaps belong?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.teaching_text: Stopping beside fast traffic to check directions or switch seats exposes your car to drifting vehicles when rest areas exist.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.question_text: What is an exit gore, and why must you never stop inside it?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.teaching_text: Indecisive drivers who almost miss their turn frequently swerve across that painted wedge at full highway speed.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.question_text: Is parking allowed on interstate shoulders, and what can happen to a vehicle left there?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.teaching_text: Unattended cars along high-speed shoulders create lethal roadside obstacles that authorities clear away quickly.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.question_text: What maximum, minimum, and pacing rules govern speed on a West Virginia interstate?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.teaching_text: Keeping a steady pace between the legal floor and ceiling prevents sudden speed gaps unless weather or signs force lower speeds.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.question_text: Why is driving much slower than interstate traffic dangerous, and which lane must you use unless passing?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.teaching_text: Closing speeds sneak up on drivers behind a slow car, forcing abrupt lane dodges across faster lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.question_text: What lighting does West Virginia law require in adverse conditions, and how else must you adjust?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.teaching_text: Poor visibility and slick pavement demand both earlier sightlines for others and extra room for a controlled stop.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: What are the interstate speed floor, speed ceiling, and default travel lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Exam questions bundle minimum pace, posted maximum, and right-lane discipline to test standard freeway cruising.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: How does the rule for an interstate shoulder differ from the rule for an exit gore?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Even a disabled car has no business sitting inside the split between mainline traffic and an exit ramp.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: What colors mark an interstate shield, and which directions do even and odd route numbers indicate?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Reading the shield number instantly tells you compass direction before you commit to an unfamiliar ramp.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: What is the difference between a three-digit interstate starting with an even digit versus an odd digit?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Mistaking a dead-end spur into downtown for a bypass loop around town can trap you in city congestion.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: Why should you map your route beforehand, and what five vehicle items should you inspect before an interstate trip?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Long stretches between exits turn running low on fuel, coolant, oil, or a spare tire into a dangerous roadside wait.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: Why are interstate interchange guide signs posted well ahead of the turnoff?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Spotting your exit name early lets you signal and glide into the proper lane smoothly instead of cutting across traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: How can you tell on an overhead guide sign when a through lane is about to end at a fork or exit?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Missing that warning banner under the green sign can pull you onto an unwanted exit ramp or force a panic merge.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: How does an interchange let two highways cross without conflict, and what are the three common designs?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: Grade-separated bridges and connecting ramps keep crossing streams apart, though sharp loops and merges vary by layout.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: Which compass directions correspond to even-numbered and odd-numbered interstate highways?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: DMV tests love flipping even and odd directions to catch drivers guessing on route-numbering questions.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: In a three-digit interstate number, what does the first digit tell you about the route?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: Checking only the very first digit tells you whether the highway circles back to the main route or branches away.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.question_text: How does an overhead sign warn of a removed through lane compared with an added lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.teaching_text: New lanes open visibly beside you, whereas a disappearing through lane needs bold color contrast overhead so drivers merge early.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.question_text: What are the three common highway interchange layouts, and how do interchanges connect crossing roads?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.teaching_text: Knowing the three standard layouts prepares you for tight loop ramps, signalized crossroad turns, or directional T-ramps.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: Which two groups of people may legally use designated mobility impaired parking spaces in West Virginia?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Reserved spaces close to entrances protect people who cannot safely walk long parking-lot distances and the drivers assisting them.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: What certification is needed for a mobility impaired placard or plate, and what transfer fee applies to the plate?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Medical verification prevents misuse of accessible spaces while keeping the official plate transfer cost modest.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: What must a vehicle display to park legally in a designated mobility impaired area?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Having an eligible condition or passenger is not enough if the vehicle lacks visible authorization on the spot.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: What should a license applicant include if a physical disability or medical issue might affect driving?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Individual evaluation beats rigid blanket rules, so giving examiners clear facts up front helps match safe licensing options.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: Which two West Virginia sources can give a driver a list of adaptive aid manufacturers like hand controls?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Getting vetted equipment makers from licensing or rehabilitation staff ensures vehicle controls are safe and road-ready.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: What four protections and services does the DMV provide under the Americans with Disabilities Act?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Federal accessibility protections ensure communication support, reasonable policy adjustments, and working animals inside every office.
sec13-card-sec13-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Aids, policy flex, service animals welcome

visual_sync.text_span: Aids, policy flex, service animals welcome

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: How far in advance should you contact the DMV if you need an auxiliary aid or procedure modification?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Giving two days notice lets the office arrange interpreters, accessible formats, or procedural adjustments before you arrive.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: What changes is the DMV not forced to make under the ADA, and may it charge extra for accommodations?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Agencies need not overhaul core standards or absorb extreme burdens, yet billing disabled applicants for needed aids is barred.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: Who handles DMV accessibility questions, and what is one example of a reasonable office modification?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Simple practical help like fetching forms from an out-of-reach rack keeps public service barrier-free for wheelchair users.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.question_text: What medical step and plate transfer fee apply to mobility impaired parking, and when is parking there illegal?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.teaching_text: Test questions combine the doctor certification, exact ten-dollar-fifty-cent transfer fee, and visible display rule.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.question_text: What is the deadline for requesting a DMV accommodation, and how much can the DMV charge you for it?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.teaching_text: Knowing both the two-day request window and the ban on surcharges nails every ADA service question.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: What does West Virginia law require you to switch on during rain or reduced visibility?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Daytime spray and gray skies hide unlit cars in mirrors long before dark arrives.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: When is wet pavement slickest, and why does that happen?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: Fresh raindrops mix with road grime before heavy downpours wash it away, stretching stops and loosening curve grip.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: What happens to tire grip on wet pavement up to thirty-five miles per hour, at thirty-five, and at fifty-five?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: Once water lifts the rubber completely off the asphalt, steering and braking inputs have zero traction to work with.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.question_text: In a severe rainstorm at fifty-five miles per hour, what small forces can trigger an uncontrollable skid?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.teaching_text: Floating on a sheet of water removes all tire grip, letting even a crosswind gust spin the car.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: Which driving and tire maintenance habits cut your risk of hydroplaning?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: Deep grooves channel water out from under the footprint instead of trapping a slick wedge beneath bald rubber.
sec14-card-sec14-F23.must_match_memory_hook: Slow down, inflate, replace worn treads

visual_sync.text_span: Slow down, inflate, replace worn treads

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: How little water can float smaller cars, and what depth sweeps most vehicles away?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: Buoyant cars lose wheel weight fast and can roll into deep currents that trap occupants inside.
sec14-card-sec14-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Six inches floats, two feet sweeps

visual_sync.text_span: Six inches floats, two feet sweeps

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: Roughly what share of American flash flood deaths happen in vehicles, and what hidden road hazard traps drivers?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: Murky floodwater hides washed-out pavement edges, especially after dark when depth and missing asphalt look like shallow puddles.
